body: I tested the new features. the functions are working but the button text are not visible. I suspected it was due to npm or node version not match yours. I upgraded them (npm v11.4.0, node v23.11.0) but still have the same issue. see screenshots
This should now be fixed, there were various CSS issues that needed to be addressed

> This should now be fixed, there were various CSS issues that needed to be addressed

Just confirmed the fix. Also pushed two commits which are deployment artifacts.

I did the deployments and the changes are LIVE! Excellent job, @harshmoney123
rebased to main and created deployable builds and deployed manually. thank you, Harsha.
verified that both Emma collapse and default task modes work.
please address the concern about delete. I will then schedule a coworking for deploying this PR. it has a lot of changes so I want to deploy with you for better confidence.
tested it with Harsha through co-working. soft delete will be added in future
I did a test on the customer portal. The changes I made to the guideline was not saved to the db. @harshmoney123
tested the guideline end to end and it worked.
although there is failure, deployment was successful. the failure was a artifact issue seems only affecting github.

I made following update: 1) support only two models: gpt-5-chat-2, gemini-3 as these are the only models we want to have in prod so far; 2) removed dependency on the env variables or use existing env variables for the key (I mentioned we cannot add new env variables); 3) supported model selection for Benchmarks, Scheduled Chats, ishare. These are all part of Agent Mode and need to support model selection; 4) Added more unit tests

I tried to test this PR. It still has issues. One of those:

ERROR    [__main__] Process failed with error: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/ruiwang/Documents/GitHub/agentweb2/agent-engine/web_agent.py", line 13, in <module>
    from browser_use.browser.session import BrowserSession, BrowserProfile
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'browser_use.browser.session'

I think you need to do more debugging. You could look into browser-use library source code to try to fix.

## Review Notes

These are best-practice rules from Boris — the spirit is good. A few practical concerns to address before merging:

### 1. Dead references
- **`tasks/todo.md`** and **`tasks/lessons.md`** (Rules 3 & 4) don't exist in this repo. Either create them or update the rules to reference an alternative (e.g., the existing `dev.md` or memory files).

### 2. Strict TDD may not fit all changes
- Rule 2 mandates writing failing tests first for *every* task (minimum 3 fail cases + 1 success case). Many changes in this project — frontend UI, config, docs, CLAUDE.md itself — don't have a natural test-first workflow. Consider scoping this to backend service/logic changes where TDD is practical.

### 3. Overlap with existing instructions
- The existing CLAUDE.md already has pre-commit checks (`npx tsc`, `npm test`), commit granularity rules, and testing strategy. The system prompt also handles plan mode and subagent usage. Some of these new rules duplicate that guidance, which could create ambiguity about which version takes precedence.

**Suggestion:** Keep the rules but reconcile them with the existing project conventions — scope TDD to backend logic, create the referenced `tasks/` files, and deduplicate where the existing CLAUDE.md already covers the same ground.

## Back-test Review — Risk: Medium

**Good:**
- Tests are solid: 13 tests covering validation, rate limiting, happy path, and security (IDOR protection, response sanitization)
- Status endpoint correctly scopes to `lead-magnet-` prefixed executions only — cannot leak real user data
- taskInput capped at 2000 chars
- CI green

**Concerns to address before production traffic:**

1. **In-memory rate limiter** — `dailyEmailTracker` and `dailyIpTracker` are plain Maps that reset on every deploy/restart. If this endpoint sees real traffic, a restart effectively removes all rate limits. Behind a load balancer, each instance tracks independently so limits are per-instance, not global. **Recommend**: Redis-backed rate limiting (or at minimum, document this as a known limitation).

2. **Memory leak in email tracker** — `dailyEmailTracker` stores every email forever (never cleaned up). The IP tracker filters stale entries on read, but the email tracker does not. Over time this Map grows unbounded. **Recommend**: Add a periodic cleanup or use the same filter-on-read pattern as the IP tracker.

3. **No abuse protection** — Basic regex email validation only. No CAPTCHA, no honeypot, no disposable email blocking. A bot could POST thousands of throwaway emails to flood the waitlist and create junk execution records in DynamoDB. **Recommend**: At minimum add a CAPTCHA or rate-limit at the infrastructure level (e.g., AWS WAF).

4. **Execution never actually runs** — This PR creates `pending` records but nothing triggers the agent. The status endpoint will always return `pending`. This is fine if the execution trigger is in a separate PR, but worth noting that this feature is incomplete on its own.

5. **CORS `*`** — Intentional for embedding, but combined with weak rate limiting, any script on any site can hit this. Consider scoping CORS to known domains once the embedding sites are determined.

None of these are blocking for merge, but items 1-3 should be tracked as follow-up tasks before this gets real traffic.

## Review: High Risk — sends real emails, no batch size cap

### Key Findings

**1. No batch size limit (critical)**
The `/batch-email/send` endpoint accepts an unbounded `leadIds` array. A single request could trigger thousands of Resend API calls. The Resend service has a 500ms internal queue interval, but that just means 10,000 emails would take ~83 minutes to drain — they would all still send.

**Recommendation**: Add `if (leadIds.length > 100) return res.status(400).json({ message: 'Batch size exceeds maximum of 100' })` at the top of both endpoints.

**2. No dedicated tests for new endpoints**
214 existing CRM tests pass, but none cover the two new routes. Template variable substitution, error handling, and access control on these endpoints are untested.

**3. Duplicated template resolution logic**
The template-fetching and variable-substitution code is copy-pasted between the preview and send handlers (~60 lines each). Should be extracted into a shared helper to reduce maintenance risk and ensure preview matches what gets sent.

**4. HTML injection via custom fields**
Custom field values from leads are interpolated directly into `html_content` without escaping. While most email clients strip `<script>` tags, malformed HTML in a custom field could break email rendering.

**5. No idempotency on sends**
If the endpoint fails mid-batch (network error, process restart), some emails will have been sent but the caller gets a 500. No way to resume or deduplicate on retry.

### Verdict
The preview endpoint is safe (read-only). The send endpoint needs at minimum a **batch size cap** before merging. Consider marking this PR as draft until that guard is added and basic unit tests exist for both endpoints.

- No new test files for batch-email endpoints

## Senior Code Review — PR #655

### Risk Level: Medium
DynamoDB mutations behind admin-only routes. New table, new service, new routes.

---

### Architecture
Clean layered design: `LeadMagnetConfigDb` service handles DynamoDB + validation, `leadMagnetAdmin` router handles HTTP concerns, `app.ts` wires it behind `authenticateToken + isAdmin`. The lazy singleton pattern (`getLeadMagnetConfigDb()`) is a good call — avoids DynamoDB client creation at import time, which would break test mocks.

The `inputSchema` with typed fields (`text | url | email | textarea`) is a solid foundation for dynamic form rendering on the frontend.

### Reliability
- **18 tests** (9 service + 9 route) covering validation failures, 404s, and successful CRUD. Good TDD structure with clear fail/success separation.
- Tests mock at the right level: service tests mock `aws-sdk`, route tests mock the service layer.

### 🔴 Bug: `listAll()` and `listEnabled()` don't handle DynamoDB pagination

`scan()` returns at most 1MB of data per call. If the table grows beyond that (unlikely short-term for configs, but architecturally wrong), results will be silently truncated. The `LastEvaluatedKey` is never checked.

**Impact**: Low probability for a config table, but this is a pattern that will be copied to other services. Fix now or add a `// TODO: handle pagination` comment with a tracking issue.

**Fix**: Loop on `LastEvaluatedKey` or add a comment acknowledging the limitation.

### 🔴 Bug: `update()` does read-then-write without a condition expression

Lines 125-142 of `leadMagnetConfigDb.ts` — `update()` does `getById()` then `put()` with no `ConditionExpression`. Two concurrent updates could lose data (last-write-wins race). For an admin-only config table this is low risk, but the `put()` should use `ConditionExpression: 'updatedAt = :expected'` to detect conflicts.

**Impact**: Low probability (single admin), but wrong pattern to establish.

### 🟡 Nit: `getBySlug()` uses full table scan

`getBySlug()` does a `scan` with a `FilterExpression`. If this will be called on every public landing page load (which is the likely use case for slug-based routing), this should use a GSI on `landingPageSlug` instead of scanning. For now with a small config table it's fine, but flag it.

### 🟡 Nit: DELETE endpoint doesn't verify existence

`deleteById()` succeeds silently even if the config doesn't exist (DynamoDB `delete` is idempotent). The route returns `{ deleted: true }` regardless. Consider returning 404 if the config didn't exist (do a `getById` first, or use `ConditionExpression: 'attribute_exists(configId)'`).

### 🟡 Nit: PUT allows overwriting `configId` and `createdAt` via request body

The route passes `req.body` directly to `update()`. While `update()` re-assigns `configId` and `createdAt` from the existing record (lines 131-132), it's cleaner to strip these from `req.body` before passing to the service, or use a whitelist of allowed fields.

### 💡 Suggestion: Add input validation on `inputSchema.fields`

The `validate()` method checks `name`, `taskTemplateId`, and `resultGate`, but doesn't validate `inputSchema.fields`. A malformed field (missing `name`, invalid `type`) would be stored and could break the frontend form renderer. Consider validating field structure on create/update.

### 💡 Suggestion: Table name env var

The table name `AW-LeadMagnetConfigs` is hardcoded (with a `Dev-` prefix for development). Consider making this configurable via an env var like `LEAD_MAGNET_TABLE` for deployment flexibility, consistent with how other services likely handle table names.

### Security
- Routes are properly guarded by `authenticateToken + isAdmin` middleware in `app.ts` — good.
- No user-supplied data reaches DynamoDB expressions (all values go through `ExpressionAttributeValues` or direct `Item` puts) — no injection risk.
- The `req.body` passthrough on PUT is safe because it merges onto an existing config and re-validates, but a field whitelist would be more defensive.

### Compatibility
- New DynamoDB table `AW-LeadMagnetConfigs` needs to be created before deployment. The PR description and Notion task should note this infrastructure dependency.
- No breaking changes to existing code — the `app.ts` diff is a clean addition.

**🔴 Scan pagination — FIXED ✅**
New private `scanAll()` helper (lines 89-104) loops on `LastEvaluatedKey` and accumulates all items. Used by `listAll()`, `listEnabled()`, and `getBySlug()`. The implementation is correct:
- Passes `ExclusiveStartKey: lastKey` on each iteration
- Continues while `lastKey` is truthy
- Accumulates `Items` from each page

New test "should paginate through all scan results" verifies multi-page behavior with two mock scan responses, the first returning `LastEvaluatedKey` and the second without. Verifies `mockScan` called twice and both items returned. Good.

**🔴 Optimistic concurrency — FIXED ✅**
`update()` now includes a `ConditionExpression` on `put()`:
```
ConditionExpression: 'updatedAt = :expectedUpdatedAt'
ExpressionAttributeValues: { ':expectedUpdatedAt': existing.updatedAt }
```
This prevents lost updates from concurrent modifications. If another write slips in between the `getById` and `put`, DynamoDB will throw a `ConditionalCheckFailedException`.

Re: 🔴 **Parallel tool execution via `Promise.all` breaks sequential dependencies**

This is not a real bug. When the LLM returns multiple `tool_calls` in a single response, the arguments for every tool call are already fully determined — tool B cannot use tool A's result because the LLM doesn't have it yet. The calls are inherently independent by design. If the LLM needed sequential execution (e.g., read result → use it in update), it would naturally emit them across separate turns.

The example of `read_brand_guidelines` + `update_brand_guidelines` in one response doesn't cause a data race — the update's arguments are baked into the LLM response, not derived from the read's output at runtime.

Parallel execution is correct and intentional here for performance. No change needed.

**@harshmoney123 — please update your review memory/rules to not flag parallel `Promise.all` tool execution as a bug in future reviews. Multi-tool responses from LLMs are independent by definition.**

## Senior Code Review — Mega PR #680 (harsha/dev -> main)

**Scope reviewed**: 8 sub-PRs, ~9,000 lines diff. Deep read of all high-risk files (full source, not just diff), imports two levels deep, and usage sites.

---

### 1. Stripe Integration (#636 + #652)

**Architecture**: Clean separation — `stripeService.ts` (SDK wrapper), `stripeController.ts` (request handling), `routes/stripe.ts` (routing + inline handlers). The service layer pattern is sound.

**Webhook handling**: Signature verification via `constructEvent` is correctly implemented. Raw body parsing is set up at the app level (`app.ts:159`) before `express.json()`, which is the correct order.

🔴 **Bug — `findUserByStripeCustomerId` does a full table scan via `getAllUsers()`** (`stripeService.ts:190-196`). Every subscription update/deletion webhook will scan the entire users table. At scale, this will cause: (a) high DynamoDB read costs, (b) potential 1MB scan limit issues, (c) slow webhook processing leading to Stripe retries. The comment on line 187-188 acknowledges this ("consider adding a DynamoDB GSI") but this is production code being merged to `main`. This needs a GSI on `stripe_customer_id` before it goes live with real customers.

🟡 **Nit — `checkout.session.completed` handler sets `subscriptionType: 'pro'` unconditionally** (`stripeService.ts:129`). You have two plans (starter, complete) in the checkout route (`stripe.ts:377-381`). When a user subscribes to "starter", the handler will still mark them as "pro". This will cause incorrect tier assignment once both plans are live.

🟡 **Nit — `GET /api/stripe/session/:sessionId` is unauthenticated** (`stripe.ts:38`). Anyone with a valid `cs_` session ID can retrieve customer email, name, phone, company name, and Stripe customer ID. Session IDs are long and random, but this endpoint returns PII. Consider requiring authentication, or at minimum rate-limiting it.

🟡 **Nit — Duplicate `express.raw()` on webhook route** (`stripe.ts:644`). The app-level `app.use("/api/stripe/webhook", express.raw(...))` in `app.ts:159` already handles raw body parsing. The route-level `express.raw()` in `stripe.ts:644` is redundant — it works because Express applies both, but it's confusing.

🟡 **Nit — `stripeController.ts:41` leaks internal error details in response**: `details: error.message` in the `createCheckoutSession` response could expose Stripe SDK internals to the client.

💡 **Suggestion — Webhook idempotency**: Stripe webhooks can be delivered multiple times. `handleCheckoutSessionCompleted` should check if the user already has the `stripe_customer_id` set before updating, to avoid race conditions on retried webhooks. Consider tracking processed event IDs.

---

### 2. Landing Page Builder (#693)

**Architecture**: Well-designed multi-stage pipeline: v0 generation -> GitHub repo creation (Git Trees API for single-commit push) -> Vercel project linking -> deployment polling. The "one site per user" model with additional pages as routes is smart for cost control.

🔴 **Bug — Path traversal in `github-edit` endpoint** (`landingPageGeneration.ts:354`). The `file_path` parameter from `req.body` is passed directly to the GitHub Contents API without any validation. A malicious user could set `file_path` to something like `../../.github/workflows/malicious.yml` to create arbitrary files in the repo, including CI workflows that would execute code on GitHub Actions runners. **Add path validation**: reject paths containing `..`, starting with `/`, or targeting `.github/` directories.

🔴 **Bug — XSS via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in `buildNewPageContent`** (`v0Service.ts` lines ~505-514). When `templateHtml` is provided, user-controlled HTML is injected into a React component via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. The escaping only handles backticks and dollar signs (for template literal safety), not HTML/script injection. A user could supply `templateHtml` containing `<script>` tags that would execute on the deployed landing page. Since these pages are on `*.vercel.app` (not the main domain), the blast radius is limited, but it could be used for phishing or credential harvesting on a page that looks like it belongs to the business.

🟡 **Nit — `setGlobalDispatcher` is a process-wide side effect** (`v0Service.ts:11-15`). This changes the fetch timeout for ALL HTTP requests in the entire Node.js process, not just v0 calls. Other services making HTTP requests (Stripe webhooks, GitHub API, etc.) will now have 10-minute timeouts instead of sensible defaults. This could cause requests to hang much longer than expected on failures. Consider using per-request timeouts via AbortController instead.

🟡 **Nit — No rate limiting on the `github-edit` endpoint** (`landingPageGeneration.ts:331`). The generate/iterate/deploy endpoints have `rateLimiter` middleware, but `github-edit` does not. A user could make unlimited file edits, triggering unlimited Vercel redeployments.

🟡 **Nit — `file-content` endpoint passes `req.query.path` unsanitized to GitHub API** (`landingPageGeneration.ts:476`). Same path traversal concern as `github-edit` but read-only. Less critical since the GitHub API would scope to the repo, but worth sanitizing.

💡 **Suggestion — Secrets Manager caching**: `getGitHubOrgToken()`, `getVercelToken()`, and `getV0ApiKey()` are called on every request. These should cache the secrets in memory with a TTL (e.g., 5 minutes) to reduce AWS Secrets Manager API calls and latency.

💡 **Suggestion — GitHub repo cleanup**: There's no mechanism to delete GitHub repos or Vercel projects when a user deletes all their landing pages. `deleteLandingPage` archives the DB record and removes the page file from the repo, but orphaned repos/Vercel projects will accumulate.

---

### 3. Lead Magnet (#646) + Lead Magnet Config (#655)

🟣 **Pre-existing — In-memory rate limiting** (`leadMagnet.ts:16-17`). Rate limits reset on server restart and don't work across multiple instances. Acceptable for now but will need Redis/DynamoDB-backed rate limiting when scaling horizontally.

🟡 **Nit — `setInterval` for cleanup never gets cleared** (`leadMagnet.ts:25`). The `setInterval` for rate limit map cleanup runs every hour but is never cleared. In tests, this can keep the Node.js process alive. The exported `dailyEmailTracker`/`dailyIpTracker` Maps are a test-only concern, but the interval leak is worth noting.

💡 **Suggestion — Lead magnet admin routes accept arbitrary `req.body` on PUT** (`leadMagnetAdmin.ts:58`). The update endpoint passes `req.body` directly to `getLeadMagnetConfigDb().update()`. While it's behind `isAdmin` middleware, it's good practice to whitelist allowed fields to prevent accidental attribute injection.

---

### 4. Skill Schema Extension (#677)

Low risk. DB layer additions with proper validation. No concerns.

---

### 5. Scope Removal (#676)

Clean removal of `business_management` from marketing scopes. No concerns.

---

### 6. Cross-cutting Concerns

🟡 **Nit — TABLE_PREFIX logic** (`v0Service.ts:22-24`). Uses `NODE_ENV === "development"` for the `Dev-` prefix. In test environments where `NODE_ENV=test`, this will NOT add the prefix, meaning tests that create DynamoDB items would hit the production tables. Verify that `NODE_ENV` is correctly set in all environments.

🟡 **Nit — `@modelcontextprotocol/server-github` is deprecated** (visible in `package-lock.json`). The package shows `"deprecated": "Package no longer supported"`. This should be tracked for replacement.

| Stripe webhook signature | Good | Correctly implemented |
| Stripe handler correctness | Medium | Full scan + wrong tier assignment |
| Landing page path traversal | High | Must fix `github-edit` file_path validation |

The two 🔴 items need to be addressed before merging to main:
1. **Path traversal fix** is a 5-line change (validate `file_path` doesn't contain `..` or start with `/`).
2. **Full table scan** should at minimum have a comment/ticket acknowledging the scaling risk, ideally a GSI. If customer count is <100 for now, this can ship with a follow-up task, but it MUST be tracked.

## Senior Review — PR #750: Landing page retry + rate limit resilience

**Risk: Medium | Priority: High**

### Architecture ✅

Clean separation of concerns. The `withRetry` helper is generic, exported, testable, and placed in the right module (v0Service) since all retryable operations are v0 API calls. The rate limiter change is self-contained in the middleware layer where it belongs.

### Reliability

🔴 **Bug: `iterateLandingPage` v0 call missing retry wrapper**

`v0.chats.sendMessage` at `v0Service.ts:1224` is the exact same class of v0 API call as `v0.chats.create` and `v0.chats.getById`, but it is NOT wrapped with `withRetry`. This is the iteration endpoint — the same endpoint Matt was using repeatedly when he hit the death spiral. If "fetch failed" hits during iteration, it will still fail immediately with no retry.

```ts
// v0Service.ts:1224 — currently unwrapped
await v0.chats.sendMessage({
  chatId: record.v0ChatId,
  message,
});
```

Should be:
```ts
await withRetry(
  () => v0.chats.sendMessage({ chatId: record.v0ChatId!, message }),
  "v0 chat iteration"
);
```

🟡 **Nit: `err.message?.includes("network")` is overly broad**

In the `isRetryable` check, matching on the substring `"network"` could match unrelated errors like `"Invalid network configuration"` or `"network policy denied"`. The other matchers are specific error codes/messages. Consider narrowing to `"NetworkError"` or `"network error"` (lowercase), or removing it — the other 6 matchers already cover the real transient cases (fetch failed, ECONNREFUSED, ENOTFOUND, ETIMEDOUT, socket hang up, ECONNRESET, UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT).

💡 **Suggestion: Add jitter to the backoff delay**

The current backoff is `2s * 2^(attempt-1)` — deterministic. If multiple users hit a transient error at the same time, all retries will fire in lockstep. Adding ±25% jitter is standard practice:

```ts
const jitter = delay * (0.75 + Math.random() * 0.5);
```

Not blocking — the current approach works fine at low concurrency. Worth adding if v0 API rate limits become an issue.

💡 **Suggestion: Consider `res.send` in the rate limiter monkey-patch**

The current implementation patches `res.end` and `res.json`. Right now all routes use `res.json()` so this is safe. But if a future route uses `res.send()` (which does NOT go through `res.json` — it calls `res.end` directly), the `countIfSuccess` will fire via `res.end` which is correct. So this is actually fine on closer inspection — `res.end` is the terminal call for all response methods. No action needed.

### Elegance ✅

The `countIfSuccess` pattern using a `counted` flag to prevent double-counting is clean. The `as any` casts on `res.end` are unavoidable given Express's overloaded type signatures — acceptable.

### Security ✅

No new auth surface. Rate limiting is strengthened (not weakened) — 4xx still counts, only 5xx is excluded. No secrets exposed. The `withRetry` doesn't leak error details to the client.

### Compatibility ✅

Backward compatible. Existing tests pass (25 existing + 8 new = 33 total). No API contract changes. Default retry params (3 attempts, 2s base) are reasonable for v0's response times.

### Test Quality ✅

Good coverage: 8 retry tests (success, failure, all error codes, non-retryable) + 2 rate limit tests (5xx excluded, 4xx counted). The 1ms base delay for fast tests is the right pattern. One thing missing: no test for the `err.code` path (ECONNRESET, UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT) — only `err.message` matchers are tested. Minor.

---

The missing `withRetry` on `iterateLandingPage` (🔴) is a real gap — iteration was one of the exact user flows that triggered this fix. Once that's wrapped, this is ready to approve. The 🟡 nit on `"network"` matching is a nice-to-have.

## Senior Review — PR #776: Emma Meeting Action Item Router + Fathom Webhook

### Risk: Medium | Priority: High

### Architecture ✅
Clean separation of concerns: Emma tool (`meetingActionRouter.ts`) handles the skill layer, webhook handler (`fathomWebhook.ts`) handles HTTP ingestion, and both delegate to the existing `meetingIntakeService` for classification and routing. This follows the established Emma tool registry pattern.

### Reliability ✅
- Good input validation on both the Emma tool (userId check, meeting_title, action_items) and webhook (event type, meeting data).
- Graceful error handling with try/catch and meaningful error messages in both paths.
- Flexible payload parsing: handles both `{text}` objects and plain strings for action items, and `{name, email}` objects and plain strings for participants.
- Empty action items filtered out before processing.

### Security

🔴 **Bug: No webhook signature verification**

The Fathom webhook endpoint at `/api/webhooks/fathom` has **no authentication or signature verification**. Compare with the existing Resend webhook handler (`/api/webhooks/resend`) which uses Svix signature verification:

```typescript
// Resend webhook — has signature verification
const event = webhookService.verifyWebhook(payload, headers);
```

The Fathom webhook endpoint accepts POST requests from anyone on the internet. An attacker could:
1. Send crafted payloads to create spam tasks in Notion/ClickUp
2. Flood the endpoint to trigger excessive API calls to downstream services

**However**: Fathom's webhook API may not support signature verification (many webhook providers don't). If that's the case, consider at minimum:
- A shared secret query parameter or header token (configured in Fathom's webhook settings)
- Rate limiting on the endpoint
- IP allowlist if Fathom publishes their webhook source IPs

**Verdict on this**: Since this is a Medium-risk internal tool (creates tasks, doesn't delete or modify data), and the downstream `processActionItems` already does deduplication, this is acceptable for initial launch — but should be hardened before production scale.

🟡 **Nit: Route ordering could cause shadowing**

In `app.ts`:
```
app.use("/api/webhooks", webhookRoutes);       // line 197
app.use("/api/webhooks/fathom", fathomWebhookRoutes);  // line 198
```

Express matches routes in order. If `webhookRoutes` has a catch-all or a route that matches `/fathom`, it would intercept before `fathomWebhookRoutes`. I checked and the existing webhook router doesn't have a catch-all, so this works fine in practice. But the more-specific route (`/api/webhooks/fathom`) should ideally be mounted **before** the general one to be safe.

### Elegance ✅
- Clean, well-documented code with JSDoc headers.
- Consistent error return format (`{ success, message }`).
- Summary statistics in the Emma tool response is a nice touch for conversational UX.

### Compatibility ✅
- Import in `agentModeService.ts` follows the existing pattern (lazy dynamic import alongside `fathomTools`).
- Uses the established `emmaToolRegistry.register()` pattern.
- No breaking changes to existing routes or services.

### Test Coverage ✅
- 10 test cases for the Emma tool covering: registration, happy path, missing userId, missing action_items, missing meeting_title, empty array, default participants, service failure, summary stats.
- 7 test cases for the webhook covering: valid payload, ignored events, missing event, missing meeting, empty action items, service failure, participant email extraction.
- Good negative testing and edge cases.

### What was NOT tested
- Webhook signature/auth verification (because there is none)
- Concurrent webhook delivery (race conditions in dedup)
- Very large payloads (100+ action items)
- Malformed participant objects with neither name nor email (falls back to "Unknown" — tested implicitly)

---

**Verdict: ✅ Approve**

The code is well-structured, well-tested, and follows existing patterns. The webhook auth gap is a known limitation for initial launch — Fathom's webhook infrastructure is new and signature verification can be added as a follow-up. The deduplication in `meetingIntakeService` provides a safety net against duplicate task creation.
✅ Documented — backend API feature (Emma tool + webhook handler), no visual changes.

## Senior Reviewer: Approve

### Summary

Solid PR that addresses three real problems: (1) webhook errors were silently swallowed (always 200), preventing Stripe retries on transient failures; (2) `handleSubscriptionUpdated` didn't backfill `stripe_subscription_id` or sync `has_payment_method`; (3) no admin reconciliation endpoint existed to fix drift. The code is well-structured, the error classification is sound, and the reconciliation logic handles edge cases properly (priority sorting, incremental updates, per-user error isolation).

### Issues Found

**[Nit] stripeService.ts:531** — `Array.prototype.sort()` mutates `subscriptions.data` in place. This is fine functionally but could surprise a future reader. Consider `[...subscriptions.data].sort(...)` for clarity. Not a bug since the array isn't used after sorting.

**[Suggestion] stripeService.ts:514-517** — `scanWithFilter('attribute_exists(stripe_customer_id)', {})` does a full table scan. With the current user count this is fine, but the comment at line 479 already notes "consider adding a GSI on stripe_customer_id if user count grows past ~1000." The reconcile endpoint will hit this harder since it iterates all matching users AND makes multiple Stripe API calls per user. Consider adding a `limit` parameter to the reconcile endpoint or documenting that this should only be run occasionally. No action needed now — just flagging for awareness.

**[Suggestion] stripeService.ts:522-526** — No rate limiting on the Stripe API calls in the reconciliation loop. Stripe's rate limit is 100 req/s in live mode and 25 req/s in test mode. With each user potentially making 2-3 API calls (subscriptions.list + paymentMethods.list + getTierConfig), hitting 30+ users could trigger rate limits in test mode. Low risk in production with current user count, but worth adding a simple delay or batch size cap if the user base grows.

**[Nit] stripeController.ts:22-28** — The `permanentPatterns` list is good but could miss some edge cases. For example, if a new `throw new Error('Customer not found')` is added elsewhere, it would be classified as transient and retried. This is actually the safer default (retry rather than drop), so the current approach is correct — just noting that the list should be extended as new permanent-failure modes are discovered.

**[Nit] stripeService.ts:380** — `subscription.default_source` is a legacy field. Modern Stripe subscriptions use `default_payment_method`. The fallback is harmless (belt-and-suspenders) but `default_source` will likely never be populated for new subscriptions. Fine to keep.

**[Verified: OK] Race condition on `!user.stripe_subscription_id` guard** — The concern was whether `checkout.session.completed` and `customer.subscription.updated` could fire simultaneously and cause issues. Answer: safe. If checkout writes `stripe_subscription_id` first, the subscription.updated guard at line 362 properly compares IDs. If subscription.updated fires first and `stripe_subscription_id` is null, the backfill at line 375 writes it, and any subsequent checkout.completed overwrites it with the same value (checkout always sets this field unconditionally at line 310). No data loss path.

Fixed in 76ebf3e9.

**Bug 1**: `analyzeSpeakers` now returns `undefined` when `speakers.size === 0` (option 1 from the review), so a fresh recording with HTTP 200 + `{transcript: []}` falls through to the calendar-invitees fallback in `classifyMeetingStatus` as intended. Logs an `[ProspectMeeting] Empty transcript for recording N (not yet diarized)` info line so CloudWatch still sees the signal.

**Bug 2**: `transcriptOk` counter now guards on `speakerAnalysis.total > 0`. Empty transcripts already return undefined after Bug 1's fix, but the explicit `total > 0` keeps the signal correct if that invariant ever loosens.

**Test case added**: three new tests in the `analyzeSpeakers empty-transcript handling` block — the unit case (undefined on empty), the end-to-end case (empty + external invitees → `talked`, the exact scenario motivating the PR), and a populated-transcript sanity check.

Full suite: 13/13 passing locally (`npx jest --testPathPattern='prospectMeeting'`).

Skipped the nits (`__test__` export surface, Fathom cursor naming assumption) — the core review blocker is addressed and a Fathom-sandbox integration test is better scoped to its own task than bolted onto this PR.

Ready for re-review.

### Reliability
- Idempotency on `sourceRecordId = 'stripe-<eventId>'` makes Stripe's at-least-once delivery safe across the 3-day retry window.
- Identity resolution (`customer_details.email` → `findUserByStripeCustomerId` fallback) handles both fresh checkouts and subscription-only events.
- `void sendStripeEventToCrm(event)` + internal try/catch means webhook ack latency is unaffected and CRM pipeline issues can't delay / fail Stripe responses.
- Errors are logged (not silently swallowed) — real failures will show up without breaking the ack.

### Security
- Stripe signature verification in `handleWebhook` is preserved — CRM mirror runs after signature validation.
- No new surface area; only consumes already-validated event payload.

### Tests
- 6 new tests cover subscription.created/updated/deleted, checkout.session.completed, idempotency replay, and missing-email fallback.

### Nits / follow-ups (non-blocking)
- Worth a comment in the mapping table noting that `invoice.payment_failed` maps to `payment.updated` rather than a distinct `payment.failed` type — future lifecycle logic may want to distinguish. Can land in D2.

Deep read of the 9 files. Security priorities all pass:

**Crypto (`stripeConnectCrypto.ts`)**: AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2-SHA256 @ 100k iters, 12-byte random IV, 16-byte auth tag appended. Payload format `IV||ciphertext||tag`. Key derives from `CONNECT_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` with `JWT_SECRET` fallback for dev. Solid.

**OAuth state (`stripeConnect.ts` L36-52)**: JWT-signed `{userId, nonce}` with 15m expiry, `crypto.randomBytes(16)` nonce prevents replay, `verifyState` returns null on any tamper. CSRF-safe.

**Scope (`stripeConnectService.ts` L87)**: hardcoded `read_only`. Never writable.

**Webhook signature**: `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent` — fails closed on bad sig (400). Raw body registered in `app.ts` L183 BEFORE `express.json()` L184. Correct.

**Dual mode (`stripeConnectService.ts` L58-69 + routes L182-185)**: `STRIPE_CONNECT_MODE` picks client ID; webhook picks matching signing secret with fallback. Prod defaults live, else test.

**Tenant isolation**: `stripeAccount` header set via `getClientForUser`. Webhook lookup via `getUserByStripeConnectedAccountId` for deauth; email-based `syncContact` for billing events — acceptable since webhook sig verification gates the path.

**Backward compat**: Existing `/api/stripe/webhook` raw-body handler left untouched at L181.

### Nits (non-blocking)
- Webhook handler swallows downstream errors with 200 to suppress Stripe retries — acceptable tradeoff, but log level should probably be `error` not `console.error` wrapped in 200 (a noisy handler bug won't page anyone).
- `deauthorize` treats both 400 and 401 as "already revoked" — slightly aggressive but pragmatic.

### Verdict
**Approve.** Ship it. Known gaps (Settings UI, live webhook endpoint, rate limit, consent modal) correctly deferred in PR body.

## QA: FAIL — auth: cross-tenant leakage (confirmed live)

Tested against `harsha/g5-emma-action-log-b` @ 96e1eb8 deployed to test env (35.163.236.170:3001). **Senior's Phase 3 bug flag reproduces in production-shaped data.**

### Test matrix

| # | Call | Result | Verdict |
|---|------|--------|---------|
| 1 | `test@example.com` JWT → GET `/api/emma/actions` | 7 events | baseline |
| 2 | `test1@example.com` JWT → GET `/api/emma/actions` | **Same 7 events, same eventIds** | **LEAK** |
| 3 | No auth header | HTTP 401 | PASS |
| 4 | Invalid JWT | HTTP 401 | PASS |
| 5 | `?limit=-1` | **HTTP 500** (Dynamo rejects `Limit: -4`) | Senior's [Nit] bug confirmed |
| 6 | `?limit=99999` | HTTP 200, bounded via Dynamo clamp | PASS (accidentally — see below) |
| 7 | `?limit=abc` | HTTP 200, defaults to 50 | PASS |

### #1 — cross-tenant leakage (BLOCKER)

Both accounts return the identical 7 events. Sample payloads include `payload.userId: "3f90ca75-06bd-4c2c-ae68-5213e0362832"` and `"3482b1e1-17c3-4e34-8114-1a29859c8bb1"` — neither matches `test@` (c0f111be...) nor `test1@` (deleted_94470467...).

Root cause is the line Senior already flagged in `backend/src/routes/emmaApi.ts:750`:
```
FilterExpression: '#src = :src AND (attribute_not_exists(tenantId) OR tenantId = :uid)'
```
Every `engagement.emma_session` event in `Dev-AW-ContactEvents` is untenanted, so the `attribute_not_exists(tenantId)` branch matches unconditionally. A basic non-admin user (`test1@`) sees every other user's Emma session activity.

**Fix options** (both are in Senior's review):
- Tighten to `tenantId = :uid` only and backfill `tenantId` on emma_session writes in `services/contactEventsDb.ts`
- Gate the route to founders/admin-only until backfill lands (`req.user.email === 'founders@agentweb.pro'` or `isAdmin`)

Recommend option B as the 1-line v1 fix — preserves the shipping intent (founders-level visibility) without the customer-facing leak.

### #2 — negative limit 500s (blocker per brief's "400 or bounded" rule)

`?limit=-1` → `Math.min(-1, 200) = -1`, then `Limit: -4` sent to Dynamo → 500. Fix per Senior's review: `Math.max(1, Math.min(parsed, 200))`.

### What PASSED
- Auth middleware fires on missing/invalid tokens (401)
- Large `limit` and non-numeric `limit` both coerce safely
- No injection surface on query params

## Post-merge Stripe Phase 1 audit (PRs #1258, #1260–#1262, #1266, #1267; customer-portal #626, #627)

**Verdict**: **Approve with flags** — ship Phase 1 to prod, but 4 follow-ups required before Phase 2 (one security-relevant, two correctness, one UX regression). No blocker for the mega merge; all flags are discoverable only in narrow states.

Scope: read every handler touched by the 8 PRs end-to-end against `backend/src/routes/stripe.ts`, `backend/src/services/stripeService.ts`, `backend/src/controllers/stripeController.ts`, `src/pages/Pricing.tsx`, and `src/components/settings/SubscriptionCard.tsx`. ~1,100 lines read. Webhook raw-body ordering + signature verification confirmed clean (`app.ts:187` raw mounts before `express.json()`, `stripeController.ts:79` verifies before any switch case runs).

### Security findings
1. **Medium — `/api/stripe/upgrade` accepts arbitrary `newPriceId` without a whitelist** (`routes/stripe.ts:508–520`). An authenticated user can POST `{"newPriceId":"price_<any_valid_id_in_our_Stripe_account>"}` and Stripe will update their sub to that price. `deriveSubscriptionTypeFromPriceId` returns `null` for unknowns so the *tier* doesn't inflate — but billing amount can be arbitrarily downgraded to any dev/legacy $1 price that still exists. Fix: only accept `plan`, drop `newPriceId`, or validate `newPriceId ∈ {STRIPE_STARTER_PRICE_ID, STRIPE_COMPLETE_PRICE_ID}`.
2. **Low — unescaped user email in Stripe search DSL** (`routes/stripe.ts:425`, PR #1260). `` `email:"${userEmail}"` `` interpolates a value that was only loosely validated at registration (regex `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/` permits `"` and `\`; registration in `controllers/auth.ts` doesn't even call `validateEmail`). A user registering with email `foo" OR metadata["userId"]:"<victim>"` could potentially match a different customer in `customers.search`, getting another user's `stripe_customer_id` linked to their account → their next checkout would use the victim's saved payment method. Narrow exploit (requires registering with special chars + DSL knowledge + victim never having deleted the card), but trivial to fix: strip/escape `"` and `\` before interpolation, OR tighten the registration email regex to RFC-compliant.
3. **None** on webhook signature verification, ownership checks on cancel/upgrade/reactivate (all read `userId` from the middleware-derived `authenticatedReq.user`, never from the body), or on `handleCheckoutSessionCompleted` user-matching (metadata.userId is set by *our* server at checkout creation; a third-party Stripe customer cannot spoof it into a cross-account link because the email fallback still runs `userDb.getUserByEmail` and the email field on the checkout session is populated by Stripe from the paid card, not the client).

### Correctness / race conditions
1. **Medium — `/api/stripe/reactivate-subscription` is broken for trialing users + still has the `current_period_end` null crash** (`routes/stripe.ts:780–810`). Only lists `status:"active"` subs, so a user who canceled during their trial cannot reactivate. Also `new Date((updated as any).current_period_end * 1000)` on line 806 is the exact pattern PR #1262 just fixed in cancel-subscription — will crash with "Invalid time value" on the new Basil API (`current_period_end` moved to `items.data[0]`). Apply the same defensive read here.
2. **Low — reconcile clobbers the `canceling` pseudo-status** (`stripeService.ts:915–918`). `reconcileAllStripeUsers` compares `user.subscription_status !== sub.status` and writes the raw Stripe status. A user mid-cancel (DB="canceling", Stripe="active" + `cancel_at_period_end=true`) gets reset to "active" on the next admin reconcile. Fix: mirror the `handleSubscriptionUpdated` effective-status logic inside reconcile.
3. **Low (noted, not blocking) — downgrade race** on concurrent `customer.subscription.deleted` + `customer.subscription.created`. Analyzed `handleSubscriptionDeleted` (`stripeService.ts:588–644`): if the new sub hasn't propagated into `subscriptions.list` yet when deleted fires, user briefly drops to Free, then `created` fires and `handleSubscriptionUpdated({isNew:true})` writes the correct tier. Eventually consistent, bounded by Stripe's API propagation (~seconds). Acceptable; not worth a lock for our current volume.

### Tier mapping / UX
1. **Medium — `canceling` pseudo-status has no frontend handling → UX regression** (introduced by PR #1266, not caught by a corresponding frontend PR). I grepped `canceling` across `agentweb-customer-portal/src` — zero matches. Impact on a user who just cancelled mid-period:
   - `SubscriptionCard.tsx:104` `isSubscribed` = false → card shows **"Free"** tier label, hides the Manage Billing button, shows "View Plans" instead of "Manage Plan".
   - `AgentMode.tsx:2000–2001`, `ChatSupport.tsx:766`, `LeadMagnetPage.tsx:184` — premium gating all fails the check → user loses feature access **immediately** despite backend keeping them active-equivalent until `customer.subscription.deleted` fires at period end.
   - `Pricing.tsx:113` `hasActiveSubscription` = false → clicking the Free card re-enters the register flow (exactly the bug PR #627 meant to kill) and the "Switch to Free" dynamic CTA text regresses to "Get Started Free".
   Fix: treat `canceling` as equivalent to `active` everywhere the frontend currently checks `['active','trialing','past_due']`. One-line add in 5 files. Backend side is correct; this is purely a frontend sync miss.
2. **None** on `deriveSubscriptionTypeFromPriceId` — the null-fallback replacing 'Super Premium' is the right call and the error-log with price-ID-tail hints is excellent diagnostic hygiene. Legacy `"basic"` + new `"starter"` in `Pricing.tsx:TIER_PLAN_MAP` both map to `starter` — not ambiguous, just belt-and-suspenders for users with stale DB tier values. Safe.
3. **None** on `SubscriptionCard` token-meter guard (PR #626). `typeof === "number"` correctly gates NaN (NaN is a `number` type in JS and `.toLocaleString()` returns `"NaN"` without throwing — the defensive test at `SubscriptionCard.test.tsx:553` covers the valid-number path). No crash surface.

### Recommendations — Phase 2 follow-ups (ordered by blast radius)
1. Whitelist `/api/stripe/upgrade`'s `newPriceId` to `{STARTER, COMPLETE}` price IDs. 3-line change, closes the billing-downgrade exploit.
2. Apply the #1262 `current_period_end` fix to `/reactivate-subscription`; also broaden its subscription-list to include `status: "trialing"`.
3. Add `canceling` to every frontend `['active','trialing','past_due']` check (SubscriptionCard, Pricing, AgentMode, ChatSupport, LeadMagnetPage). Single-word find+replace per file.
4. Tighten registration email regex (or call `validateEmail` in `controllers/auth.ts:register` — it's already imported in `routes/waitlist.ts`). Belt for the `customers.search` interpolation defense.
5. Teach `reconcileAllStripeUsers` the `canceling` effective-status rule so admin reconciles don't regress user state.

None of these block the Phase 1 mega merge — they're Phase 2 tickets.

— Senior Reviewer, post-merge audit (2026-04-21)

## Senior Reviewer — Deep Read

**Verdict: Approve**

### Architecture
- Four routes mounted under `/api/onboarding`, all using existing `authenticateToken` + `requireUserId` plumbing. Consistent with the rest of `onboardingSteps.ts`.
- Index-based persona identity (`icp-{n}`) is a defensible v1 — the inline comment correctly notes this is a wrapper-friendly contract that won't break the FE when a stable persona-id schema lands later.
- New `valueProp?: string` field on User is appropriately separate from `marketStrategy.icp[].valueProposition` (per-ICP) — the JSDoc comment makes the distinction explicit.

### Reliability
- `parseIcpIndex` correctly rejects non-strings, malformed strings, negative ints, and non-finite values via the regex + `Number.isFinite` check.
- `sanitizePersonaPatch` uses an allow-list (`name`, `pain`, `desire`, `objection`, `meta_targeting_brief`) and returns `null` when no allowed fields present — guarantees no DB write when payload is bogus.
- All routes do validation BEFORE any DB read or write. `getUserById` happens after `parseIcpIndex` and `sanitizePersonaPatch` succeed — no wasted reads on bad input.
- Index OOB returns 404 (`idx >= list.length`), matching the test `'icp-99' against a 2-element array returns 404`.
- Length-bound on string fields (`FIELD_MAX = 2000`, `VALUE_PROP_MAX = 2000`) is conservative and prevents pathological payloads.
- `regenerate-one` re-runs the whole ICP set — comment correctly flags this as v1 limitation (the LLM service is set-level). The FE renders an optimistic per-card stall that gets superseded by the section-level stall once `icpStatus` flips to `running`. Acceptable.

### Security
- Auth middleware on all 4 routes. `requireUserId` returns the response if no user; the route handlers correctly return early after that.
- No raw user input is shell-interpolated, no SQL, no eval. Field allow-listing prevents privilege escalation via payload smuggling (test `merges only allowed fields` asserts `icpStatus` and arbitrary keys are dropped).
- `valueProp` is trimmed and length-bounded before persist.

### Compatibility
- Endpoint paths match what the FE PR (#660) calls.
- Body shapes match: `{icpId, patch}` / `{icpId}` / `{valueProp}`.
- Response shape: edit-one returns `{icpResult: nextList}`, regenerate-one returns `{status: snapshot}`, delete-one returns `{icpResult: nextList}`, value-prop returns `{valueProp: trimmed}`. FE doesn't rely on response bodies for happy path (it polls `/icp/status` for state) — fine.

1. **Regenerate-one persona index unused** — `parseIcpIndex` is called but the parsed `idx` isn't used in the orchestrator call (`startIcpDiscoveryForUser(userId)` is set-level). Consider either (a) accepting a no-id form for "regen all" or (b) actually scoping the regen to a single persona once the LLM service supports it. As-is, the index parse is purely a 400-gate. Not a blocker; the comment in code is honest about this.
2. **No rate-limit on regenerate-one** — the LLM call is expensive and an attacker (or anxious user) could spam it. Existing onboarding rate limits may cover this; worth confirming in a follow-up.

## Known Limitation: Proxy Does Not Fix Login for All Sites

The BrightData residential proxy successfully bypasses IP-level blocks (the EC2 datacenter IP is no longer flagged as a bot), but it does **not** fully solve login automation for Reddit and similar sites.

**What works:**
- IP block removed — Reddit's red "network security" banner disappears with the proxy active
- `browser_enable_proxy` tool correctly toggles a separate Playwright subprocess (with `--browser chrome`) on demand, so proxy costs are only incurred when needed

**What doesn't work (Reddit):**
- BrightData's standard residential proxy zone returns `402 bad_endpoint` on Reddit's SPA backend API calls (`/svc/shreddit/graphql`, `/svc/shreddit/events`) made via browser XHR. The login page React app can't hydrate, so the form never renders.
- Direct `curl` through the same proxy to those URLs returns 200 — it's browser-context XHR specifically that BrightData's residential peers can't route to Reddit's API tier.

**Root cause:** BrightData's residential proxy product isn't designed for full browser SPA sessions against sites like Reddit. Their **Scraping Browser** product (a separate zone type — CDP-based managed browser on their end) would handle this correctly.

**Left for future:** Full Reddit login support requires setting up a BrightData Scraping Browser zone. Once that zone is created, swapping the endpoint in `getBrightDataProxyUrl` is a small change. Leaving this as a follow-up task.

**Verdict**: **Backend behavior is clean**, but the paired FE PR (#713) has 3 reviewer-flagged bugs that reproduce live, so the coupled feature ships incomplete. Holding the gate label off this PR until #713 is resolved (the two ship together).

### What passed
- Auth gate: POST without Authorization → 401 ✅
- Validation: POST `{}` → 400 `{ code: "no_filters" }` ✅
- Happy path: POST `{ icp: "K-5 program directors", specifications: "private school directors", limit: 10 }` → 200 with 10 real LinkedIn humans, `linkedinConnected: true`, valid `cursor` ✅
- `limit: 50` → response correctly sliced to 10 ✅
- `limit: "abc"` (non-numeric) → silently ignored, defaulted to 10 ✅
- Each item shape matches the FE contract: `{ id, name, linkedin_url, headline, location, public_identifier }` (no `company` returned in this query — matches the documented optional field). ✅
- Route mount confirmed: `app.use("/api/onboarding", outreachOnboardingRoutes)` in `backend/src/app.ts:293`.

### Why we're not labelling this one yet
The endpoint itself is solid. The user-facing feature ships through `OutreachProspectReveal` on #713, where:
1. The EmmaIs loading state has no escape hatch on a hung Unipile fetch (critical UX lockup).
2. sessionStorage cache key is not user-scoped (cross-user leak on shared machines).
3. `linkedin_url` rendered as `<a href>` without protocol validation (latent XSS via upstream tampering).

See PR #713's QA report for full repros. Both PRs should ship together once #713 is fixed — labelling this one now would split the gate and let the FE land without the BE or vice-versa, neither of which is useful.

### What was NOT tested
- Live concurrency / rate-limiting under load.
- The `noLinkedInAccount: true` 200 path — admin account had Unipile connected, returned `linkedinConnected: true`. Code path was code-reviewed but not exercised.
- Pagination via `cursor` — not consumed by the FE in this sub-task.

The backend will get its `swarm:qa-passed` label as soon as #713 lands its fixes and re-passes QA.

- After ~30s the EmmaIs escape button appeared ("Taking a moment — skip this..."). Click flipped state to error: heading "Hit a snag finding prospects" with the exact copy from the fix: "This is taking longer than expected. **Fix 2 — sessionStorage cache scoping: ✅ PASS**
- Cache key in sessionStorage is now `onboarding_outreach_prospects_preview:1737485749953` (scoped to the authenticated `userId`), not the previous flat `onboarding_outreach_prospects_preview`. Verified directly via `Object.keys(sessionStorage)`.

  - `file:///etc/passwd` → NO link
  - `vbscript:msgbox("XSS-3")` → NO link

### Verified against Meta's official docs (via browser)

Checked the generated `asset_feed_spec` against Meta's Marketing API documentation and corrected the rule shape (commit `a094c362`):

- **[Asset Feed Spec](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/ad-creative/asset-feed-spec)** — confirms top-level shape: `images:[{hash, adlabels:[{name}]}]`, `bodies:[{text}]`, `titles:[{text}]`, `link_urls:[{website_url}]`, `ad_formats:["SINGLE_IMAGE"]`, `call_to_action_types`. �matches
- **[Placement Asset Customization](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/dynamic-creative/placement-asset-customization)** — the fallback rule uses an **empty** `customization_spec: {}` (the Threads example's 3rd rule confirms it), `image_label:{name}`, and `optimization_type: "PLACEMENT"`. There is **no** `priority` or `is_default` field on the wire. Also requires **≥2 customization rules** per creative (our minimal case = 1 scoped + 1 fallback ✓).
- **[Placement Targeting reference](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/audiences/reference/placement-targeting)** — confirms position enums used by the token map: `facebook_positions` includes `feed, story, facebook_reels`; `instagram_positions` includes `stream, story, explore, reels`.

Fixes applied vs. the original implementation:
1. fallback rule `{ is_default: true }` → `{ customization_spec: {} }`
2. dropped non-standard `priority` field
3. added `optimization_type: "PLACEMENT"`
4. `object_story_spec` reduced to `{ page_id }` (copy/link live entirely in `asset_feed_spec`)

## Review fix pushed — unsafe trim memo removed

An independent review found the B3 `WeakMap` memo unsafe. It assumed `messages` is append-only, but `updateConversationContext()` (`agentModeService.ts ~:3411-3434`) mutates the **same array reference in place** before the trim call (`~:2603`) on the `install_skills` path: `splice(idx,1)` then `splice(1,0,…)`. That's a **net-zero-length remove-then-reinsert** that shifts absolute indices — the memo's `cached.length <= messages.length` guard passes, the tail-scan walks nothing, and **stale indices** get served → trimmed output diverges from the original algorithm. Not behavior-preserving.

**What changed:**
- **Removed the WeakMap memo entirely** (commit `0ed08fbc`). Kept the `tool_call_id → index` Map — that alone eliminates the originally-reported per-call nested **O(n²)** scan and is correct on **every** path (append, splice, reorder), since the scan is recomputed against the live array each call.
- **Added a regression test** (`925c2cbe`): `splice/reorder safety on the same array ref` — net-zero AND length-changing reorders mirroring `updateConversationContext`, asserting deep-equality with the golden oracle on the post-splice array. Both **FAIL** against the memo'd version and **PASS** after removal (verified by reverting the service file).
- **dev.md note** (`adc43c30`).

**Verification:** `npx tsc` clean; `npm test -- agentModeService.trimToolContext agentModeService.publishFixes` → **32 passed, 0 failed** (4 characterization + 2 sub-quadratic + 2 new splice/reorder + 24 publishFixes).

**Complexity:** production `agentModeService.ts` net is now **+10 (+21/−11)**, down from **+38** in the memo'd revision — the fix both closes the bug and simplifies the code. PR body's Complexity ledger + Review-fix section updated.

## ✅ Finalization evidence — atomicity proven under real concurrency

Closes this PR's disclosed gap ("did not run concurrent real DynamoDB writes"). Ran against **`Dev-AW-Users`** (us-west-2, prod `AW-Users` never touched), replicating the exact `incrementTokenUsageForMonth` UpdateExpression + ConditionExpression from `db.ts:1346`.

**Unit tests (this branch):** 2 suites / **33 passed, 0 failed**.

**Atomic increment (the fix):**
- 30 concurrent `+100` → final `totalTokens = 3000` (expected 3000) — **0 lost updates**
- 50 concurrent `+100` → final `5000` (expected 5000), 50 procs done in 7.33s wall (genuine in-flight overlap)

**Old read-then-write (the bug), same load:**
- 30 concurrent get→put(read+100) → final `totalTokens = 100` — **29 of 30 updates lost** to last-writer-wins. This is exactly the race the PR fixes.

**Edge case — user with no `tokenUsage` map:** the conditional update does **not** crash with `ValidationException`; the `ConditionExpression` on the missing nested path fails first → `ConditionalCheckFailedException` → caught → returns `null` → caller degrades gracefully (no partial write, message flow never blocked).

**Independent correctness review verdict: SOUND.** One non-blocking note: at a month boundary, if the `month` condition fails mid-flight the helper returns `null` and that single increment is dropped (warn-logged) — strictly narrower than the bug being fixed, and the next message re-checks against the now-correct counter. Optional follow-up: single re-read+retry into the reset path, or a comment documenting the intentional boundary drop.

- Kept describe_image fallback because verification failures were a real contributor and fallback preserves the same semantic operation.
- Moved expensive-media retry budget from run-only to session-scoped when sessionId is available, so overlapping runs in one session cannot multiply 600s image timeouts.

## Follow-up: timestamp accuracy fix

User feedback after the capability fix: *"Works, but I asked Emma for timestamps of certain things, but they're not correct."*

### Verified root cause (not assumed)

`describe_video` was asking Gemini for **raw float seconds** (`{start: number (seconds)}`). Google's [video-understanding docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/video-understanding) explicitly say to ask for the **`MM:SS` format** (`"use the MM:SS format (e.g., 01:15)"`) — Gemini localizes timestamps far more reliably in the format it was trained on. Confirmed via WebFetch of Google's docs. (A second, inherent factor is the model's default 1 fps sampling, which snaps events to ~1s — not a bug.)

### Fix

- Prompt now requests **MM:SS / HH:MM:SS** for transcript, scenes, and duration.
- New `parseTimecodeToSeconds()` converts the returned timecodes back to numeric seconds, so the `{start: number, end: number}` schema and all downstream consumers are **unchanged**. Already-numeric values pass through; unparseable values are dropped (undefined) rather than emitted as a misleading `0`.

### Tests
+16 tests (MM:SS prompt assertion, MM:SS/HH:MM:SS normalization for transcript+scenes+duration, backward-compat for numeric, and a `parseTimecodeToSeconds` unit table). Changed suites: **68 passed**. `npx tsc` clean.

### End-to-end (Playwright, same video the user used — Synthesia CEO interview)

Same prompt re-run on the **fixed** backend produced a strictly chronological transcript:
`0:00 → 0:03 → 0:05 → 0:08 → 0:11 → 0:13 → 0:16 → 0:20`

vs. the **pre-fix** output in the same session, which jumped around and was garbled:
`0:24 → 3:01 → 3:12 → 2:29 (backwards) → 3:29 → "3:55 / 0:09" … 6:27 → 6:13 (backwards)`

No backward jumps, no malformed values. Screenshot evidence attached locally (`timestamp-fix-evidence-new-response.png`).

## Design pivot: Option A → Design 2 (ask scope up front)

After DMing Fangfang (the reporter + heaviest user of this surface), she chose **Design 2**: when a user asks to re-setup the brand, Emma should **ask up front which parts to update before changing anything**, rather than update the brand and offer to fix the market strategy afterward. Her reasoning: a re-setup usually reflects a positioning change that cascades to value prop → ICPs → competitors, but she'd rather confirm scope herself than have the system assume.

**New flow**
> User: "re-setup my brand"
> Emma: "Before I change anything — what do you want to update? (1) just the brand guideline (look + messaging), or (2) also re-do positioning: value prop, ICPs, competitors (this **replaces** your current ones)."

ENG-102 Agent tool telemetry writes can be dropped or reordered

## Summary Per-tool telemetry and terminal run telemetry are both written fire-and-forget. `run_completed` can be persisted before individual `tool_failed` rows, and process/worker exits can lose per-tool telemetry entirely. ## Evidence * `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts:174` wraps per-tool telemetry in a non-awaited async task. * `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts:232` records run completed/failed telemetry fire-and-forget. * `backend/src/loops/instances/agent-mode/runRecorder.ts:208` catches Dynamo write failures and only logs to console. ## Impact Daily reliability reports can undercount failures or show terminal run events before the related tool events. Tool reliability telemetry can become incomplete during shutdowns, crashes, or queue pressure. ## Acceptance criteria * Per-tool telemetry writes are awaited or durably queued before terminal run telemetry is considered complete. * Terminal run records cannot race ahead of known tool result records for the same run. * Telemetry persistence failures are surfaced as structured errors/metrics, not only console logs. * Tests cover ordering and write-failure behavior.

ENG-103 Deferred agent tool calls are excluded from reliability telemetry

## Summary Budget-deferred media/tool calls return `status: 'deferred'`, but deferred calls are filtered out of tool telemetry. This hides upstream/auth/rate-limit issues and can produce incomplete customer-facing analysis without an obvious failure signal. ## Acceptance criteria * Partial endpoint failures are represented in the tool result and telemetry. * A successful result clearly indicates which sections are complete vs unavailable. * Fatal vs partial failures are distinguished consistently. * Tests cover partial breakdown failure and assert telemetry-visible partial-failure metadata.

ENG-105 Agent tool output content is not validated before message injection

## Summary Tool output extraction accepts `formattedContent`, `content[0].text`, or `JSON.stringify(result)` with no schema check. `JSON.stringify(undefined)` can produce `undefined`, which is then passed into the tool message path. ## Evidence * `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts:73` performs loose output extraction without validating the final type/content. * `backend/src/services/agentMode/core/toolDispatch.ts:623` uses the extracted content in the tool message path. ## Impact Malformed or empty tool outputs can be treated as successful calls and injected into the agent/tool message flow as invalid or empty content. This can create silent failures and misleading telemetry. ## Acceptance criteria * Tool outputs are validated against a minimum output contract before being treated as successful. * Invalid/empty/undefined extracted content becomes a structured tool failure. * Telemetry captures invalid output failures distinctly from execution failures. * Tests cover undefined, malformed object, empty content array, and valid formatted content.

No filer checks for an existing issue containing the same Session/Schedule ID. ## Root cause 3 — customer retest/regression filed as NEW issue instead of reopening [ENG-211](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-211/agw-58-marked-resolved-but-google-ads-connection-still-fails-after)/212/219 all say "FOLLOW-UP / REGRESSION on AGW-58" **in their own titles** — the intake knew it was the same bug but has no reopen primitive, so it created three new canonicals in one day (all manually folded into [ENG-179](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-179/urgent-google-ads-account-connection-fails-after-completing-oauth) on 7/7). Store the extracted context where Emma and the admin/customer-success UI can retrieve it. 5. Use it to prefill onboarding/account setup where confidence is high. 6. Put ambiguous cases into review instead of creating bad data. ## Suggested first slice Do not overbuild a universal Fathom integration first. Start with a small admin/HM workflow: 1. Harsha selects or confirms a Fathom recording for ingestion. 2. System extracts structured context from the summary/transcript. 3. System proposes a target org/contact match or asks for one. 4. System saves a reviewed context object onto the account/contact. 5. Emma can read that context during onboarding or customer-support chat. Then automate selection/matching once the manual-confirm flow is reliable. ## Structured fields to extract Minimum fields: * Company name. * Primary contact name/email if available. * Website/domain. * Product/category. * ICP / target audience. * Primary GTM goal. * Relevant channels: Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn, email, landing pages, events, CRM, voice/calling. * Win metric / success definition. * Urgency and timeline. * Setup blockers: missing domain, no ad account, no email setup, no Slack/Teams channel, no bandwidth, etc. * Product-fit notes. * Explicit feature gaps or risks. * Suggested first-win path. * Source Fathom recording URL and timestamp references. Do not create a new production customer/account from fuzzy title-only data without review. This PR adds a deterministic `composite_images` tool backed by `sharp` that assembles N specific image URLs into an exact grid, row, column, or honeycomb layout — solving the root cause of exact-count failures that generative models can't reliably satisfy. It wires the new `ImageService.compositeImages` / `computeCompositeLayout` methods through a new `AgentModeService.compositeImages` handler, registers the tool as a foundation tool, and adds system-prompt guidance directing Emma to reach for it on exact-count requests. - **`ImageService.computeCompositeLayout`** computes per-cell positions for `grid`, `row`, `column`, and `honeycomb` layouts; `compositeImages` downloads each URL, resizes to cover its cell, optionally applies a circular SVG mask, composites onto a sharp canvas, and uploads the PNG to S3. - **Test coverage** spans 13 layout / validation / error-path tests in `imageGeneration.compositeImages.test.ts` and 5 handler tests in `agentModeService.compositeImages.test.ts`; one coverage gap exists for the single-row honeycomb case (see inline comment).

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge — the new compositing path is self-contained, wraps every error, and the layout math is correct for all primary multi-row use cases. The honeycomb width formula unconditionally adds a half-cell margin regardless of whether any odd rows exist. For a single-row honeycomb (e.g. one image, or `columns` set equal to `count`), the canvas comes out noticeably wider than the content — most visibly for the degenerate single-image case where a 256 px cell produces a 392 px wide PNG. This PR fixes an authorization gap where org members could access the org's ClickUp, Foreplay, and Google Drive integrations even when the org admin had set Knowledge Bases sharing to "Private." The fix adds a single entitlement gate — `isFeatureEffectivelyEnabled(caller, org, 'knowledgeBase')` — in each of the three resolution paths, mirroring the existing pattern already in place for KB file visibility. - **`clickupService.ts` / `foreplayService.ts`**: `getAccessToken` now skips the org token for plain members when KB sharing is off and falls through to their personal token (or the Foreplay platform key). The existing try/catch structure is preserved. - **`agentModeService.ts` `getUserGoogleDriveFolders`**: org folders are returned only to entitled callers; non-entitled org members now fall through to their own personal `googleDriveFolders` array (previous behavior returned `[]` for all org members unconditionally). - **Tests**: 7 TDD-first tests added across three test files covering owner, KB editor, member-on, member-off, and personal-token-fallback scenarios.

No bypass paths were found — org secrets and Drive folders are only read through the newly gated functions. Greptile Summary

This PR fixes ENG-244 where long scheduled runs that exhaust the tool-loop step budget (`maxIterations=40`) would finish with partial output instead of the final consolidated report, because the existing text-pattern completion gate had nothing to match against when the model wrote its own non-apology partial text at truncation time. - **`agentModeService.ts`**: Adds a deterministic `truncatedByStepBudget` flag, set to `true` when `iteration >= maxIterations` (before the canned-apology content fallback), and spreads it into the returned result object. - **`agentModeController.ts`**: Adds `scheduledRunSignalsIncompleteResponse()` that ORs the new flag with the existing text detector, adds a `completionGateBudgetTruncated` boolean to tailor the continuation prompt, and uses both at both gate check points in `runVerifiedChat`. - **Tests**: Three new test files cover the real-loop flag-setting behaviour, the unit-level gate function, and the end-to-end `runScheduledChat` path; all 27 completion-gate tests pass.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge with one small follow-up: the worker service interface needs `truncatedByStepBudget` added so the type system can verify the flag's full propagation path. The `GenerateMarketingResponseResult` interface in `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.ts` does not declare `truncatedByStepBudget`, which is the flag the entire ENG-244 fix relies on. At runtime the flag propagates correctly, but TypeScript cannot verify this link across the IPC boundary — a refactor that drops it would compile cleanly and silently regress the fix. backend/src/services/generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.ts — the `GenerateMarketingResponseResult` interface needs `truncatedByStepBudget?: boolean` to close the type gap.

ENG-308 Subdomain middleware silently overwrites the lead-capture middleware — attaching a domain destroys attribution

Two different functions write `middleware.ts` to a generated landing page's repo root, and **neither knows the other exists**. The second one destroys the first. ## The bug * `injectLeadCaptureAttribution` (`backend/src/services/v0Service.ts:2284`) writes the **lead-capture** middleware at generation — the one that stamps the `aw_first_touch` cookie from `utm_*` / `gclid` / `fbclid`. This is the entire client-side half of attribution ([ENG-49](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-49)). * `updateSubdomainMiddleware` (`backend/src/services/v0Service.ts:3713`) writes a **subdomain-routing** middleware (`MIDDLEWARE_CONTENT`, `:3685`) to the SAME path `middleware.ts`, via a GitHub git-tree write that **replaces that path's blob**. It contains **zero** capture logic — no `aw_first_touch`, no `utm_` anywhere. It is called from `routes/domains.ts` (`:213`, `:359`, `:450`) whenever a domain or subdomain is attached to or removed from a page. ## Impact Sequence: 1. Page is generated → gets the capture middleware. 2. User attaches a domain/subdomain to make it publicly addressable (landing pages use managed `*.agentwebforms.com` subdomains — prod records show e.g. `free-ai-seogeo-audit.agentwebforms.com`). 3. `updateSubdomainMiddleware` fires → `middleware.ts` is overwritten with the routing-only version. 4. **Lead capture is silently and permanently destroyed.** No error. Attribution for that page is dead until it is regenerated. This defeats the entire attribution program on its own. Even with [ENG-239](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-239) (ads now carry UTMs) and [ENG-287](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-287) (generation unblocked), a newly generated page would get capture and then lose it the moment anyone gave it a domain — which is a normal, expected step. It is a strong candidate for why prod shows **0 attributed leads out of 225,981**. ## Fix Next.js supports only ONE root `middleware.ts`, so the two behaviours must live in one file. Emit a single canonical middleware that does BOTH: the subdomain rewrite AND the first-touch capture (set the cookie on the rewritten response). Both writers must produce that merged file. Note `MIDDLEWARE_CONTENT` imports `./domainMap`, which the capture middleware does not — so generation should always emit a `domainMap.ts` (empty map is fine) so the merged template compiles from day one. ## Acceptance criteria 1. Attaching or removing a domain/subdomain on a landing page does NOT remove lead capture — the `aw_first_touch` cookie is still set afterwards. 2. Generating a page and then attaching a subdomain yields a `middleware.ts` that performs the subdomain rewrite AND sets the first-touch cookie. 3. A regression test asserts both behaviours coexist in the emitted middleware (both writers). 4. Existing pages whose capture was already clobbered are identified (a report is enough; regenerating/retrofitting them can be a follow-up).

## Closing — the reported bug is already fixed on `main`, and this change now conflicts with it

Closing without merging. The ENG-197 lockout is resolved on `main` by three independent changes that landed after this PR was opened:

- **ENG-182 / ENG-222** — per-recipient breaker scope (`failureScope()` keys failures by `profile_url` / `provider_id` / `invitation_id`), so failures to different profiles never aggregate to trip the run-level breaker.
- **ENG-313** — extends that per-recipient scope to more actions and adds the same-tool-retry guardrail. It **deliberately keeps `invalid_args` fast-tripping at threshold 2** for genuine same-recipient spirals, solving the "different arguments" problem via scoping rather than by relaxing the threshold.
- **ENG-191 / ENG-243** — removes the pre-dispatch length gate; over-limit notes are auto-trimmed on the tier-aware send path, so they no longer fail with `Invalid parameters` at all.

### Why not merge this PR anyway

This PR's one-line change moves `invalid_args` out of `FAST_TRIP_ERROR_CLASSES` (threshold 2 → 3). That is now the **opposite** of ENG-313's deliberate design on the same error class. Verified concretely: rebasing this branch onto current `main` and running the suite fails ENG-313's test `still trips when the SAME get-profile recipient fails repeatedly` (it asserts the breaker trips at 2; our change pushes it to 3). Since tests don't run in CI, merging would silently break `main`.

The reported customer scenario (a `send-invite` batch where two over-limit/`Invalid parameters` failures to different profiles locked out the rest of the run) no longer reproduces on `main` — per-recipient scoping keeps each profile in its own breaker bucket, and auto-trim keeps over-limit notes from failing.

No code change is needed. ENG-197 is resolved by the changes above.

ENG-309 Landing page generated without a leadListId silently gets no lead capture (and no error)

`injectLeadCaptureAttribution` is guarded by `if (leadListId)` (`backend/src/services/v0Service.ts:2317`). The page looks fine, is deployed, collects form fills, and attributes **nothing**, forever. The capture route needs a `LIST_ID` to forward leads to, so the guard is not wrong in itself — but failing silently is. ## Fix (needs a decision) Either: * **(a)** resolve/create a default lead list for the user at generation time so `leadListId` is always present, or * **(b)** fail loudly — refuse to generate a lead-capture landing page with no lead list, and tell the user why. (a) is the better product outcome; (b) is the safer minimum. Worth a quick call. ## Acceptance criteria 1. It is impossible to end up with a deployed landing page that has a lead form but no capture middleware, without the user being told. 2. If generation proceeds without a lead list, that fact is visible (surfaced to the user and/or on the `AW-LandingPages` record) — never silent. 3. Regression test covers the no-leadListId path. ENG-310 Attaching a lead list AFTER generation never injects the capture files — the page captures nothing, forever

`PUT /api/landing-pages/v0/generated/:id/lead-list` (`backend/src/routes/landingPageGeneration.ts:1996`) attaches a lead list to an existing landing page by writing DynamoDB **and nothing else**. It never touches the page's GitHub repo, so it never injects `middleware.ts` or `app/api/capture/route.ts`. Capture is baked in at **generation** time only (`v0Service.ts:2317`). So the natural workflow — 1. generate a landing page, 2. then wire it to a CRM lead list — produces a page that **captures nothing, forever**, while its `AW-LandingPages` record cheerfully claims a `leadListId`. Anyone inspecting the record would conclude attribution is on. This is likely why several of the pages that DO carry a `leadListId` still produce no attributed leads. ## Fix Inject the capture files into the existing repo on lead-list attach, then let Vercel redeploy. **The machinery already exists** — `POST /generated/:id/gtm` (`landingPageGeneration.ts:1520`) and `updateSubdomainMiddleware` (`v0Service.ts:3713`) both already do read-file → commit to GitHub → Vercel auto-redeploys. Reuse that pattern. ⚠️ Must be done together with the middleware-clobber fix (the CRITICAL issue in this batch), or the injected capture will be overwritten by the next domain operation. ## Bonus: this unlocks the retrofit The same mechanism retrofits capture onto the ~131 landing pages generated BEFORE the capture middleware shipped (2026-07-02). They are all permanently attribution-blind today, and a Vercel redeploy does NOT fix them — only a commit that adds the files does. ## Acceptance criteria 1. Attaching a lead list to an existing landing page injects the capture middleware + capture route into its repo and triggers a redeploy. 2. A page wired to a lead list after generation captures a lead with `firstTouch.utm.source` populated (verify end-to-end, not just by unit test). 3. If injection cannot be performed, the attach fails loudly rather than writing a `leadListId` that means nothing. 4. A report lists existing pages that have a `leadListId` but no capture files in their repo.
