ENG-528 Emma admin tool: inspect and change client token allowance safely

## Capability gap found during real support work On 2026-07-26, Harsha asked Emma/Codex to investigate Kevin Rajan's exhausted quota and upgrade `harsha@agentcapx.com` to the Pro allowance. Emma could inspect the client list and confirm the account identity/tier, but had no tool to: * return the effective allowance and current usage for a named client, * compare the legacy monthly counter with the per-model usage ledger, * change a client's subscription tier, * grant a temporary token bonus, or * verify the resulting effective allowance. The operation therefore required god-access to production DynamoDB (`AW-Users`, `AW-Settings`, `AW-UsageRecords`). Per the standing rule, this is an Emma capability gap, not an acceptable long-term support workflow. Related metering/admin work: [ENG-249](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-249/feature-request-emma-mcp-payment-and-metering-layer-1-pager-prd) and [ENG-515](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-515/token-usage-breakdown-dashboard). ## Proposed capability boundary Add a narrowly scoped admin-only Emma tool for client allowance operations. Reads should expose usage/tier/effective allowance and ledger reconciliation. Writes must require explicit confirmation, use conditional updates/idempotency, return before/after state, preserve an audit trail, and never expose secret values. ## PURE / MOCKABLE assessment MOCKABLE: yes. The service contract can be tested entirely against mocked user, settings, usage-ledger, auth, and audit adapters; no live Stripe or production DynamoDB access is required for implementation tests. ## Complexity impact Reduce complexity by wrapping the existing admin subscription/token-bonus service contract in one auditable Emma operation instead of maintaining a parallel backend-poke runbook. ## Acceptance criteria (must pass before PR opens) ### Behavioral contract (HUMAN-WRITTEN FROM STANDING BACKEND-POKE DIRECTIVE — agent MUST NOT modify) 1. An authorized AgentWeb admin can ask Emma to resolve a client by exact email and see current tier, current-month usage, base allowance, bonus allowance, effective allowance, reset date, and whether the account is currently blocked. 2. With explicit confirmation, the admin can change the account's subscription tier or grant a positive current-month token bonus through Emma. 3. Mutations are conditional/idempotent and return verified before/after state; concurrent changes are detected rather than overwritten. 4. Every mutation is audit-logged with acting admin, target user, timestamp, reason, and before/after values. 5. Non-admin callers cannot enumerate or mutate client accounts, and no secret/token values are returned. 6. The tool reuses the existing subscription/token-usage services rather than writing DynamoDB directly. ### Implementation tests (AGENT-WRITTEN against the contract above) * Unit and route/MCP tests for reads, confirmed writes, rejected unconfirmed writes, authorization, conditional conflict, audit output, and idempotency. * Cite every behavioral assertion in the PR verification section. ## Operational evidence * Target account: `harsha@agentcapx.com` * User ID: `e86420f2-4374-4774-9361-e4c3abac5516` * Observed usage: 3,033,275 tokens in July 2026 * Free allowance: 3,000,000 * Pro allowance: 300,000,000 * Emma verdict: inspection partly available; allowance mutation and detailed reconciliation required god-access.

Root cause, `.github/workflows/tests.yml` `detect-changes` step: ```yaml filters: | backend: - 'backend/**' - '.github/workflows/tests.yml' - '.github/scripts/eb-deploy.sh' ``` `backend/**` has no exclusion for test paths, so `backend/src/__tests__/**` sets `backend=true`, and `backend-staging-deploy` gates only on `needs.detect-changes.outputs.backend == 'true'` plus the two test jobs and Greptile. ## Why it's worth doing Two distinct costs, and the second is the worse one: 1. **Runner minutes.** A full build + package + S3 upload + EB deploy + verify on every test-only PR, on a repo whose org Actions budget carries `prevent_further_usage: true` and is currently projected at **91% of a $200 cap** (`$58.82` spent on day 10). A test-only PR therefore occupies the one shared staging slot and blocks real backend PRs behind it. The swarm already serializes ready-flips by hand because of this lane (`loop-sprint-worker.md` §9); test-only PRs consuming it makes that constraint tighter than it needs to be. ## Design nuance for whoever picks this up Do **not** naively narrow the filter — there are two live constraints: * [ENG-743](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-743/staging-deploy-job-reports-success-even-when-the-elastic-beanstalk) deliberately added `tests.yml` and `eb-deploy.sh` to the `backend` filter so a change to the deploy job can be exercised on its own PR. Any narrowing must preserve that. * Splitting `backend` into two outputs (e.g. `backend_tests` vs `backend_deployable`) is probably the shape — test jobs keep firing on `backend/**`, while only the deploy job requires a non-test change. ENG-1528 Switching a pooled colleague's scheduled task 404s — drivers read across the bill, apply is owner-only

Reported from production on `founders@agentweb.pro`, 2026-08-24. Confirmed in code. ## Symptom Clicking **"Switch this task to gpt-5.4-nano"** on a scheduled task returns: ``` POST https://api.agentweb.pro/api/subscription/usage-runway/apply 404 Not Found ``` Nothing is switched. The button is offered on rows where it cannot possibly succeed. ## Cause — two different scopes for the same schedule list The two halves of this feature disagree about **whose** schedules are in play. **Reading** (`llmUsageDriversResolverService.ts:620`) pools across the whole bill: ```ts const pooledUserIds = await resolvePooledLedgerUserIds(usage.billingUserId); const lists = await Promise.all(pooledUserIds.map((id) => scheduleDb.getSchedulesByUserId(id))); ``` **Writing** (`llmModelChangeService.ts:167`) is strictly owner-only, and deliberately so: ```ts if (!schedule || schedule.userId !== userId) { throw new ModelChangeNotFoundError("Scheduled chat not found"); } // "Owner-only, exactly as `updateScheduledChat` does. No org bypass: an org // member does not get to retune a colleague's schedule because they share a bill." ``` So every schedule belonging to a *pooled colleague* renders with a confirm button, and every one of those buttons 404s. The reported account's list contains exactly that: `Harsha Daily X Post (Autonomous)`, `Harsha X Reply Guy — Mentions (auto)`, `Managed Client Weekly Ads Update`. All ten rows report `scheduleExists: true` — the resolver found them, because it looked across pooled users. The write then refuses them because they are not owned by the caller. **This is not the deleted-schedule case (ENG-1438).** These schedules exist. The 404 is an ownership refusal wearing a not-found status. ## Why the reporter tied it to "0 days recovered" Coincidence of which rows they happened to click. Ownership, not the estimate, decides the 404 — a 0-day row owned by the caller would apply fine, and a 5-day row owned by a colleague would still 404. ## Why it matters This is the exact defect ENG-1438 was written to remove: *"exclude deleted schedules from the switchable list so no customer is offered an action that cannot succeed."* The same principle is being violated by a different mechanism. It also spends the customer's trust at the worst moment — the one click in this whole feature that changes something. ## The decision this needs The owner-only rule is deliberate and documented. So the question is not "remove the check", it is **which of these**: 1. **Surface ownership** — the driver payload gains an owner (or a plain `switchable` flag), and the UI says "owned by another member" instead of offering a button. Keeps the security rule, removes the false offer. Requires a backend field. 2. **Allow pooled owners to apply** — reverses a rule whose comment argues explicitly against it. A product/security call, not a bug fix. 3. **Hide non-owned schedules from the list entirely** — but they are real spend on this bill, and hiding them recreates the blindness ENG-1440 existed to fix. (1) looks right: the spend stays visible, the action stops lying, and the security boundary is untouched. ## Also worth fixing regardless The 404 currently surfaces as `"Scheduled chat not found"`, which is untrue and unhelpful — the schedule exists, the caller just does not own it. Whatever is chosen above, the message should say so.

Identical failure both times. ## The failure `.github/scripts/eb-deploy.test.sh` — **2 of 79 checks**, everything else green: ``` [eb-deploy] [verify] Status=Ready Health=Red Version=backend-20260729-pr2216 [eb-deploy] Environment reached Ready on version '...'; confirming health. ##[error]EB_DEPLOY_FAILED: ... its health stayed Red for 1s after becoming Ready, and the underlying instance/target health could not be established, so the deploy is NOT confirmed: describe-instances-health returned no instances. ``` Both occurrences were byte-identical, including the `1s`. ## Why it looks like wall-clock flake rather than a real defect The harness runs the real `eb-deploy.sh` against a mock AWS CLI, and the mock queue supports scripted delays (`sleep "${first#*|}"`, line 147). Its defaults are extremely tight: ```sh EB_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS='0' EB_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS='2' EB_HEALTH_SETTLE_SECONDS='1' ``` so a case expecting health to settle Green has a **one-second wall-clock budget**, measured with `date +%s` (line 278). On a shared, loaded GitHub runner, a scheduling stall inside that window is enough for the script to give up before the mock's healthy response is consumed — surfacing exactly as *"stayed Red for 1s"* and *"returned no instances"*. `date +%s` also has 1-second granularity, so a budget of 1 second can be anywhere from just over 0s to nearly 2s of real time depending on where the boundary falls. Not reproduced locally — filed on the evidence of two identical CI occurrences rather than a repro. ## Why it is worth fixing rather than re-running Each hit costs a full CI cycle. On this repo `main` moves fast enough that PRs go `behind` while a re-run happens, which forces a re-sync and *another* full cycle. Twice today that turned a green PR into roughly twenty extra minutes. It also trains the reflex this repo can least afford: dismissing a red `CI script tests` as "probably the EB flake" — the same job also guards the Dependabot supply-chain checks (`10 checks run, 0 failed` in both logs). ## Suggested direction 1. Make the settle logic **deterministic** in tests — drive it from the mock's own event sequence rather than wall-clock, or inject a clock. 2. Failing that, raise `EB_HEALTH_SETTLE_SECONDS` in the harness well above runner jitter (a value only the test uses, so production behaviour is untouched). 3. Have the two affected cases assert the *decision* rather than "it happened within N seconds", if timing is not what they exist to prove. ## Evidence * PR #1092, head `bffd72da` — job 97419071309 * PR #1093, head `3b8d179a` — job 97422638173

ENG-1526 override_tracking_check is HMAC-bound on Meta and free-text on Google; no write confirmation; audit trail no-ops

## Three related gaps in one control surface ### 1. The override is unbound on the Google path Same file, two lines: ``` 18818 Meta: const overrideTrackingCheck = overrideApproved; 34124 Google: const overrideTrackingCheck = args.override_tracking_check === true; ``` Meta binds the override to an HMAC (`computeTrackingOverrideDigest`) over the exact call, issued by a preview the user actually saw, and refuses a replay that doesn't present the matching token. Its comment states the threat model: > *"the model could preview a plain activation, let the user approve THAT, and then add* `override_tracking_check` *to the replay — waiving the measurement check on something the user was never told would skip it. An override the model can introduce after approval is not user-granted, whatever the tool description says."* Google's only defence **is** that tool description (`"Never set it on your own."`) — the exact thing that comment dismisses as insufficient. ### 2. Google Ads writes have no confirmation gate `isMetaWriteAction` halts the turn and requires user approval. `buildGoogleAdsWriteConfirmation` **does not exist** — zero matches. Enabling a campaign that spends real money requires no confirmation. ### 3. The audit trail silently no-ops `recordGoogleAdsMeasurementCheck` opens `if (!sessionId) return;` — under a docstring promising a launch decision *"can never be silently hidden"*. The block message and the tool description both tell users "the override is recorded". On an external MCP client with no session id, it is not. Separately: `googleAdsMeasurementChecks` has **two writes and zero readers** repo-wide — no route, no service, no UI. Even when written, nobody can read it. ## Fix Reuse Meta's existing digest/token handshake rather than writing a second one; make the audit write fail loudly when it cannot record; and give the record a reader (or stop promising it in user-facing copy). Found in the [https://claude.ai/code/artifact/c542456e-4aa3-414b-b103-9ab1e77a7916]() audit.

ENG-1519 A tool identifier is being attributed as a model (twitter:get_user_tweets in byModel)

Found while reviewing the spend breakdown on the founders account, 2026-08-24. ## Symptom The **Models** group in "Where your usage went" lists: ``` twitter:get_user_tweets 4% 427 calls ``` That is a tool identifier, not a model. ## Why it reaches the customer `/api/subscription/usage-drivers` returns it inside `drivers.byModel`. The portal renders `byModel` verbatim through `modelLabel()`, which only strips `anthropic|amazon|google|openai` vendor prefixes — anything else passes through unchanged. So whatever the ledger puts in that field is what the customer reads. The UI is doing the right thing with wrong data; this needs fixing in the attribution/ledger layer, not the portal. ## Why it matters beyond cosmetics `byModel` is not a neutral list. It is the input to the surface whose whole job is *"which model should you switch?"* — a row there implies a switchable model. `twitter:get_user_tweets` cannot be switched, has no cheaper equivalent, and would produce a nonsensical recommendation if one were ever generated for it. It also silently distorts the model breakdown: 4% of the cycle is attributed to a "model" that does not exist, so every real model's share is understated against a denominator containing a non-model. ## Worth checking while in there Whether this is one leaked key or a class — i.e. are other tool identifiers (`x-account` appears as a *feature*, correctly) landing in `byModel` for other accounts? A single bad row and a systematic mis-tagging of one call type need different fixes. ## Not reproducible on every account `aseth@argusoft.com`'s `byModel` contains only real model ids (`anthropic.claude-opus-5`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14`, `openrouter/qwen/qwen3.8-max`), so this is specific to the call types the founders account exercises — likely the X/Twitter integration path.

ENG-1362 A Google Ads account named "Test" has test_account=false — it is real, billable, and the name is the only thing saying otherwise

A connected Google Ads account whose descriptive name is **"Test"** has `customer.test_account = false`. It is a real, billable, ENABLED account container. The name is the only thing suggesting it is safe, and the name carries no authority. Verified read-only against production on 2026-08-19, via `call_google_ads_reporting_api` on the two accounts connected to [hshah@argusoft.com](): | customer id | descriptive_name | test_account | manager | currency | | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | | 2883029950 | AgentWeb | **false** | false | INR | | 3413286111 | **Test** | **false** | false | INR | `3413286111` is a leaf account (`manager: false`), so it can serve ads directly. Anything enabled in it spends real INR. ## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note Google's own safety mechanism for this is `customer.test_account`. A true test account **cannot serve ads and cannot spend** — that is the guarantee. This account has the word "Test" in its name and none of that protection. The two look identical to a human skimming an account picker, and identical to any agent that reasons over the descriptive name. We already rely on name strings as a safety signal elsewhere, which is what makes this a pattern and not a one-off. Campaign `24151546304` on `2883029950` is literally named `ENG-1182 Tracking Validation — DO NOT ENABLE` and sits on an ENABLED ₹500/day budget. The name is doing the work a flag should be doing. Both cases fail the same way: the string says safe, the API says billable. The realistic failure is not malice. It is someone — or an Emma run — picking the account that says "Test" to try something, because that is exactly what the name invites. ## Current exposure: zero, and that is the point Swept `3413286111` read-only on 2026-08-19 across five GAQL queries: * 0 campaigns (including REMOVED), 0 ad groups, 0 ads, 0 budgets * account-level all-time `cost_micros` 0, impressions 0, clicks 0 — read from the `customer` resource directly, not inferred from the empty campaign list * `customer.status = ENABLED` — the container is live, it simply has no contents The risk is **prospective, not active**. Nothing is wrong today. This is filed now precisely because it is cheap to fix while the account is empty, and expensive to discover after something is built in it. Worth recording how the empty result was confirmed: a campaign query returning 0 rows looks identical whether the account is genuinely empty or the query was scoped wrong. The `customer` resource was queried separately and returned a real row with real zero metrics. Two resources agreeing is what makes this a finding rather than a guess. ## Proposed fix Do not trust the name. Read the flag. 1. **Surface** `test_account` **wherever an account is chosen or displayed** — connected-accounts list, account pickers, and any agent-facing account listing. A real test account should be visibly, unmistakably marked; everything else should read as billable by default. 2. **Have** `list_connected_accounts` **return** `test_account` so agent reasoning has access to the fact rather than inferring from a string. Today the flag is queryable but not surfaced, so an agent choosing "the test one" has only the name to go on. 3. **Rename** `3413286111` to something that does not claim a safety property it lacks (e.g. `AgentWeb Sandbox (BILLABLE)`). A rename is not a control, but it stops the name actively lying. (1) and (2) are the durable fixes; (3) is a cheap immediate mitigation. ## Explicitly not proposed Blocking writes to non-test accounts. Every real customer account is `test_account: false` — that is the normal case, not the exception, and gating on it would block all legitimate work. The fix is to make the flag **visible**, not to make it a gate. ## How to verify Read-only, no writes, no spend: ``` SELECT customer.id, customer.descriptive_name, customer.test_account, customer.manager, customer.currency_code FROM customer ``` Run per connected customer id. A fix is confirmed when the `test_account` value for each account is visible in the UI and in `list_connected_accounts` output without running GAQL by hand. ## Context Found while closing out the zero-spend verification for [ENG-1157] / [ENG-1182]. That sweep originally covered `2883029950` only — the second connected account was not swept until this check, which is itself part of the finding: a second billable account was easy to miss. It has now been swept and is clean.

ENG-1268 Customer-reported fixes get marked resolved without end-to-end verification — RankAI churned after being "fixed" 3 times

## What's wrong RankAI's tracking issue was reported "fixed" three separate times (2026-07-24, 07-30, 08-03) with no end-to-end verification behind any of the three claims, before the account churned at ~$5,200 lifetime spend. The same discipline gap is separately named on AgentWeb's own ad account ([ENG-1018](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1018/meta-campaign-spend-cap-update-reports-success-but-there-is-no-way-to): "verify by raw Graph API GET, don't trust the response") — this is the version of that same gap that cost a real customer, not just internal time. The general failure mode: a fix gets pushed, the person/system that pushed it declares it fixed, and nobody independently confirms the actual customer-facing symptom is gone before the issue closes. ## Why urgent This directly caused a real, named churn. It's also a repeat pattern (3 times on the same issue) rather than a one-off mistake, which means it's a process/tooling gap, not a person having a bad day. ## Proposed shape For customer-reported bug fixes specifically (as opposed to internal engineering bugs, which already have the Post-Merge Verifier / Closure Reconciler machinery per `autonomous-execution-and-merge.md`): require a recorded, independent verification step — checking the actual customer-facing symptom via a raw API read or equivalent ground-truth check, not the fix-author's own claim — before the Linear issue is allowed to move to a closed/resolved state. This should reuse the existing Post-Merge Verifier pattern rather than invent a parallel system. ## Acceptance criteria 1. A customer-reported bug issue cannot transition to a closed/resolved state without an attached verification record (what was checked, how, and the result). 2. The verification check is against the actual customer-facing symptom (e.g., "pixel fires on a live page load," checked via a raw read), not "the code change merged." 3. Given a fix that was pushed but not yet independently verified, attempting to close the issue is blocked with a clear reason. 4. RankAI's actual issue history (three false "fixed" claims) is used as a regression case: replayed against the new gate, none of the three would have been allowed to close without the missing verification step. ## Test cases * Unit/integration test: closing a customer-reported issue without a verification record is rejected. * Unit/integration test: closing with a valid verification record succeeds. * Regression: RankAI's three historical "fixed" comments, replayed, are correctly rejected by the new gate. ## Complexity ledger Complexity: Medium — extends existing verification/closure machinery (Post-Merge Verifier, Closure Reconciler) to cover customer-reported bugs specifically, rather than building something new. ## Source AgentWeb Landscape Study — August 2026 Amendment, "unsexy things" #6.

ENG-1362 A Google Ads account named "Test" has test_account=false — it is real, billable, and the name is the only thing saying otherwise

A connected Google Ads account whose descriptive name is **"Test"** has `customer.test_account = false`. It is a real, billable, ENABLED account container. The name is the only thing suggesting it is safe, and the name carries no authority. Verified read-only against production on 2026-08-19, via `call_google_ads_reporting_api` on the two accounts connected to [hshah@argusoft.com](): | customer id | descriptive_name | test_account | manager | currency | | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | | 2883029950 | AgentWeb | **false** | false | INR | | 3413286111 | **Test** | **false** | false | INR | `3413286111` is a leaf account (`manager: false`), so it can serve ads directly. Anything enabled in it spends real INR. ## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note Google's own safety mechanism for this is `customer.test_account`. A true test account **cannot serve ads and cannot spend** — that is the guarantee. This account has the word "Test" in its name and none of that protection. The two look identical to a human skimming an account picker, and identical to any agent that reasons over the descriptive name. We already rely on name strings as a safety signal elsewhere, which is what makes this a pattern and not a one-off. Campaign `24151546304` on `2883029950` is literally named `ENG-1182 Tracking Validation — DO NOT ENABLE` and sits on an ENABLED ₹500/day budget. The name is doing the work a flag should be doing. Both cases fail the same way: the string says safe, the API says billable. The realistic failure is not malice. It is someone — or an Emma run — picking the account that says "Test" to try something, because that is exactly what the name invites. ## Current exposure: zero, and that is the point Swept `3413286111` read-only on 2026-08-19 across five GAQL queries: * 0 campaigns (including REMOVED), 0 ad groups, 0 ads, 0 budgets * account-level all-time `cost_micros` 0, impressions 0, clicks 0 — read from the `customer` resource directly, not inferred from the empty campaign list * `customer.status = ENABLED` — the container is live, it simply has no contents The risk is **prospective, not active**. Nothing is wrong today. This is filed now precisely because it is cheap to fix while the account is empty, and expensive to discover after something is built in it. Worth recording how the empty result was confirmed: a campaign query returning 0 rows looks identical whether the account is genuinely empty or the query was scoped wrong. The `customer` resource was queried separately and returned a real row with real zero metrics. Two resources agreeing is what makes this a finding rather than a guess. ## Proposed fix Do not trust the name. Read the flag. 1. **Surface** `test_account` **wherever an account is chosen or displayed** — connected-accounts list, account pickers, and any agent-facing account listing. A real test account should be visibly, unmistakably marked; everything else should read as billable by default. 2. **Have** `list_connected_accounts` **return** `test_account` so agent reasoning has access to the fact rather than inferring from a string. Today the flag is queryable but not surfaced, so an agent choosing "the test one" has only the name to go on. 3. **Rename** `3413286111` to something that does not claim a safety property it lacks (e.g. `AgentWeb Sandbox (BILLABLE)`). A rename is not a control, but it stops the name actively lying. (1) and (2) are the durable fixes; (3) is a cheap immediate mitigation. ## Explicitly not proposed Blocking writes to non-test accounts. Every real customer account is `test_account: false` — that is the normal case, not the exception, and gating on it would block all legitimate work. The fix is to make the flag **visible**, not to make it a gate. ## How to verify Read-only, no writes, no spend: ``` SELECT customer.id, customer.descriptive_name, customer.test_account, customer.manager, customer.currency_code FROM customer ``` Run per connected customer id. A fix is confirmed when the `test_account` value for each account is visible in the UI and in `list_connected_accounts` output without running GAQL by hand. ## Context Found while closing out the zero-spend verification for [ENG-1157] / [ENG-1182]. That sweep originally covered `2883029950` only — the second connected account was not swept until this check, which is itself part of the finding: a second billable account was easy to miss. It has now been swept and is clean.

This directly contradicts an already-shipped, deliberate product policy: the customer portal's `UsageMeter` component (`agentweb-customer-portal/src/components/layout/UsageMeter.tsx`) explicitly documents "The unit is never named to the customer; they see a percentage of 'monthly usage'" ([ENG-1116](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1116/flip-enforcement-from-tokens-to-cost-enforce-cost-cap-alone-is-a-no-op)/1509/1515), and `SubscriptionCard`/`TokenWarningModal` follow the same percentage-only convention ("You've reached your monthly usage limit", "{pct}% of your monthly allowance used"). The scheduled-chat notification path was never brought in line with that policy, so it leaks internal COGS/allowance numbers whenever a scheduled chat is blocked — reaching real paying customers by email, unprompted. ## Acceptance criteria (behavioral contract) 1. **No dollar figure ever appears** in the scheduled-chat cost/token-limit-blocked email (subject, HTML body, or text body) or in the in-app blocked-run message (`actualResponse`). Verify: search the rendered output for `$` — must not be present. 2. **No raw token count ever appears** in either surface (e.g. `1,050,000 / 1,000,000 tokens`). Same reasoning — the unit is never named to the customer, whichever dimension gated. 3. **The customer sees a percentage instead**, matching the existing in-app convention (e.g. "you've reached your monthly usage limit (106% used)."), computed from `usageStatus.costPercentUsed` when the cost cap is the trigger and `usageStatus.percentUsed` when the token cap is the trigger (selection logic unchanged — still `deriveBlockedByCost`). 4. **Neither the email nor the in-app message names which internal dimension ("cost" vs "token") gated** — both read as a generic "monthly usage limit," consistent with `UsageMeter`'s documented policy. (The `usageMode === 'paused'` message is already compliant and unchanged.) 5. Existing scheduled-chat notification tests (`emailService.scheduledChat.test.ts`, `agentModeController.scheduledChat.test.ts`) are updated to assert the new wording and explicitly assert the absence of `$` and raw counts — no other scheduled-chat test behavior changes. ## Not in scope The customer's own in-app usage dashboard (`UsageMeter`, `SubscriptionCard`, `TokenWarningModal`) already follows this policy correctly and is not touched. Ad-spend reporting (`agentModeService.ts` campaign/lead cost summaries) is a different domain — that's the customer's own Meta/Google spend, not internal LLM COGS — and is out of scope. ## Complexity ledger Net lines ~flat (message-construction rewrite, no new abstractions); removes two dimension-named branches per surface in favor of one shared percentage branch. Behavior-preserving except for the blocked-message copy itself (the fix).

ENG-1563 Ground quality.status in the AA Index benchmark instead of hardcoded "unknown"

## The gap `RecommendationQuality.status` (in `llmUsageDriversResolverService.ts`) is hardcoded to `"unknown"` for every model-switch recommendation, on the theory that no quality evidence exists. That's not true: `qualityScore` — sourced live from the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — already exists for every model and already powers the model picker's meters and the cost/quality "dominance" filter (see `agentModeService.sonnet45.test.ts`, `agentModeService.dominanceLegacy.test.ts`). We're discarding a real signal instead of labeling it honestly. [ENG-1217](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1217/usage-runway-v2-ux-runway-quest-visual-ranked-optimization-missions) AC5 requires: *"The UI never calls a cheaper model equivalent in quality unless task-specific evaluation evidence supports that claim. Unknown quality is labeled unknown."* That's a bar against implying **task-specific** parity — it does not require ignoring a general benchmark signal. Those are different bars; this issue closes that gap without weakening AC5. ## Direction Extend the type: ```ts interface RecommendationQuality { status: "unknown" | "benchmark_comparable" | "benchmark_lower" | "task_verified"; source: "none" | "artificial_analysis" | "task_eval"; reason: string; } ``` * `benchmark_comparable` **/** `benchmark_lower` (`source: "artificial_analysis"`) — derived from the existing AA `qualityScore` delta between `fromModel`/`toModel`. Copy names its source and explicitly disclaims task-specific verification, e.g. *"Generally rated similar on independent benchmarks — not yet tested on your specific work."* Never wording that could read as "tested on your work" or "equivalent quality." * `unknown` (`source: "none"`) — kept for the true no-data case: a model pair where AA hasn't scored one or both sides. Reuse [ENG-1532](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1532/quality-unknown-renders-on-every-row-with-identical-wording-so-it)/PR #1109's once-per-surface display pattern for this case. * `task_verified` (`source: "task_eval"`) — type slot reserved, **not populated by this issue**. See the linked follow-up. * **Never blend AA score and future task-eval results into one opaque number.** Each tier renders its own explicit provenance string, always. ## Why this shape (research, 2026-08-25) Surveyed how Cursor, v0, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, and dedicated LLM routers (Martian, Not Diamond, Unify, OpenRouter, RouteLLM) auto-select models: * No product uses a static third-party benchmark (Artificial Analysis, LMArena Elo) as a named routing input — we'd be first movers on this specific piece. * Nobody labels "benchmark-comparable" vs. "verified for your task" as a customer-facing distinction. Closest internal analog: Not Diamond ships a pretrained general router as day-one default, with a customer-specific trained router (`train_custom_router`) as an explicit later upgrade — that's the shape adopted here. * Unify is the one vendor that blends a benchmark-trained score with live measurements into a single number — the exact pattern this issue avoids, because it's the mechanism that would quietly recreate [ENG-1200](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1200/ui-bug-founder-account-defaulting-to-inferior-model-leading-to-drastic) (a confident-looking number nobody can trace to "was this tested for you"). * Cursor's own stated philosophy is that benchmarks predict production satisfaction poorly — reason to treat `benchmark_comparable` as a deliberate, temporary floor to unblock now, not a permanent resting state. ## Acceptance criteria (human-written) 1. `quality.status` is never `"unknown"` for a model pair where both models have an AA `qualityScore` — it resolves to `benchmark_comparable` or `benchmark_lower`. 2. Every `benchmark_*` status's copy names its source (independent/Artificial Analysis benchmark) and explicitly disclaims task-specific verification. 3. `unknown` still renders, via the existing once-per-surface pattern, for any model pair missing an AA score on either side. 4. No code path combines an AA-derived value and a task-eval-derived value into a single numeric or status field. 5. `task_verified` / `source: "task_eval"` exist in the type but nothing in this PR sets them. ## Related * [ENG-1532](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1532/quality-unknown-renders-on-every-row-with-identical-wording-so-it) — the display-frequency fix this issue builds on (shipped, PR #1109). * [ENG-1217](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1217/usage-runway-v2-ux-runway-quest-visual-ranked-optimization-missions) — the AC5 requirement this field satisfies. * [ENG-1200](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1200/ui-bug-founder-account-defaulting-to-inferior-model-leading-to-drastic) — the incident that made task-specific evidence the bar in the first place. * Follow-up (separate issue): populate `task_verified` from an Okareo eval harness, gated on canary/progressive rollout before promotion — not this issue's scope.

<details>
<summary>Full details: Security And Access Control Integrity</summary>

**Explanation**

The new `set-daily-invite-cap` action introduces an owner-level configuration write without an enforceable approval or role boundary. `resolveLinkedInAccountForWrite` accepts any org member for an account with `sharedWithOrg=true` (linkedInDailyVolumeGate.ts:61-72), and `setDailyInviteCap` then writes `daily_invite_cap` to the actual owner record (linkedInDailyVolumeGate.ts:194-207). A shared member can therefore raise another user's safety ceiling to 30 or set it to 0, affecting all users of that account. The action only has prompt instructions to ask about Premium and not run unattended (agentModeService.ts:33062-33075); `linkedinOutreach` does not verify a live user confirmation, owner/admin role, or schedule state. Scheduled execution reaches the same `executePreparedAgentTool` path with only user/session identifiers, while the repository's default `AGENT_TOOL_GATEWAY_ENFORCE=false` leaves the generic confirmation recommendation in observe mode. The setter also emits no audit record containing actor, previous cap, new cap, or approval; the generic action log does not provide that trail. This is not a production outage path, but it is a customer-impacting excessive-privilege and approval-control gap.

**Resolution**

Restrict `set-daily-invite-cap` to the account owner or an explicitly authorized org role such as `org:accounts:manage`; do not treat ordinary `sharedWithOrg` usage permission as configuration-write permission. ENG-1580 Google Drive Knowledge Base has no bridge to ad-creative upload — Emma cannot use client Drive assets (images/video) in Meta campaigns

## Urgent — blocking a live customer campaign launch **Source:** Phoenix Technologies (Vince Magaline / David), `#phoenix-agentweb`, 2026-08-25. Vince wants to launch a **new** Meta campaign using ad creatives (images/video — "insurance group ads," "Aug 25 Winning Angle Ads") that David put in Google Drive folders and connected via the Knowledge Base "Add Folder" flow. Even once [ENG-1577]() (Shared-Drive `supportsAllDrives` bug) ships and the folders successfully connect, **Emma still cannot actually use the files inside them as ad creative.** The Knowledge Base connector was built for text/document reference material, not binary creative-asset ingestion, and nothing bridges the gap. This is a real, load-bearing capability hole, not a bug in the folder-connect flow — customers will hit this the moment they try to do exactly what onboarding docs imply is supported ("share your ad creative folder with Emma"). ## What I verified in the code (backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts, origin/main@68425770f) `readGoogleDriveSharedFile` → `readGoogleDriveFileContent` (~line 22151-22206) is the function Emma's `read_knowledge_base_files` tool calls for a `gdrive:` KB identifier. Its content-type handling: * PDF → `pdf-parse` → text * XLSX/XLS → `xlsx` → CSV text * DOCX/DOC → `mammoth` → text * txt/md/html/csv/json/xml/log or `text/*` or `application/vnd.google-apps.*` → UTF-8 text * **Everything else (this is every image and video mimetype: PNG, JPG, MP4, MOV, etc.) →** `content.toString('base64')` That base64 string becomes the `content` field of a JSON tool result handed back to the model. Two concrete failure modes on top of "this isn't a real integration": 1. **No consumer exists.** I grepped every Meta ad-creative tool definition (`backend/src/emma/tools.ts`, AD_CREATIVE CREATE / UPLOAD_IMAGE / UPLOAD_VIDEO, ~line 1000-1160). They accept `image_url` (a fetchable URL), `image_hash` (from a prior `UPLOAD_IMAGE` call), or `video_id` (from `UPLOAD_VIDEO`). Nothing in the codebase takes a `gdrive:`-sourced base64 blob and produces any of those three. There is no "materialize this KB file as a real asset" tool. `list_knowledge_base_files`'s own tool description says outright: *"the Google Drive entries here are READ-ONLY shared folders — CREATING or EDITING Google Docs/Sheets is a SEPARATE capability."* It was never scoped for this. 2. **Even if something did consume it, real files would come back corrupted.** `readSingleKnowledgeBaseFile` / `readGoogleDriveFileContent` cap combined content at `maxContentLength = 1_000_000` characters and silently truncate past that (`'\n\n[Content truncated due to size limit]'`). Base64 inflates size ~33%; any real ad image above roughly ~750KB raw, and essentially any video file, gets cut mid-stream. Truncated base64 does not decode — it's not "a smaller image," it's garbage bytes. It's a systemic gap in the asset-ingestion story, not a one-off. ## Proposed direction (not yet decided — needs a real design pass, flagging the shape for context) The existing, working pattern is: creative → lands as bytes on AgentWeb's own S3 → gets a URL → that URL goes into `image_url`/is uploaded via `UPLOAD_IMAGE` to get an `image_hash`. Given a `gdrive:` KB identifier + file name (or a raw Drive file ID) pointing at an image/video mimetype, downloads the raw bytes via the existing service-account Drive client (`getGoogleDriveClient()` / the binary-download branch already in `readGoogleDriveFileContent`, i.e. `drive.files.get({fileId, alt:'media', supportsAllDrives:true})` — already fixed by [ENG-1577](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1577/phoenix-google-drive-folder-connection-returns-folder-not-found-after)). 2. Re-uploads those bytes to AgentWeb's own S3 (mirroring however Emma's self-generated creatives already get hosted there), skipping the text-extraction/truncation path entirely for binary mimetypes. 3. Returns a real `image_url` (or feeds `UPLOAD_IMAGE`/`UPLOAD_VIDEO` directly) that the existing `AD_CREATIVE CREATE` tool can consume unmodified. 4. Exposed as a new tool (or an explicit mode on an existing one) so Emma has something to actually call, since today there is nothing. Alternatives worth weighing before committing: whether this should be a generic "materialize any KB file as a hosted asset" tool (reusable beyond ads — landing page images, blog assets, etc.) vs. a narrower "Drive → ad creative" specific tool. Recommend the generic version given the existing S3-hosting pattern is already shared infrastructure. ## Acceptance criteria (draft — needs review) 1. Given a `gdrive:` KB-connected folder containing an image file, Emma has a tool call that produces a usable `image_url` (or `image_hash` via `UPLOAD_IMAGE`) for that file — verified by successfully calling `AD_CREATIVE CREATE` with the result and confirming Meta accepts it. 2. Given a video file in the same folder, the equivalent works via `UPLOAD_VIDEO` → `video_id` (+ required thumbnail). 3. A file whose size would previously have silently truncated (>1MB) instead transfers in full — binary files must not go through the text `maxContentLength` truncation path at all. 4. Text/document files in the same folder are unaffected — this doesn't regress the existing (working) text-based KB read path. 5. Found auditing the production session evidence attached to [ENG-426](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-426/cap-repeated-tool-calls-per-response-in-agentmode-search-web-runaway) (session `e6c9e693-ff33-4883-a18a-9d674b4074c4`, 2026-08-25): after a targeted turn hit the time limit, the user asked in chat to "reassess using a new model." The next generate call still resolved `gemini-3.7-flash` — the same model already in use — and the session resumed stale earlier research context instead of answering the repeated question or actually switching models. ## The bug Model resolution in `agentModeController.ts` reads strictly from the client-supplied `llmModel` request-body field (e.g. line ~6898: `const { ..., llmModel: requestedLlmModel } = req.body`), which is only populated by the customer portal's model picker/API param. Confirmed via `git grep -n "requestedModel\s*=" origin/main` (agentweb): there is exactly one input to model resolution, and no code path anywhere in the generate/message pipeline parses the user's chat message text for an intent to switch/reassess models and updates `requestedModel` accordingly. A prose instruction like "reassess using a new model" is therefore inert by construction — it reaches the model as ordinary conversation content, gets no special handling, and the next turn silently keeps running on whatever model was already selected. The user gets no acknowledgement that nothing changed. **Distinct from** [ENG-1205](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1205/optimized-mode-model-correction-is-invisible-in-chat-and-an-in-chat): that ticket covers a model request that IS captured (via the picker) but rejected by optimized-mode policy, silently dropped. Here, no request is ever captured in the first place — there is no in-chat mechanism to request a model change at all. ## Production evidence * Session `e6c9e693-ff33-4883-a18a-9d674b4074c4` (2026-08-25) — same session audited on [ENG-426](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-426/cap-repeated-tool-calls-per-response-in-agentmode-search-web-runaway) (193 web searches, 73 file reads, 503 messages, $8.68 recorded cost over ~4h). * Latest recorded policy decision: `gemini-3.7-flash`, unchanged before and after the user's in-chat request to reassess with a new model. ## Recommendation (reversible, minimal — pre-approved fast path per taste-calibration.md) Close the silent-no-op only: detect that a turn's response is unchanged-model after language resembling a model-change/reassess request, and have Emma say so explicitly instead of continuing silently — same "silence is not acceptable" principle already established as precedent in [ENG-1205](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1205/optimized-mode-model-correction-is-invisible-in-chat-and-an-in-chat) AC3. Do NOT build actual in-chat natural-language model switching as part of this fix — that's a materially larger feature (parsing intent, wiring to the picker/session state, UX for confirmation) and should be a separate, explicitly scoped decision if ever prioritized. ## Acceptance criteria (draft — needs confirmation before a swarm PR locks tests, per loop-acceptance-tests.md) 1. When a user's in-chat message reads as a request to change/reassess with a different model, and the following turn runs on the same model as before, the response explicitly acknowledges that the model didn't change and why (mirrors [ENG-1205](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1205/optimized-mode-model-correction-is-invisible-in-chat-and-an-in-chat) AC3 style) — it never silently continues as if the request was actioned. 2. Regression test: a synthetic transcript containing an explicit "use a different/new model" instruction asserts the acknowledgement from (1) fires; a transcript with no such instruction asserts it does not (no false positives). **Explanation**

The new domain-claim flow still permits cross-account ownership and disclosure of Resend DNS verification records. After `emailDomains[]` is written, `confirmEmailDomainClaim()` failures are caught and ignored in `crm.ts`; the claim remains unconfirmed. `claimEmailDomain()` allows takeover of an unconfirmed claim after 10 minutes. A second account can then pass an eventually consistent `getUsersByEmailDomain()` scan, claim the domain, call Resend `getDomain()`, and receive the domain's DNS record `value` fields through `GET /email-domains`. The new delete route has a similar race because it releases the claim before its conditional user-record removal. If removal fails, the old account record remains while another account can claim the released domain. These paths are introduced by the PR and match the check's weak tenant isolation and cross-account data leakage conditions. This is not a production outage path; it is a privacy and ownership-integrity failure under persistence or concurrency failures.

**Resolution**

Make domain ownership changes atomic or use a durable fencing/reconciliation protocol. Do not allow an unconfirmed claim to expire when the user's domain record has already been persisted. If confirmation fails, fail the operation and retain or reconcile the claim before returning success. For deletion, atomically remove the user's domain record and release the claim, or reacquire/retain the claim whenever removal fails. Before attaching an existing Resend domain, verify the authoritative application ownership claim and prevent any account from receiving another account's DNS verification records.

A transient failure after the three confirmation attempts therefore leaves a persisted domain with an unconfirmed claim. Another account can later take the claim while the first account still owns the persisted record. This is a production cross-account ownership and sending-access integrity failure, not a production-outage path. **Resolution**

Do not swallow claim-confirmation failures. Make domain persistence and claim confirmation atomic, or use a lease/fencing and reconciliation design that cannot expire a claim while its domain record remains persisted. If confirmation fails, return failure and conditionally remove the just-written domain record and release only the current owner's claim; do not report successful registration. Add a negative test that forces confirmation failure and verifies that a second user cannot claim the domain while the first record remains. Obtain and record Harsha's explicit pre-merge approval for the data-plane changes before merge, with rollback and post-deploy verification evidence.

<summary>Full details: Security And Access Control Integrity</summary>

**Explanation**

The new accepted-invitation CRM path weakens attribution integrity. In `agentModeService.ts:32940-32969`, the handler accepts invitation A, then trusts independently supplied `profile_url`/`provider_id` and name/company/title values when writing `linkedin.invite.accepted` to CRM. It never proves that the supplied profile is the sender for `invitation_id`. A caller with valid access to its CRM list can therefore accept one invitation while marking another person contacted and attaching the accepted-event audit record to that person. The `canDestructiveCrmList` check prevents cross-tenant list writes, but it does not prevent wrong-person writes. The changed tests cover list access and provider resolution, but no mismatched-invitation identity case. This is a customer-impacting data-plane attribution failure, not a production outage.

**Resolution**

Bind the CRM identity to the accepted invitation on the server. Before mirroring, resolve `invitation_id` for the selected `account_id` from the received-invitation data and derive the sender's canonical provider/public identifier. Compare any caller-supplied `profile_url` or `provider_id` with that identifier; if the identity cannot be proven, skip the CRM mirror while preserving the successful LinkedIn acceptance. Prefer authoritative profile fields over LLM-supplied name/company/title values. Reject or ignore simultaneous `profile_url` and `provider_id` values for this action. Add negative tests for a mismatched profile, mismatched provider, and unresolvable invitation. Retain the existing `canDestructiveCrmList` guard. Because this PR adds CRM lead and engagement writes, obtain the explicit Harsha pre-merge approval required by `AGENTS.md` for data-plane changes.

<summary>Full details: Performance And Algorithmic Complexity</summary>

**Explanation**

New `accept-invitation` handling can enumerate an unbounded number of CRM lists in the live request path. When `args.list_id` is omitted, the new code calls `resolveListIdForAccount` (`agentModeService.ts:32950-32952`). That resolver calls `getLeadListsByUserId`, which paginates through every page and appends every full list item to an in-memory array (`db.ts:5164-5196`); its fallback scans the entire table (`db.ts:5199-5222`). The resolver then filters the full result. This can consume unbounded reads and memory and delay the accepted-invitation response. The helper existed before the PR, but the new accept path activates this behavior. The other new loops have explicit bounds, so no additional O(n²) or N+1 issue is established. This is a production request-path resource-exhaustion risk for users with many lists.

**Resolution**

Use a bounded account-to-list lookup instead of loading all user lists. Add a DynamoDB index or binding record keyed by the user and LinkedIn account, and query only the required binding metadata. If a scan fallback remains, enforce a hard page/item budget, use a projection for `listId` and `linkedInAccountId`, and return a best-effort no-op when the budget or a request timeout is reached. @coderabbitai All three findings from this review are addressed in **6b72ad84b**. Detail below, including the two pre-merge check warnings, which were the most valuable part of this review.

---

### 1. Cross-account read — Sensitive Data Protection / Security And Access Control (⚠️ both)

**Correct, and it was a regression this PR introduced.** Verified against the code rather than taken on trust.

Listing through `new AdAccount('act_X')` was implicitly account-scoped — Meta could only ever return X's ads. Reading through `new Campaign(id)` / `new AdSet(id)` is not: a node id addresses a node globally, and one Meta OAuth token routinely reaches several ad accounts. So a caller could select account A, pass a node id from account B, and receive B's ads labelled as A's.

The observation that `AD_CREATIVE GET` already documents and blocks this case is accurate — that guard exists at `agentModeService.ts` (ENG-471) with the same reasoning, and the new list paths bypassed it entirely.

`metaService.assertNodeInAccount` now reads the node's `account_id` and compares it against the selected account *before* anything is listed through it, on both `listAds` and `listAdCreatives` including the ad-set-precedence path. It fails closed on every uncertain branch:

- unknown/absent node owner → refuse
- empty selected account → refuse (an empty value compares equal to nothing, so treating it as "no mismatch" would pass every node the token can reach)
- owner ≠ selected → refuse, naming both

`act_` prefixes are normalised on both sides.

Negative tests added as requested: foreign campaign, foreign ad set, owner-less node, empty selected account, and prefix normalisation — each asserting the payload edge is **never called**, so no foreign data is fetched let alone returned. Plus a test that an unscoped account-wide read spends no ownership call.

### 2. Unenforced page bound — Performance And Algorithmic Complexity (⚠️)

Fixed; see the inline thread. `maxPages` is now normalised and clamped inside `drainCursor` before it is used as a bound.

The transport-timeout half of that resolution is deliberately **not** done here: configuring an abortable timeout on the SDK's HTTP layer is global to every Meta call in the service, a materially larger blast radius than this PR. The unbounded-walk risk is closed by the clamp.

### 3. `campaign_id` silently ignored on AD_CREATIVE LIST (nitpick)

Agreed, and worth more than a nitpick — it is this PR's own thesis pointed back at it. Meta exposes no campaign→adcreatives edge, so the scope genuinely cannot be honoured, but returning an account-wide list labelled "(complete list)" while quietly discarding the requested scope is the same silent-scope-drop defect in a different place.

The response now carries `scopeIgnored` and states plainly that `campaign_id` was **NOT** applied, that the list is not limited to that campaign, and that `AD LIST` with `campaign_id` is the supported route. Three tests cover it, including that the note stays absent when no unsupported scope was supplied.

---

**"Bounded by pages, but not by time" is a fair characterisation and I've taken it.** `drainCursor` awaits each page sequentially, so a bounded page count still compounds into an unbounded wait — and since the previous code issued a single request, that tail is one this PR introduced. **On the transport-timeout half, still declining, with the reason stated rather than buried.** Applying an abort signal to `node.get`, the initial list call and every `cursor.next()` means configuring the SDK's *shared* HTTP layer — `FacebookAdsApi.init()` returns a process-wide default API object, so a deadline set there silently changes every Meta call in this service, including writes and the launch gate. That is a materially larger blast radius than the risk it addresses, on a PR whose whole subject is a read path.

The honest limit of what I did ship is documented in the test rather than glossed: **the deadline gates whether a NEW page is STARTED, not whether an in-flight one is aborted**, so a single slow call can overshoot the budget by its own duration. A single hung request was already possible before this change and is not a regression introduced here — what this PR added was the *compounding*, and that is what is now bounded.

If a per-call Graph deadline is wanted, it deserves its own row: it touches every Meta caller and needs its own regression pass over writes, the tracking gate and CAPI.

**A per-call transport abort via `AbortController`.** Verified in the vendored SDK rather than assumed: `FacebookAdsApi.init()` installs a process-wide default through `setDefaultApi`, and `Http.request`/`requestPromise` are statics that construct their axios options internally with no timeout, options object or signal parameter. The only way to reach the transport is patching that shared static, which would put a client-side deadline on every **write** as well.

That is the dangerous half. A timed-out write may have SUCCEEDED on Meta's side while we report failure — a retry then double-creates a campaign, or we tell a customer an ad is still running immediately after pausing it. That is this PR's own failure class (confidently reporting something untrue) moved onto live ad spend.

`Promise.race` bounds how long *we* wait, not how long the socket stays open — stated plainly in the code comment rather than implied. For a read that is sufficient: nothing is left half-applied and the user-visible hang is gone. A genuine per-call Graph deadline deserves its own row, with its own regression pass over writes, the tracking gate and CAPI.

**Explanation**

A run with many steps therefore performs Θ(n²) scan work per transition in the worst case, and Θ(n³) across all transitions. `checkpoints` grows with the definition, and no workflow-size or run-size limit exists. Index checkpoints by step ID once per transition, or maintain a checkpoint map and the next-step index in `WorkflowRunState`. Use constant-time lookups for `findNextStep()` and completion checks. Atomically claim the source question before allowing CAMPAIGN CREATE, using a DynamoDB conditional update or transaction keyed by `sourceQuestionId` and the session version. Preserve the source question ID, account ID, answerer, timestamp, and objective in the audit record, and add tests for cross-account bare/no-kind cards and concurrent reuse.

ENG-1643 One consent doctrine: an unambiguous typed affirmative resolves an approval-shaped card

Slice 3 of [ENG-1635](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1635/meta-write-confirmation-gate-ignores-prior-structured-approval-12). Today the product carries two contradictory consent doctrines: typing past an open card **abandons** it (`agentModeController.ts:7314-7343` clears + re-ask directive; `emma/tools.ts:138` "only an explicit click counts") while the write gate's own prompt says *Reply "yes" / "confirm"* (`agentModeService.ts:19371`). The model conflates them — Vince's typed "Yes, looks good" on the deployment brief was rejected for a card click (session 822c1ed4, 08-27 17:16:46Z), and the model invented "billable account" doctrine that exists nowhere in the repo. **Design (Claude Code answer routing: typed and clicked answers resolve the same way when unambiguous):** in the typed-past-a-card path, before clearing: * If the typed message **unambiguously binds to exactly one option** (label/keyword binding, `verifyExplicitStatement`-style — the same mechanism Path 1 of the objective gate already uses at `agentModeService.ts:19134-19154`), resolve the card with that option (`answeredBy: 'user'`, provenance noting typed-text resolution). * A bare affirmative ("yes", "approved", "looks good") resolves ONLY an approval-shaped card (a card with exactly one clearly-affirmative option, e.g. Approve/Reject); on a multi-choice card (Leads/Sales/Traffic/Awareness) a bare affirmative still clears + re-asks — never auto-picks. * `immutable`, delegation, and one-live-question invariants unchanged (`askUserQuestion.ts` primitives). ## Acceptance criteria 1. Approval-shaped card + typed "yes, looks good" / "approved" → card resolves to the approve option; no re-ask; answer attribution records typed resolution. 2. Multi-choice card + bare "yes" → today's behavior (cleared + re-ask directive); never auto-resolved. 3. Multi-choice card + typed text that keyword-binds to exactly one option ("leads") → resolves that option; ambiguous text → re-ask. 4. `applyAnswer` invariants (no re-answer, delegated=recommended, no 'model' answerer) hold — extend `askUserQuestion.test.ts`.

<summary>Full details: Security And Access Control Integrity</summary>

**Explanation**

The PR introduces a monitoring gap for a customer-impacting scheduled operation. The new dedicated alert is started with `void sendAgentModeOncallAlert(...).catch(...)` at `agentModeController.ts:5359-5379`, but the pre-existing generic validation-failure alert is unconditionally skipped when `linkedInInviteSendRequirementMissed` is true at `agentModeController.ts:5661`. The alert helper can reject when `emailService.sendOncallAlert` fails and only logs/releases its dedupe reservation. Therefore, a blocked LinkedIn run can file its issue but produce no oncall alert. The changed code reduces monitoring on that production failure path. No database approval-gate or audit-storage change was introduced.

**Resolution**

Keep the generic alert as a fallback. Await or retain the dedicated alert promise, and suppress the generic alert only when the dedicated alert reports successful delivery or a verified prior delivery through deduplication. If the dedicated alert rejects, log the failure and send the generic alert. Add a test that rejects the dedicated alert and verifies that the generic oncall alert is sent.

<details>
<summary>Full details: Performance And Algorithmic Complexity</summary>

**Explanation**

The new per-account dedupe key activates a quadratic path in the oncall alert helper. `sendAgentModeOncallAlert` performs synchronous dedupe work before its first `await`; after the global map exceeds 1,000 keys, every new `linkedin_invite_blocked:<accountId>` alert scans the entire map. If N distinct accounts are blocked within 24 hours, active entries are not removed and the cumulative work is O(N²). The map can also grow with the number of distinct accounts in the window. This runs from the scheduled-run path, even though the promise is discarded with `void`.

**Resolution**

Change alert dedupe cleanup to an amortized bounded structure, such as an expiry queue or min-heap with incremental cleanup, and enforce a maximum number of retained dedupe keys with a documented eviction policy. Do not scan the full map on every alert. Preserve the 24-hour suppression behavior for active keys.

ENG-1183 Staging deploy budget still assumes Rolling; Immutable rollouts time out CI on deploys that succeeded

Staging CI times out on deploys that actually succeeded, because the deploy budget is still calibrated for the pre-Immutable policy. ## What happens `Backend deploy to staging` fails with: ``` EB_DEPLOY_FAILED: ... did not come up Ready on version '...' within the overall deploy budget of 1800s. Last observed Status=Updating Health=Green ``` `Health=Green`. Nothing is wrong. The rollout just isn't finished. First occurrence: run 31680773689 (PR #2380), 2026-08-13 08:28-08:58 UTC. EB logged `Deployment succeeded. Terminating old instances` at **08:46:19** — 12 minutes before CI gave up. The code was live. The red X is a false negative. ## Why now ENG-1128 set staging to Immutable on 2026-08-11 18:48:32 UTC. That worked — **zero abort events on staging since the switch**, both the `/var/app/staging/` race and the wedge mode are gone. But Immutable is slower by construction, and nothing re-tuned CI: | policy | shape | duration | | -- | -- | -- | | Rolling (before) | deploy in place onto the 2 existing instances | 3-5 min | | Immutable (now) | launch a parallel fleet, health-check, swap, drain the old fleet | 8-40 min | The 1800s budget dates from the Rolling era, when 30 minutes was enormous headroom. Most of the Immutable tail is the **graceful drain**, which is deliberate: `asgLifecycleGuard.ts` (ENG-657 / ENG-764) parks each dying instance in `Terminating:Wait` for up to `DRAIN_CEILING_MS` (10 min) so in-flight scheduled runs finish. That must not be shortened. ## Fix — two parts **Part 1 (immediate, unblocks CI).** In `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, raise the pair together: * `timeout-minutes: 35` -> `50` * `EB_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: '1800'` -> `'2700'` * `EB_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` -> `'1200'` (the "wait out a pre-existing update" cap is still 600s; a busy Immutable environment now stays busy for 40 min, so this will start failing deploys for the other reason) The step timeout must stay above the script budget — otherwise the runner SIGKILLs the script mid-poll and we lose the diagnostic line for a bare "step timed out". **Part 2 (the real fix).** In `.github/scripts/eb-deploy.sh`, stop blocking on the drain. The script waits for `Status=Ready` on the target version, and EB withholds that until the last old instance is reaped. But the drain is *old instances finishing old work* — our version is already serving at `Deployment succeeded`. Treating that event plus the new fleet on the target version as success lands deploys in ~10-15 min and leaves the drain running untouched behind us. Tradeoff, stated plainly: during teardown the fleet is mixed (new instances on the new version, old ones draining on the old one). The script's purpose (ENG-743) is proving the environment took the version, and this slightly weakens that claim. Right call for staging; **do not do this for prod.** `eb-deploy.test.sh` has 72 checks and gets extended with Part 2. ## Not needed No AWS-side change. This is entirely repo-side. ## Evidence * Deploy step over 36h: 22 success, 1 failure. * Today's 28 red runs: 26 `Require Greptile Review` (gate working as designed, 4/5 vs required 5/5), 3 backend tests, **1** deploy. * Immutable rollout durations on staging: 8m45s, 8m52s, 16m55s, 18m15s, 19m39s, 27m28s, and the 08:28 one still `Updating` 40 min in. * The 08:28 outlier started 2 min after the previous rollout completed, while its instances were still draining: the environment hit **7 instances in a 2-instance environment**, ELB went `Degraded -> Severe`.

Closing as superseded by #2673.

This PR re-tuned three numbers on the `Backend deploy to staging` job in `tests.yml`. **ENG-1463 deleted that job.** `main`'s `tests.yml` now has seven jobs — `detect-changes`, `backend-build`, `partner-build`, `ci-scripts-tests`, `relay-build`, `remotion-build`, `eb-config-conflict` — and none of them deploy. That is also why this PR went `CONFLICTING`: there is nothing left to apply it to.

The *reasoning* held up, though, and #2673 carries it forward. Specifically this paragraph:

> `EB_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` waits out a pre-existing update. It is still at the 600s default, which assumed an environment frees up in 3-5 min. A busy Immutable environment stays busy for 40, so that cap would have started failing deploys for the other reason. Hasn't bitten yet; it would have.

That was right, and it was never staging-specific. `backend/.ebextensions/rolling.config` has set `DeploymentPolicy: Immutable` on **production** since 2026-07-01, and no workflow has ever set `EB_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, so production still runs on the 600s default today. #2673 sizes it there, with the floor and ceiling asserted in `eb-deploy.test.sh` rather than argued in a comment.

The other two numbers this PR moved are already on production and need no change: `EB_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: '2700'` and `timeout-minutes: 50`, set by Harsha in ad4fbfed6 (ENG-734).

Closing as superseded by #2673, and — unlike #2390 — not because the idea was wrong.

**Why it can't be rebased.** The early exit is gated on `EB_READY_ON_DEPLOYMENT_SUCCEEDED`, which this PR sets on exactly one job: `Backend deploy to staging` in `tests.yml`. ENG-1463 deleted that job. Merging as-is would put ~250 lines into `eb-deploy.sh` — the production deploy path — behind a flag that nothing on `main` can ever set. That is dead code in the one script whose false-success and non-convergence modes have already cost ~17h (ENG-865) and ~29h (ENG-836) of production downtime.

**Why not just enable it for production instead.** Two reasons, and the first is this PR's own:

> **Off by default.** `EB_READY_ON_DEPLOYMENT_SUCCEEDED` is unset in the script and set only on the staging job. `deploy.yml` does not set it, so **both production deploys keep demanding the full `Status=Ready`.**

That was the safety argument the design rested on. Turning it on for production removes it, and nothing new justifies that. Under ENG-1463 the case got *weaker*, not stronger: GitHub Actions now proves buildability only, so the production deploy is the check that proves the runtime path. Shortening its verification is a change to the last real gate.

Second, the data doesn't ask for it. I measured the last 24 consecutive production backend deploys:

| median EB step | ~535s |
| max | 1352s (22m32s) |
| budget | 2700s |

~2x headroom, nothing red. **Explanation**

The PR adds a bearer-like HMAC removal token to the full tool result (`agentModeService.ts:35622-35653`). `extractToolContent` JSON-serializes that full result for the model, and the controller persists the tool message. Public interactive-share requests then reload the raw session history and pass it to the model while running as the session owner (`generateSharedResponse` calls `generateSessionResponse(..., session.userId, ..., true)`). Therefore an anonymous holder of an interactive-share link can place prompts in a model context that contains the owner's Google Ads removal capability. The client transcript filter hides tool messages from direct display, but it does not remove the token from persisted history or shared-turn model context. The token also has no user/session binding, expiry, or single-use state. This is newly introduced credential exposure through a public interface and does not require exposing the JWT secret.

**Resolution**

Do not place the removal capability in persisted or public-share model history. Disable Google Ads and other side-effecting tools for anonymous interactive-share turns, or require an authenticated owner confirmation path before any such tool is available. Store approval state server-side and bind it to the owner user ID, session ID, customer ID, action, and resource; use a short-lived, single-use capability. Redact the capability from tool messages, session APIs, shared transcripts, logs, and telemetry. Add a test that an interactive-share request cannot receive or replay a conversion-action removal capability.

<summary>Full details: Security And Access Control Integrity</summary>

**Explanation**

Scheduled runs always enable `completionGate` (`agentModeController.ts:5220`). The requirement matcher treats an exact non-publish tool call as satisfied without checking its result (`requiredCallSatisfaction.ts:241-274`), and `call_google_ads_api` is not a publish tool (`hardeningGaps.ts:57-59`). The confirmation text matches the scheduled continuation detector, which then sends “Do NOT wait for confirmation” and starts another model turn (`agentModeController.ts:2606-2677, 3454-3478`). The first tool result includes the token in the tool message and persists it, so the next model turn can replay the token and remove the conversion action without owner approval. The new halt is also classified as `agent_tool_succeeded` instead of a failure, which weakens the existing tool-reliability monitoring signal (`agentModeService.ts:501-520`, `agentToolGatewayService.ts:929-980`).

**Resolution**

Keep irreversible conversion-action approval separate from the scheduled best-effort completion gate. When a scheduled run receives this structured approval halt, park the run and notify the account owner. Do not auto-continue it, including when the generic confirmation detector matches. Resume only after an authenticated owner approval. Bind the approval to the owner/session, add expiry and single-use consumption, and record distinct approval-required and removal-executed audit events. ENG-1183 Staging deploy budget still assumes Rolling; Immutable rollouts time out CI on deploys that succeeded

Staging CI times out on deploys that actually succeeded, because the deploy budget is still calibrated for the pre-Immutable policy. ## What happens `Backend deploy to staging` fails with: ``` EB_DEPLOY_FAILED: ... did not come up Ready on version '...' within the overall deploy budget of 1800s. EB logged `Deployment succeeded. Terminating old instances` at **08:46:19** — 12 minutes before CI gave up. The code was live. The red X is a false negative. ## Why now ENG-1128 set staging to Immutable on 2026-08-11 18:48:32 UTC. That worked — **zero abort events on staging since the switch**, both the `/var/app/staging/` race and the wedge mode are gone. But Immutable is slower by construction, and nothing re-tuned CI: | policy | shape | duration | | -- | -- | -- | | Rolling (before) | deploy in place onto the 2 existing instances | 3-5 min | | Immutable (now) | launch a parallel fleet, health-check, swap, drain the old fleet | 8-40 min | The 1800s budget dates from the Rolling era, when 30 minutes was enormous headroom. Most of the Immutable tail is the **graceful drain**, which is deliberate: `asgLifecycleGuard.ts` (ENG-657 / ENG-764) parks each dying instance in `Terminating:Wait` for up to `DRAIN_CEILING_MS` (10 min) so in-flight scheduled runs finish. That must not be shortened. ## Fix — two parts **Part 1 (immediate, unblocks CI).** In `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, raise the pair together: * `timeout-minutes: 35` -> `50` * `EB_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: '1800'` -> `'2700'` * `EB_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` -> `'1200'` (the "wait out a pre-existing update" cap is still 600s; a busy Immutable environment now stays busy for 40 min, so this will start failing deploys for the other reason) The step timeout must stay above the script budget — otherwise the runner SIGKILLs the script mid-poll and we lose the diagnostic line for a bare "step timed out". **Part 2 (the real fix).** In `.github/scripts/eb-deploy.sh`, stop blocking on the drain. The script waits for `Status=Ready` on the target version, and EB withholds that until the last old instance is reaped. But the drain is *old instances finishing old work* — our version is already serving at `Deployment succeeded`. Treating that event plus the new fleet on the target version as success lands deploys in ~10-15 min and leaves the drain running untouched behind us. Tradeoff, stated plainly: during teardown the fleet is mixed (new instances on the new version, old ones draining on the old one). The script's purpose (ENG-743) is proving the environment took the version, and this slightly weakens that claim. Right call for staging; **do not do this for prod.** `eb-deploy.test.sh` has 72 checks and gets extended with Part 2. ## Not needed No AWS-side change. This is entirely repo-side. ## Evidence * Deploy step over 36h: 22 success, 1 failure. * Today's 28 red runs: 26 `Require Greptile Review` (gate working as designed, 4/5 vs required 5/5), 3 backend tests, **1** deploy. * Immutable rollout durations on staging: 8m45s, 8m52s, 16m55s, 18m15s, 19m39s, 27m28s, and the 08:28 one still `Updating` 40 min in. * The 08:28 outlier started 2 min after the previous rollout completed, while its instances were still draining: the environment hit **7 instances in a 2-instance environment**, ELB went `Degraded -> Severe`.

ENG-1184 Termination lifecycle hook is missing from .ebextensions, so the graceful drain only exists on the deploy path

`backend/src/services/asgLifecycleGuard.ts` documents its hook name as: > Fixed hook name, mirrored in `.ebextensions/07-termination-lifecycle.config`. **That file does not exist on** `main`**.** `backend/.ebextensions/` contains only `03-root-volume`, `04-disk-alarm`, `05-instance-recycling`, `06-log-retention`, `chromium`, `rolling`, `timeout`. ## Why it matters The `agentweb-drain-before-terminate` termination hook therefore exists only because `.github/scripts/eb-deploy.sh` reinstalls it on every deploy: ``` aws autoscaling put-lifecycle-hook \ --lifecycle-hook-name agentweb-drain-before-terminate \ --lifecycle-transition autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING \ --heartbeat-timeout 900 --default-result CONTINUE ``` Any termination path that does not run that script has **no hook at all**, so the ASG terminates instances on its own schedule and the graceful drain never gets its window. That is exactly the ENG-657 / ENG-764 failure — an in-flight scheduled run killed mid-execution and left for the ENG-324 reconciler to requeue ~20 min later. Reachable via: * a deploy from the EB console * an EB rollback to a previous application version * **ASG replacing an unhealthy instance** (no deploy involved at all — this one needs nothing unusual to happen) * a new environment created from saved config The guard is fail-safe when the hook is missing (it still drains, just without the ASG waiting for it), so this is a silent degradation, not a crash. It reduces the drain from "guaranteed" to "only if the last mutation happened to be one of our deploys." ## Fix Add `backend/.ebextensions/07-termination-lifecycle.config` declaring the hook, matching the name pinned in `TERMINATION_LIFECYCLE_HOOK_NAME`, so it is part of environment configuration rather than a side effect of one deploy path. Keep the `eb-deploy.sh` call as the idempotent belt-and-braces. Worth confirming while doing it whether `.ebextensions` can express an ASG lifecycle hook directly (`Resources:` block against `AWSEBAutoScalingGroup`) — if not, the alternative is a `.platform/hooks/predeploy` script, but the config route keeps it declarative. Found while investigating the staging deploy timeouts. Rated above that one: this is a correctness hole in run durability, not a CI annoyance.

Before this PR, the same malformed call failed at `JSON.parse` and did not reach the tool. This is on the production tool-dispatch path and can cause unauthorized customer-impacting image edits. The added `additionalProperties: false` protections do not cover `generate_image` or other approval-sensitive tools.

Do not execute repaired arguments that add or alter approval/control fields. Prefer rejecting repaired calls for side-effecting or approval-gated tools. Its repeated `(?:(?!👉?\s*next\s*steps?...)[\s\S])*` scans a long whitespace run once per character because the negative lookahead contains `\s*`. This can block a Node.js worker for seconds and can starve production request workers under concurrent large or adversarial responses.

**Resolution**

Remove raw recipient addresses and subjects from the new suppression logs. Log only the suppression event, environment, and recipient counts; use a keyed hash or another approved non-reversible identifier only if correlation is required.
