ENG-1812 Adopt the vendor idempotency token in v0 (ENG-1250 §6, first adapter)

First adapter to adopt [[ENG-702]] AC1's idempotency token. Part of [[ENG-1250]] §6. ## Why v0 first [[ENG-702]] names it as one of the two dangerous retry-heavy paths: *"the v0 code documents in its own comments that a retried correction can be applied and charged twice"*, and *"the v0 retry loop books duplicates under one reservation"*. It is also the only adapter that already had a canonical idempotency notion to reuse, so it sets the shape for the other eight. ## The unit of charge is one per RESERVATION, not per attempt `meteredV0` returns a **thunk**, and `withRetry` re-invokes it. So every retry inside one reservation booked another charge — exactly the defect the row names. The token now comes from `v0UsageGuard` itself, via a new `meteringKeyFor(guardKey, reservedAt)`: * Every `withRetry` attempt inside one reservation shares the key → the transactional write collapses them into **one** charge. * A guard-permitted retry after a failure mints a **new** reservation, so a new key, and is charged in full — because it really did call v0 again. Deriving it from the guard rather than inventing a parallel notion is the point. Two independent definitions of "the same v0 call" would drift, and the failure would be silent: the guard deduping while the ledger charged twice, or the reverse. ## Adoption shape for the remaining adapters The guards' callbacks now receive the key (`create(meteringKey)` / `send(meteringKey)`). A plain `() => Promise` stays assignable in TypeScript, so this was backward compatible and adoption stays per-call-site — 11 of 11 v0 metering sites threaded, verified by grep, with no change to retry or guard semantics. ## Testing 59 tests across the four v0 suites, 239 across all fourteen affected; typecheck clean. Four mutations fail, including "reservation time dropped from key" and "guard key dropped from key" — the two ways the identity could silently become too coarse or too fine.

## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium ## What's wrong (verified against `origin/main` @ `a54b424b2`, 2026-09-03) `PUT /api/agent-mode/schedule-templates/:templateId` writes whatever `visibility` the caller passes, with no admin check: ```ts // controllers/agentModeController.ts:13637 if (visibility !== undefined) updates.visibility = visibility; ``` The only authorization on that route is ownership of the row (`:13620`, `existing.createdBy !== user.userId` → 404). So **any authenticated user can promote their own private schedule template to** `visibility: 'system'` **or** `'public'`**, making it visible to every user on the platform.** That bypasses the entire review workflow that exists for exactly this purpose: `scheduleTemplateService.submitForReview()` (private → `pending_review`), `approveTemplate()` (`pending_review` → `public`), and `rejectTemplate()`, plus the admin-only queue at `GET /api/admin/schedule-templates/pending-review`. The review path is reachable at `POST /schedule-templates/:templateId/submit-for-review` (`routes/agentMode.ts:352`) — and is trivially skippable by calling PUT instead. The sibling create route gets this right: `createScheduleTemplate` (`:13536`) hardcodes `visibility: 'private' as const` and ignores the body field. Only the update route leaks. ## Blast radius `getScheduleTemplates` (`:13560`) returns the caller's own templates plus **all **`system` and `public` rows, so a promoted template appears in every user's template picker (`useAgentModeSchedules.ts:476`) and in Emma's `list_schedule_templates`. A schedule template carries a `startingMessage` — an agent prompt — plus `requiredFunctionCalls`. A hostile or careless one is prompt-injection surface reaching every customer's agent, and `createScheduleFromTemplate` **copies** `startingMessage` **onto the schedule at creation** (`:13778`), so revoking the template afterwards does not undo schedules already created from it. Currently unexploited: production `AW-ScheduleTemplates` (6 rows, read-only scan 2026-09-03) holds 5 `private` and 1 `public`, zero `system`. The one `public` row ("Multi-Campaign Performance Report") predates this audit and was not checked for how it got there. ## Related confusion worth fixing at the same time The `manage_schedule_template` MCP tool advertises `visibility: 'system' | 'private' | 'public' | 'pending_review'` in its input schema (`mcp/server/apiTools.ts:780`) but routes `create` to the user endpoint that silently drops the field. A non-admin `PUT /api/agent-mode/schedule-templates/:templateId` cannot set `visibility` to `system` or `public`. Attempting it is rejected explicitly (403 or a validation error), not silently ignored — a silent drop is how the `manage_schedule_template` confusion above started. 2. A non-admin may still move their own template `private` ⇄ `pending_review` (the supported self-service transitions), so `submit-for-review` keeps working. 3. The admin route (`routes/adminScheduleTemplateRoutes.ts`, `isAdmin`-gated) is unchanged and remains the way a `system` template is created. 4. `manage_schedule_template`'s input schema no longer advertises visibility values its route cannot deliver, or is repointed at a route that can. 5. An audit of existing non-`private` rows records how each reached that visibility; any that bypassed review are reported (not silently demoted — demoting a template in active use would break schedules referencing it). ## Complexity ledger New: one authorization check on an existing route, plus a tool-schema correction. ENG-1250 Usage accounting v2: one auditable spend ledger and admission gate for every AgentWeb-paid call

## Outcome Implement one org-level accounting architecture in which every **AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable** upstream call is recorded exactly once, priced honestly, visible in a spend history, and applied to the same monthly usage limit. This is the end-to-end architecture contract requested by Harsha. It replaces the current split between `tokenUsage.totalCost`, the daily `AW-UsageRecords` aggregates, the effectively dead `extraCostUsage` rail, vendor-specific counters, and unmetered vendor calls. ## Billing boundary Debit the user's/org's monthly usage balance when: * AgentWeb pays an upstream and the action is attributable to a billing subject. * The cost is measured by the vendor, or a versioned allocated rate exists. Do not debit when: * The customer pays through their own connected account (for example Meta ad spend or customer-owned SaaS/API usage). * The cost is shared platform overhead without a reviewed allocation policy. * The unit has no price. Unpriced paid egress must fail closed or be explicitly allowlisted as platform-funded; it must never become a silent $0 charge. ## Architecture ### 1. Immutable spend events are the source of truth Create an append-only, per-call usage event store ([ENG-702](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-702/make-vendor-usage-writes-idempotent-and-fail-loud-gate-before-any) data-plane gate) rather than treating a mutable monthly counter or daily aggregate as authoritative. Required event fields: * `eventId` / idempotency key * `occurredAt`, billing month * `billingUserId`, `orgId`, `actingUserId`, optional `onBehalfOf` * provider, operation, feature, unit, quantity * `costMicroUsd` * cost source: `measured | allocated` * rate-card version when allocated * session/task/run/request references * lifecycle: `reserved | settled | voided` * external vendor reference when available Retries with the same idempotency key must return the original event and add $0. ### 2. One charging API All paid egress goes through one service; callers may not write the ledger or monthly counter directly. Conceptual contract: 1. Resolve the org billing subject. 2. Classify the call as AgentWeb-paid, customer-paid, or platform overhead. 3. Resolve a measured cost or versioned allocated rate. 4. Reserve known/estimated spend when practical. 5. Check admission against settled spend + outstanding reservations. 6. Execute the vendor call. 7. Settle actual spend or void the reservation. 8. Atomically persist the idempotent event and update the billing-subject/month aggregate. LLM, image/video, v0, X, search, enrichment, voice, rendering, and future vendor adapters must use the same service. ### 3. Monthly state is a projection, not an independent counter Maintain an atomic `billingUserId + month` projection for fast admission: * settled chargeable spend * active reservations * included monthly allowance * purchased credits * admin grants/reversals * migration adjustment * remaining usable balance * current policy mode Invariant: summing immutable settled events must reproduce the monthly spend projection within one micro-dollar. Raw spend is always preserved. Credits and migration adjustments change available allowance; they never erase or rewrite spend. ### 4. Admission semantics * A new job is admitted only when remaining balance covers its reservation or the policy explicitly permits an overrun. * Work admitted before the boundary may finish under the existing admitted-work rule. * Fixed-price calls reserve the exact allocated rate. * Variable-cost calls reserve a documented maximum/estimate and settle the actual amount. * Concurrent requests use conditional/transactional writes so two calls cannot both spend the same remaining balance. * `full_choice | optimized | paused` is derived from this one monthly projection; token volume remains an analytical dimension, not a second competing gate. ### 5. Versioned vendor rate registry One reviewed registry defines provider, operation, unit, rate, currency, effective dates, and source. Pricing rules: * Vendor-reported cost wins when available. * Shared wallets/subscriptions use an explicit allocated rate ([ENG-703](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-703/set-the-allocated-vendor-rate-card-blocks-every-metering-adapter-from)). * A price change creates a new version; historical events retain the rate version used. * No adapter embeds an independent dollar literal. ### 6. Coverage Bring existing slices onto the charging API: * LLM providers, embeddings, image/video * X ([ENG-664](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-664/meter-x-twitter-api-usage-cost-per-account-and-per-tool)) * v0 ([ENG-694](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-694/meter-v0-landing-page-generation-including-the-unguarded-iterate-path)) * [You.com]() and Google CSE ([ENG-695](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-695/meter-paid-web-search-youcom-google-custom-search-and-thread-the)) * Apollo and [enrich.so]() ([ENG-696](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-696/bring-apollo-and-enrichso-onto-the-ledger-and-close-the-six-bypassed)) * ElevenLabs, 2captcha, Placid ([ENG-698](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-698/meter-the-single-call-site-per-unit-vendors-elevenlabs-2captcha-placid)) * Remotion Lambda ([ENG-699](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-699/meter-remotion-lambda-renders-at-submission-time)) * other AgentWeb-paid voice/search/media/email vendors identified by [ENG-701](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-701/make-metering-coverage-a-ci-fact-instead-of-an-audit-artifact) The CI paid-egress registry must fail when a new paid client/call site has no charging adapter or explicit platform-funded exemption. ### 7. Read models and product UX Produce daily/provider/member/feature/session aggregates from immutable events. The org usage screen must show: * billing subject and pooled-org behavior * raw spend versus adjustments and usable balance * daily trend * spend by provider, product feature, and acting member * reservations/in-flight spend * why the account is optimized or paused * reset date and purchased-credit history No admin should need direct DynamoDB inspection to explain a pause. ### 8. Reconciliation Run two independent checks: * Internal: immutable event sum = monthly projection = dashboard total. * External: vendor invoice/wallet/usage export versus attributed ledger totals, allowing only documented timing or allocation differences. Drift above one cent or the vendor-specific threshold alerts and prevents enabling enforcement for that provider. A successful vendor call without a settled/voided event is an operational error. ### 9. Migration and rollout 1. Land schema/idempotency behind the explicit data-plane approval gate. 2. Dual-write old and new rails in observe-only mode. 3. Reconcile LLMs first; the existing gate cannot move until the crater class is resolved. 4. Add vendor adapters one family at a time. 5. Run at least seven days of shadow reconciliation and boundary/concurrency tests. 6. Switch admission to the new monthly projection. 7. Observe a month reset and credit purchase/reversal. 8. Stop writes to `extraCostUsage` and the legacy independent cost counter. 9. Delete legacy paths only after rollback evidence and one clean period boundary. ## Complexity impact Adds one idempotent event rail, one monthly projection, and one rate registry; removes multiple counters, special cases, and manual reconciliation paths. Net result must be fewer charging paths than today. ## Acceptance criteria (from Harsha's request) 1. Every AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable API cost is deducted from the same org monthly usage balance exactly once. 2. Customer-paid integrations and unallocated platform overhead are not charged. 3. A pause is explainable to the cent from per-call events, including provider, feature, acting member, and adjustment history. 4. Vendor spend, immutable events, monthly projection, and dashboard reconcile within the defined threshold. 5. Retries, concurrent calls, failed calls, reservations, refunds/reversals, org inheritance, and month rollover have automated tests. 6. No production enforcement moves to the new rail until shadow reconciliation passes and Harsha approves the data-plane change. 7. The legacy `extraCostUsage` and independent counter paths are retired rather than maintained as fallbacks.

ENG-1813 hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan doesn't check ENG-1811 debt -- an autocomplete run that deletes its last pending step in the same turn won't get auto-nudged to fill the debt

Follow-up from PR agentweb#2808's round-4 review (ENG-1811 debt-ledger fix). hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan (backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts, ~line 881) and the workPlanHasPendingStep helper it (and scheduleAutoWorkPlanContinuation) rely on have no awareness of workPlan.pendingRequiredFunctionCalls (the ENG-1811 debt ledger). Concrete scenario: an autocomplete work plan's model, in one turn, calls modify_work_plan with removeStepCounts that removes the LAST remaining pending step (creating real, unresolved debt for that step's requiredFunctionCalls), and does not re-add it. Since modify_work_plan itself succeeded this turn, hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan's own short-circuit ("calls.some(toolCallSucceeded) -> return false, not stalled") fires BEFORE it would ever reach the pending-step check -- so no further auto-continuation round gets scheduled, and the unattended run just stops. This is narrower than the original ENG-1811 bug and does NOT reopen the core guarantee that PR #2808 fixed: the session-level pendingRequiredFunctionCalls ledger is still correctly populated and persisted, setWorkPlanStatusAttempt still correctly BLOCKS the plan from ever being reported "finished" while the debt is outstanding, and AgentModeService.buildWorkPlanContextMessages / buildMarketingContext now correctly render a "NOT actually finished" banner (not "ALL STEPS DONE") on the next turn that touches this session. So the plan can never be silently marked done -- it just means the autocomplete self-driving loop specifically won't automatically retry to go fill the debt on its own; the plan is left correctly-blocked-but-unattended until a user, a schedule, or an admin next interacts with the session. Suggested fix: thread pendingRequiredFunctionCalls (resolved against real calledFunctions) into workPlanHasPendingStep (or a sibling check consulted alongside it in hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan / scheduleAutoWorkPlanContinuation's pre-fire re-check), so an autocomplete run whose last pending step got deleted while leaving genuine debt is treated as still-stalled and gets another auto-continuation round instead of silently going quiet. Deliberately scoped OUT of PR #2808 (round-4 review finding, confirmed real via direct code read -- backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts lines ~881-901, ~1543-1546, ~1605-1608) to avoid further scope creep on an already-urgent, already-twice-self-corrected PR. Disclosed in PR #2808's description as a known follow-up.

Step removal (call A) and re-addition (call B) are two independent invocations, each with its own fresh session read and its own removeStepCounts argument. Call B's own removeStepCounts does not mention stepCount 2 (it isn't removing anything), so removedOriginal is undefined in call B, and the re-added step goes through the completely unprotected new-step branch. ENG-1807 Scheduled-chat /test-history reports passed:false for a run that actually completed correctly after a worker-drain interruption

## `test-history` reports `passed: false` for a scheduled-chat test run that actually completed correctly **Found while live-testing PR #2792 (ENG-1552 / monitor_lead_volume fix) on real prod, 2026-09-07.** ### Repro (verified, not inferred) 1. `POST /api/agent-mode/scheduled-chats/{scheduleId}/test` on a real scheduled chat. 2. `GET .../test-history` for that run returns: ``` {"runId":"d254d793-...","status":"failure","passed":false,"actualFunctionCalls":[], "functionCallMisses":["list_meta_ads_campaigns","get_meta_ads_metrics","monitor_lead_volume", "list_html_templates","perform_data_analysis","create_html_from_template"], ...} ``` 3. The underlying session (`sessionId: 611594de-e280-4eec-902f-4909a9ad4d57`) has `error: "Worker is draining — no new requests accepted"`, thrown from `GenerateMarketingResponseWorkerService.runInWorker` (`generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.js:378`) — almost certainly hit during a deploy's rolling-instance drain (multiple unrelated deploys were cycling through prod back-to-back at the time). 4. Despite that, the session's actual final assistant message and the real generated report (fetched directly, HTTP 200, 1.4MB real content, verified by reading it) show the run **did** complete correctly — all required tools were genuinely called and the report contains real, correct data. 5. So `test-history`'s `passed: false` / `actualFunctionCalls: []` is **wrong** for what actually happened: it reflects only the pre-interruption attempt, not the session's real, eventually-correct outcome. ### Why this isn't "working as intended" This codebase already has a purpose-built mechanism for exactly this class of problem: `priorToolCalls` (ENG-657, `agentModeController.ts` ~line 3569) — "tool calls already made in a PRIOR (abandoned) portion of this session that this run is RESUMING... otherwise a resumed run would be wrongly marked `passed: false` for calls it made before the interruption." That's precisely what happened here. The open question (not yet traced to a fix) is whether `testScheduledChat`'s `/test-history` recording path (`agentModeController.ts:12017`) actually reads from the same recovered/resumed tool-call ledger the general scheduled-run path already relies on, or independently persists a stale snapshot from the first, interrupted attempt. Separately, `testScheduledChat`'s own background dispatch already has one related, but distinct, fix in place — `ENG-1189` wraps it in `trackScheduledRun` specifically so a deploy's graceful shutdown doesn't abandon the run outright. That fix is for the OUTER dispatch; the error here came from an INNER component (`GenerateMarketingResponseWorkerService`) with its own separate drain state, which `ENG-1189`'s fix doesn't appear to cover. ### Impact Low-severity but real: whoever runs a manual `/test` and trusts `test-history`'s `passed`/`status` field alone (its literal, stated purpose — "poll get_scheduled_chat_test_history to check results") gets told a run failed when it actually succeeded. Someone debugging a real regression under this same false signal would waste time chasing a phantom failure, or worse, miss a genuine failure buried under "just infra noise" if this pattern is common enough to become background noise. ### Scope note Confirmed unrelated to ENG-1552/ENG-1553 — this is entirely in `agentModeController.ts`'s test-run dispatch/scoring path, no shared files or dependency either direction. Should be its own small, separate PR, not bundled into upcoming L2 Diagnose work. ### Not yet done (deliberately, scoping this as a bug report, not a fix) Have not traced exactly where `test-history`'s persisted record gets written/read, so have not confirmed the precise line-level fix. Next step for whoever picks this up: find where the `runId`'s test-history entry is persisted (likely near `testScheduledChat`'s `runScheduledChat` call or wherever its result gets written to the schedule's test-history list) and confirm whether it threads through `priorToolCalls`-style resumed-ledger data the way the general scheduled path does.

ENG-1250 Usage accounting v2: one auditable spend ledger and admission gate for every AgentWeb-paid call

## Outcome Implement one org-level accounting architecture in which every **AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable** upstream call is recorded exactly once, priced honestly, visible in a spend history, and applied to the same monthly usage limit. This is the end-to-end architecture contract requested by Harsha. It replaces the current split between `tokenUsage.totalCost`, the daily `AW-UsageRecords` aggregates, the effectively dead `extraCostUsage` rail, vendor-specific counters, and unmetered vendor calls. ## Billing boundary Debit the user's/org's monthly usage balance when: * AgentWeb pays an upstream and the action is attributable to a billing subject. * The cost is measured by the vendor, or a versioned allocated rate exists. Do not debit when: * The customer pays through their own connected account (for example Meta ad spend or customer-owned SaaS/API usage). * The cost is shared platform overhead without a reviewed allocation policy. * The unit has no price. Unpriced paid egress must fail closed or be explicitly allowlisted as platform-funded; it must never become a silent $0 charge. ## Architecture ### 1. Immutable spend events are the source of truth Create an append-only, per-call usage event store ([ENG-702](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-702/make-vendor-usage-writes-idempotent-and-fail-loud-gate-before-any) data-plane gate) rather than treating a mutable monthly counter or daily aggregate as authoritative. Required event fields: * `eventId` / idempotency key * `occurredAt`, billing month * `billingUserId`, `orgId`, `actingUserId`, optional `onBehalfOf` * provider, operation, feature, unit, quantity * `costMicroUsd` * cost source: `measured | allocated` * rate-card version when allocated * session/task/run/request references * lifecycle: `reserved | settled | voided` * external vendor reference when available Retries with the same idempotency key must return the original event and add $0. ### 2. One charging API All paid egress goes through one service; callers may not write the ledger or monthly counter directly. Conceptual contract: 1. Resolve the org billing subject. 2. Classify the call as AgentWeb-paid, customer-paid, or platform overhead. 3. Resolve a measured cost or versioned allocated rate. 4. Reserve known/estimated spend when practical. 5. Check admission against settled spend + outstanding reservations. 6. Execute the vendor call. 7. Settle actual spend or void the reservation. 8. Atomically persist the idempotent event and update the billing-subject/month aggregate. LLM, image/video, v0, X, search, enrichment, voice, rendering, and future vendor adapters must use the same service. ### 3. Monthly state is a projection, not an independent counter Maintain an atomic `billingUserId + month` projection for fast admission: * settled chargeable spend * active reservations * included monthly allowance * purchased credits * admin grants/reversals * migration adjustment * remaining usable balance * current policy mode Invariant: summing immutable settled events must reproduce the monthly spend projection within one micro-dollar. Raw spend is always preserved. Credits and migration adjustments change available allowance; they never erase or rewrite spend. ### 4. Admission semantics * A new job is admitted only when remaining balance covers its reservation or the policy explicitly permits an overrun. * Work admitted before the boundary may finish under the existing admitted-work rule. * Fixed-price calls reserve the exact allocated rate. * Variable-cost calls reserve a documented maximum/estimate and settle the actual amount. * Concurrent requests use conditional/transactional writes so two calls cannot both spend the same remaining balance. * `full_choice | optimized | paused` is derived from this one monthly projection; token volume remains an analytical dimension, not a second competing gate. ### 5. Versioned vendor rate registry One reviewed registry defines provider, operation, unit, rate, currency, effective dates, and source. Pricing rules: * Vendor-reported cost wins when available. * Shared wallets/subscriptions use an explicit allocated rate ([ENG-703](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-703/set-the-allocated-vendor-rate-card-blocks-every-metering-adapter-from)). * A price change creates a new version; historical events retain the rate version used. * No adapter embeds an independent dollar literal. ### 6. Coverage Bring existing slices onto the charging API: * LLM providers, embeddings, image/video * X ([ENG-664](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-664/meter-x-twitter-api-usage-cost-per-account-and-per-tool)) * v0 ([ENG-694](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-694/meter-v0-landing-page-generation-including-the-unguarded-iterate-path)) * [You.com]() and Google CSE ([ENG-695](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-695/meter-paid-web-search-youcom-google-custom-search-and-thread-the)) * Apollo and [enrich.so]() ([ENG-696](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-696/bring-apollo-and-enrichso-onto-the-ledger-and-close-the-six-bypassed)) * ElevenLabs, 2captcha, Placid ([ENG-698](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-698/meter-the-single-call-site-per-unit-vendors-elevenlabs-2captcha-placid)) * Remotion Lambda ([ENG-699](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-699/meter-remotion-lambda-renders-at-submission-time)) * other AgentWeb-paid voice/search/media/email vendors identified by [ENG-701](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-701/make-metering-coverage-a-ci-fact-instead-of-an-audit-artifact) The CI paid-egress registry must fail when a new paid client/call site has no charging adapter or explicit platform-funded exemption. ### 7. Read models and product UX Produce daily/provider/member/feature/session aggregates from immutable events. The org usage screen must show: * billing subject and pooled-org behavior * raw spend versus adjustments and usable balance * daily trend * spend by provider, product feature, and acting member * reservations/in-flight spend * why the account is optimized or paused * reset date and purchased-credit history No admin should need direct DynamoDB inspection to explain a pause. ### 8. Reconciliation Run two independent checks: * Internal: immutable event sum = monthly projection = dashboard total. * External: vendor invoice/wallet/usage export versus attributed ledger totals, allowing only documented timing or allocation differences. Drift above one cent or the vendor-specific threshold alerts and prevents enabling enforcement for that provider. A successful vendor call without a settled/voided event is an operational error. ### 9. Migration and rollout 1. Land schema/idempotency behind the explicit data-plane approval gate. 2. Dual-write old and new rails in observe-only mode. 3. Reconcile LLMs first; the existing gate cannot move until the crater class is resolved. 4. Add vendor adapters one family at a time. 5. Run at least seven days of shadow reconciliation and boundary/concurrency tests. 6. Switch admission to the new monthly projection. 7. Observe a month reset and credit purchase/reversal. 8. Stop writes to `extraCostUsage` and the legacy independent cost counter. 9. Delete legacy paths only after rollback evidence and one clean period boundary. ## Complexity impact Adds one idempotent event rail, one monthly projection, and one rate registry; removes multiple counters, special cases, and manual reconciliation paths. Net result must be fewer charging paths than today. ## Acceptance criteria (from Harsha's request) 1. Every AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable API cost is deducted from the same org monthly usage balance exactly once. 2. Customer-paid integrations and unallocated platform overhead are not charged. 3. A pause is explainable to the cent from per-call events, including provider, feature, acting member, and adjustment history. 4. Vendor spend, immutable events, monthly projection, and dashboard reconcile within the defined threshold. 5. Retries, concurrent calls, failed calls, reservations, refunds/reversals, org inheritance, and month rollover have automated tests. 6. No production enforcement moves to the new rail until shadow reconciliation passes and Harsha approves the data-plane change. 7. The legacy `extraCostUsage` and independent counter paths are retired rather than maintained as fallbacks.

ENG-493 Express 'trust proxy' never configured — req.ip collapses to one value for every request, breaking per-IP rate limiting

Found while live-testing ENG-492's new forward-lead rate limiter on the EC2 test env. ## The bug No file in the backend ever calls `app.set('trust proxy', ...)`. Without it, Express's `req.ip` is the raw TCP socket peer, not the real client — it ignores `X-Forwarded-For` entirely regardless of whether an upstream proxy sets it correctly. **Confirmed empirically in prod** (not just theoretical): pulled a live EB log bundle for `Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3` and checked `/var/log/nginx/access.log`. nginx's own `$remote_addr` field is always one of exactly 2 internal ALB addresses (`172.31.0.31`, `172.31.18.3`) — expected, since nginx sits behind the ALB. But the REAL client IP is already present in the log as a separate field (via the ALB's own X-Forwarded-For), e.g. `45.253.245.23`, `34.105.84.37` — so nginx receives the correct client IP just fine. Since nginx proxies to the Node app over localhost on the same instance, and `trust proxy` is never set, `req.ip` inside Express resolves to `127.0.0.1` for every single request, from every different real user, everywhere. There is currently no way for any Express-level, per-IP logic in this app to distinguish one real caller from another. Also confirmed in the EC2 test env (single ngrok tunnel): the exact same collapse happens there, empirically — 22 rapid test requests from one machine exhausted a 20-request/IP quota, and a completely unrelated real page's lead submission got rejected as collateral damage moments later. ## Why this matters Any Express-level rate limiter keyed by `req.ip` (the standard/default keying for `express-rate-limit`) is not actually per-client in this app — it's a de facto GLOBAL limit shared by every caller. This already affects the pre-existing `auth.ts` login/register limiter (10 attempts / 15 min), silently, though it's likely gone unnoticed because 10 login/register attempts combined across the ENTIRE platform in 15 minutes is a high enough bar to rarely get hit in practice. It would NOT have gone unnoticed for a higher-traffic public endpoint — this is exactly what surfaced it (see [ENG-492](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-492/forward-lead-had-no-rate-limiting-phone-hashing-didnt-match-metas-capi), which avoided the problem entirely by keying its own new limiter by `listId` instead of IP rather than depend on this being fixed). ## Suggested fix Add `app.set('trust proxy', )` to the Express app setup (server.ts/app.ts), with the correct hop count for this exact topology (ALB -> nginx -> Node, one hop before the app instance if measuring from the app's own perspective — needs confirming against the specific EB platform's ALB/nginx chain, ideally verified the same empirical way this bug was: temporarily log `req.ip` alongside real requests, or a scoped test, and confirm it now varies per real distinct caller instead of always being 127.0.0.1). This is a cross-cutting change (affects every `req.ip` consumer in the app, not just rate limiters), so it deserves its own focused pass rather than a drive-by fix. ## Related * ENG-492: the rate limiter that surfaced this. Sidestepped it by keying on `listId` instead of IP, so it does not depend on this ticket being fixed. * `routes/leadMagnet.ts` already has a code comment from an earlier author flagging the exact same gap ("req.ip returns ::1 or ::ffff:127.0.0.1 behind a proxy without 'trust proxy' set... ensure app.set('trust proxy', 1) is configured in server.ts") — never acted on.

ENG-1813 hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan doesn't check ENG-1811 debt -- an autocomplete run that deletes its last pending step in the same turn won't get auto-nudged to fill the debt

Follow-up from PR agentweb#2808's round-4 review (ENG-1811 debt-ledger fix). hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan (backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts, ~line 881) and the workPlanHasPendingStep helper it (and scheduleAutoWorkPlanContinuation) rely on have no awareness of workPlan.pendingRequiredFunctionCalls (the ENG-1811 debt ledger). Concrete scenario: an autocomplete work plan's model, in one turn, calls modify_work_plan with removeStepCounts that removes the LAST remaining pending step (creating real, unresolved debt for that step's requiredFunctionCalls), and does not re-add it. Since modify_work_plan itself succeeded this turn, hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan's own short-circuit ("calls.some(toolCallSucceeded) -> return false, not stalled") fires BEFORE it would ever reach the pending-step check -- so no further auto-continuation round gets scheduled, and the unattended run just stops. This is narrower than the original ENG-1811 bug and does NOT reopen the core guarantee that PR #2808 fixed: the session-level pendingRequiredFunctionCalls ledger is still correctly populated and persisted, setWorkPlanStatusAttempt still correctly BLOCKS the plan from ever being reported "finished" while the debt is outstanding, and AgentModeService.buildWorkPlanContextMessages / buildMarketingContext now correctly render a "NOT actually finished" banner (not "ALL STEPS DONE") on the next turn that touches this session. So the plan can never be silently marked done -- it just means the autocomplete self-driving loop specifically won't automatically retry to go fill the debt on its own; the plan is left correctly-blocked-but-unattended until a user, a schedule, or an admin next interacts with the session. Suggested fix: thread pendingRequiredFunctionCalls (resolved against real calledFunctions) into workPlanHasPendingStep (or a sibling check consulted alongside it in hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan / scheduleAutoWorkPlanContinuation's pre-fire re-check), so an autocomplete run whose last pending step got deleted while leaving genuine debt is treated as still-stalled and gets another auto-continuation round instead of silently going quiet. Deliberately scoped OUT of PR #2808 (round-4 review finding, confirmed real via direct code read -- backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts lines ~881-901, ~1543-1546, ~1605-1608) to avoid further scope creep on an already-urgent, already-twice-self-corrected PR. ENG-1797 Metering coverage guard cannot see helper-indirected metering — v0 is allowlisted as unmetered while metered, and un-metering it would ship green

The [[ENG-701]] coverage guard cannot see metering that goes through a helper, so `v0Service.ts` is simultaneously **metered in reality** and **allowlisted as unmetered** — and a regression that removed the metering would not fail the build. Found while verifying [[ENG-1139]]'s blocker list on 2026-09-07 against `origin/main` @ `0f601ca24`. Not filed as part of that work; raising it separately because it sits on ENG-701/[[ENG-694]]. ## What the guard checks `vendorMeteringCoverageGuard.test.ts` decides a module is metered with `isMetered()`, which requires **both** a direct import of `recordUsage`/`recordVendorUsage` *from* `usageRecorderService` **and** a call to one of them. That strictness was deliberate — a CodeRabbit finding on ENG-701 asked for it, so a bare substring match in a comment or an unused import could not claim coverage. ## Why that now misfires [[ENG-694]] metered v0 through a wrapper rather than at the call site: ```ts // services/v0Service.ts:18 import { meteredV0 } from "./v0Metering"; // ...11 call sites meteredV0({ userId, operation: "chat_create" }, () => v0.chats.create({ ... })) ``` `v0Service.ts` therefore imports `meteredV0`, not `recordUsage` — so `isMetered()` returns **false**, the staleness detector never fires, and this entry survives: ```ts { path: 'services/v0Service.ts', vendor: 'v0 (Vercel)', issue: 'ENG-694', reason: '9 billable v0.chats.create/sendMessage sites; none record usage yet.' } ``` The reason string is now false: those sites *do* record usage. ## The consequence, demonstrated The stale entry is not cosmetic — it is a standing amnesty. Stripping 10 of the 11 `meteredV0` wrappers out of `v0Service.ts` and re-running the guard: ``` Tests: 14 passed, 14 total ``` **A change that silently un-meters every v0 landing-page generation ships green.** That is precisely the failure ENG-701 was built to prevent: *"coverage discovered by an audit decays the moment the audit ends"*. (Mutation reverted; the tree was left clean.) ## Why deleting the entry is not the fix Removing the allowlist entry makes the guard *fail* instead — `v0Service.ts` still matches the `v0-sdk` signature and `isMetered()` still returns false, so it would be reported as an unmetered violation. The detector itself has to learn about indirection. ## Suggested shape Treat a module as metered when it reaches the recorder **transitively** — e.g. resolve relative imports one hop and check whether the imported module is itself metered. One hop covers `meteredV0` and any future `meteredX` helper, keeps the guard a pure function over the in-memory file map, and preserves the anti-substring strictness ENG-701 asked for. Whatever the fix, it should come with the inverse test: a fixture where the helper's metering is removed and the guard **fails**. ## Not touched No code changed. Main thread is idle in `select()` inside `asyncio.base_events._run_once` -- the event loop itself has nothing scheduled, meaning it's blocked waiting on a network read that isn't returning. CPU time stayed frozen at `0:05` across the entire 5+ minute observation window (checked twice, ~90s apart, identical). `ss -tnp` showed live `ESTAB` connections from the process to `104.18.3.115:443` (Cloudflare-fronted, consistent with OpenRouter) persisting the whole time -- a real request is open, just never completing. **Suspected mechanism (not yet confirmed):** this is very possibly the exact risk ENG-1820's own review flagged and accepted as a tradeoff -- `require_parameters: true` used to guarantee OpenRouter would only route to providers declaring full support for every parameter in the request (including `parallel_tool_calls`, the one that was breaking everything). Without it, OpenRouter can route to *any* available provider for the model, including ones that might silently ignore an unsupported parameter -- or, as may be happening here, ones that are slow/degraded/hanging on this specific request. The old behavior (`require_parameters: true`) would fail FAST and LOUD (404, "no endpoints found") when no compliant provider existed; the new behavior may silently pick a bad provider and hang instead. **Also notable:** `create_openrouter_llm` (`agent-engine/openrouter_gateway.py`) sets `max_retries: 1` on the `ChatOpenAI` client but does **not** set an explicit request `timeout`. ENG-1822 Removing OpenRouter require_parameters may cause silent multi-minute hangs instead of fast 404s

Discovered live while E2E-testing ENG-1820's fix on production (execution `1788877994807`, session `2a6a2922-6a05-4929-8297-015c64685c21`, 2026-09-08, model `azure->openai->gpt-4.1`). **What happened:** After ENG-1820 removed `require_parameters: true` from `openrouter_gateway.py` (to fix the 404 that was blocking every task's first real action, see ENG-1820), a real production task reached Step 1, loaded cookies, and then went completely silent -- 5+ minutes with zero forward progress, before this ticket was filed (still running/unresolved as of filing). **Confirmed genuinely hung, not just slow:** got a `py-spy dump` of the live process (PID 2535591) mid-hang. Main thread is idle in `select()` inside `asyncio.base_events._run_once` -- the event loop itself has nothing scheduled, meaning it's blocked waiting on a network read that isn't returning. CPU time stayed frozen at `0:05` across the entire 5+ minute observation window (checked twice, ~90s apart, identical). `ss -tnp` showed live `ESTAB` connections from the process to `104.18.3.115:443` (Cloudflare-fronted, consistent with OpenRouter) persisting the whole time -- a real request is open, just never completing. **Suspected mechanism (not yet confirmed):** this is very possibly the exact risk ENG-1820's own review flagged and accepted as a tradeoff -- `require_parameters: true` used to guarantee OpenRouter would only route to providers declaring full support for every parameter in the request (including `parallel_tool_calls`, the one that was breaking everything). Without it, OpenRouter can route to *any* available provider for the model, including ones that might silently ignore an unsupported parameter -- or, as may be happening here, ones that are slow/degraded/hanging on this specific request. The old behavior (`require_parameters: true`) would fail FAST and LOUD (404, "no endpoints found") when no compliant provider existed; the new behavior may silently pick a bad provider and hang instead. **Also notable:** `create_openrouter_llm` (`agent-engine/openrouter_gateway.py`) sets `max_retries: 1` on the `ChatOpenAI` client but does **not** set an explicit request `timeout`. This means the effective timeout, if any, falls back to whatever the underlying `openai`/`httpx` client defaults to -- not confirmed what that actually is in this SDK version, or whether it's long enough that a customer would just perceive this as "AgentWeb hung" long before it fires. The only guaranteed backstop is `task_monitor.py`'s own `TASK_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=900` (15 minutes) task-level timeout, which is a very long time for a customer to wait for a "task failed" message. **Severity:** if this reproduces reliably (not yet confirmed -- only one observed instance, still in progress as of filing), this could mean ENG-1820's fix traded "task fails instantly with a clear error, 100% of the time" for "task sometimes hangs silently for minutes before failing" -- which may be a worse customer experience even though the underlying capability (task completing successfully at all) is what's actually being tested for the first time here. **Not yet done:** * Confirm whether this specific execution eventually completes, times out at 900s, or is a true indefinite hang. * Determine whether this is reproducible (try again) or was a one-off OpenRouter-side transient issue. * Check whether an explicit request-level `timeout` should be added to `create_openrouter_llm`'s `ChatOpenAI` construction regardless of root cause, as a defensive backstop shorter than the 900s task-level timeout. * Decide whether `require_parameters` needs to come back in some scoped form (e.g. per-parameter rather than blanket), now that removing it entirely has a real observed downside, not just a hypothetical one.

ENG-1823 web_agent.py reports task success from is_done() instead of is_successful() -- customers see 'completed' on tasks the agent itself flagged as failed

Discovered live while investigating ENG-1822 (traced by an independent review of PR #2823, then independently re-verified against the real installed browser-use source before filing this). **Confirmed via direct read of** `browser_use/agent/views.py` **(**`AgentHistoryList`**):** ```python def is_done(self) -> bool: """Check if the agent is done""" if self.history and len(self.history[-1].result) > 0: last_result = self.history[-1].result[-1] return last_result.is_done is True return False def is_successful(self) -> bool | None: """Check if the agent completed successfully -- the agent decides in the last step if it was successful or not. None if not done yet.""" if self.history and len(self.history[-1].result) > 0: last_result = self.history[-1].result[-1] if last_result.is_done is True: return last_result.success return None ``` `is_done()` only checks whether the agent invoked the `done` action at all -- it is completely blind to that action's own `success` field. `is_successful()` is the one that actually reads `.success`. `agent-engine/web_agent.py` **(**`execute_task`**, ~line 435) uses the wrong one:** ```python task_is_done = False # Initialize task_is_done agent_message = None if result.is_done(): task_is_done = True agent_message = result.history[-1].result[-1].extracted_content ``` `task_is_done` then flows straight into the function's returned `"success"` field (~line 530: `return {"success": task_is_done, ...}`). `agent-engine/task_monitor.py` (~line 1325) does `if result['success']: update_execution_status(execution_id, 'completed', ...)`. **Net effect:** DynamoDB's execution `status` (and whatever the customer ultimately sees) is driven purely by "did the agent call `done()`," never by whether that `done()` call itself said `success: true` or `success: false`. A task where the model explicitly says "I'm done, but I failed to accomplish this" (`success: false`) still gets reported as `completed`. **Directly observed in production, not theoretical:** this is exactly the mechanism behind the incident that surfaced ENG-1822 -- session `2a6a2922-6a05-4929-8297-015c64685c21`, execution `1788877994807`. The agent's own `done` action said `"success": false` with the message "The page is currently blank... No further actions have been taken yet" (a hallucinated non-result -- the browser never actually navigated). DynamoDB shows `status: completed` for that execution anyway. **Fix is not a simple find-replace.** `task_is_done` is currently used for two different purposes that need to stay separate: 1. "Did the agent finish running at all (vs hit the step limit or crash)?" -- this correctly gates whether to attempt the ENG-859 partial-extraction salvage path (a run that hit the step limit without ever calling `done()` should still get partial extraction attempted). `is_done()` is the semantically correct check for *this* purpose and should stay as-is here. 2. "Should the customer/DynamoDB be told this succeeded?" -- this should be `is_successful()`, not `is_done()`. Needs its own careful fix (likely tracking both `task_is_done` and a separate `task_succeeded` flag) and its own test coverage -- not bundled into PR #2823 (ENG-1822's timeout fix), which is a distinct, unrelated root cause. Not yet investigated: whether `output_as_json`/other downstream branches in `execute_task` also implicitly assume `task_is_done == success` in a way that needs updating alongside the main fix.

## Live-tested against the real Grok API — found and fixed a real calibration bug

No UI exists for this feature (confirmed earlier), so "preview" here meant exercising the real backend against the real `openrouter/x-ai/grok-4.6` API directly (via a scratch script, deleted after — not committed). Two rounds:

**Round 1 (before this fix):** a genuinely strong draft ("Spent 3 years building a $0 to $2M ARR SaaS...") and a throwaway "just posting to post lol nothing interesting here really" scored **0.34% apart**, both `netPositive: false`. The formula math was correct (unit-tested against an independent reference), but Grok was estimating negative-feedback probabilities (`report`, `blockAuthor`, etc.) on an intuitive "does this seem annoying" scale (1-3%) instead of X's real near-zero base rates — the source repo itself notes reporting is >1000x rarer than favoriting. Since those weights (-234 for report, etc.) are only that large *because* real rates are tiny, 10-100x-too-high estimates swamped every draft's score regardless of quality.

**Fix:** added explicit base-rate anchoring to the prompt.

**Round 2 (after the fix), live-tested again:**
| draft | score | netPositive |
|---|---|---|
| strong ("$0 to $2M ARR playbook...") | 0.0657 | **true** |
| weak ("just posting to post lol...") | 0.00089 | false |
| spammy ("FOLLOW ME NOW OR ELSE!!!...") | 0.00089 | false (correctly ordered below weak; visibly elevated notInterested/blockAuthor/report) |

73x spread between good and bad content, correct ordering, spammy content's negative-feedback signals visibly elevated over merely-boring content. This is now a real, working signal rather than a formula that happened to unit-test clean.

ENG-1828 Agent-engine fabricates task results instead of genuinely completing simple browsing tasks ("kitchen-sink" bundled-action hallucination)

## Summary Across the ENG-1818/1820/1822/1823 investigation, the same failure pattern was observed **5 times** on real production executions: instead of genuinely browsing, the agent's very first LLM call returns a single response with EVERY possible action field populated simultaneously (`done`, `search_google`, `go_to_url`, `write_file`, etc. all non-null at once) instead of exactly one. `browser-use` executes the first populated key -- which happens to be `done` -- so the agent self-terminates on step 1 with a fabricated result, never having actually navigated anywhere. This is separate from and NOT fixed by ENG-1823 (which correctly ensures a *self-reported* failure is reported as failed) -- in most of these cases the agent's own `done` action claims `success: true`, so the status-reporting layer has nothing to catch; the content itself is simply invented. ## Evidence -- 5 confirmed occurrences, all traced to real production executions | Execution ID | Date | Model | `done.success` | Text (excerpt) | | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | | 1788877994807 | 2026-09-08 | azure->openai->gpt-4.1 | false | fabricated fake HTML report, browser never navigated | | 1788881552500 | 2026-09-08 | azure->openai->gpt-4.1 | true | identical pattern, same task retried | | 1788897303516 | 2026-09-08 | azure->openai->gpt-4.1 | true | "This is just an example output as requested. No real action was performed yet..." | | 1788941528263 | 2026-09-09 | azure->openai->gpt-4.1 | true | "Example output:\n\n..." -- browser log shows "page is blank, no actions taken yet" | | 1788942560713 (1st attempt) | 2026-09-09 | azure->openai->gpt-4.1 | false | "Navigating to [https://httpbin.org/status/404]()..." (hadn't actually navigated) | **Notable pattern**: all 5 occurrences are on `azure->openai->gpt-4.1` specifically. The one clean, genuinely-successful run observed in the same investigation window (execution 1788941718489, [httpbin.org/uuid]() extraction) was ALSO on `azure->openai->gpt-4.1` and did NOT exhibit this pattern -- and a `google->google->gemini-3.1-pro-preview` retry (execution 1788942560713, 2nd attempt) also did not exhibit it, picking exactly one clean action per step. So this isn't purely a "gpt-4.1 is bad at this" story -- it's intermittent even on the same model, but has not yet been observed on Gemini in this investigation's sample (small sample, not a confirmed model-specific pattern). **Also notable**: the trivially-easy/well-known-answer tasks (e.g. "load [example.com](), report its title" -- a fact the model likely already has memorized) reproduced this 4/4. The one harder, genuinely-unknowable task (a random UUID from [httpbin.org]()) got a clean, honest, correctly-executed run. Suggests the model may be shortcutting to a plausible memorized/guessed answer instead of performing the actual browsing action when it judges the answer to be "obvious" -- worth testing directly (does artificially describing an equally-simple-but-unknowable task reproduce it? does explicitly instructing "you must actually browse, do not guess" reduce the rate?). ## Root-cause hypothesis (NOT YET CONFIRMED -- worth investigating first) This may be directly connected to ENG-1820's own documented tradeoff. `browser-use`'s per-step call is `llm.with_structured_output(AgentOutput, include_raw=True, method="function_calling")`, which via langchain's `bind_tools(tools, tool_choice="any", ...)` exposes every possible action as a distinct "tool" and asks the model to call `tool_choice="any"` (any ONE of them) -- normally with `parallel_tool_calls: false` also set, which should prevent the model from returning more than one tool call per turn. ENG-1820 removed `require_parameters: true` from the OpenRouter gateway (`agent-engine/openrouter_gateway.py`) because it was making OpenRouter hard-reject every request (`parallel_tool_calls` isn't declared as a supported parameter for most models in OpenRouter's catalog). Without `require_parameters`, OpenRouter can now route to providers that never explicitly declared support for `parallel_tool_calls` -- and per OpenRouter's own semantics, an unsupported parameter is typically **silently dropped**, not rejected, when `require_parameters` is off. If the provider fulfilling this request silently ignores `parallel_tool_calls: false` and returns multiple parallel tool calls, and `langchain`'s structured-output parser merges each tool call's arguments into the same `AgentOutput` pydantic object (since every action is a field on one shared schema), that would produce EXACTLY the observed shape: one object with several action fields populated simultaneously, `done` typically first because of field-declaration order. **How to verify this directly**: capture the raw OpenRouter response body (not just the parsed langchain object) for a reproduction -- check whether it contains multiple entries in `choices[0].message.tool_calls`, or a single tool call whose arguments blob is anomalously large/multi-field. If confirmed, potential fixes range from re-scoping `require_parameters` to just `parallel_tool_calls` (if OpenRouter's all-or-nothing semantics allow any partial scoping -- ENG-1820's investigation found they don't, so this may not be viable as originally conceived) to using OpenRouter's `provider.only`/`provider.order` to allow-list providers that are confirmed to respect `parallel_tool_calls`, to a code-level defensive fix (reject/retry any AgentOutput with more than one populated action field instead of silently executing the first). ## Impact Customers can receive a fabricated, plausible-looking "completed" result for a task the agent never actually performed. This is a customer-trust issue independent of whether the status-reporting layer (ENG-1823) is correct -- when the agent itself claims success, there is currently no mechanism to catch that the claim is fabricated. ## Related * Surfaced repeatedly during the ENG-1818/1820/1822/1823 investigation (2026-09-08/09) -- see those tickets for full context on the same subsystem. * ENG-1823 (Done) fixes a related but distinct bug: it ensures a *self-reported failure* is correctly reported as failed. ENG-1495 Assistant message React key drifts after post-accept session refresh, remounting the message and wiping local UI state

## Found while building [ENG-1491](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1491/post-accept-ux-client-side-surface-flip-start-step-1-suggested-reply) (ships separately, not blocked in code — blocked in visibility) Live-reproduced 5 times against a fresh test-env with console instrumentation (removed before shipping [ENG-1491](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1491/post-accept-ux-client-side-surface-flip-start-step-1-suggested-reply)). Every "Use this workplan" accept on the FIRST recommendation of a session showed **"This workplan is already active."** instead of **"Workplan started."** — even though the accept endpoint's own raw HTTP response body, captured via network inspection, consistently said `"alreadyApplied":false` (a genuinely fresh accept). This means the existing [ENG-1472](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1472/emma-recommend-a-published-workplan-inline-during-chat) success-state UX has likely never been visibly correct for a real user's first accept in a session — not something [ENG-1491](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1491/post-accept-ux-client-side-surface-flip-start-step-1-suggested-reply) introduced. ## Root cause (confirmed via console instrumentation, not guessed) `getMessageKey(message, index)` in `agentModeRenderHelpers.ts` returns `msg-${message.messageIndex ?? index}`. For the assistant's just-streamed message, `messageIndex` is `undefined` while it's still the live/optimistic SSE-streamed object, so the key falls back to its position in the CLIENT's in-memory array (e.g. `msg-1`, since the client array was just `[user, assistant]`). The moment `WorkPlanRecommendationCard`'s `handleAccept` calls `onRefreshSession()`, `refreshCurrentSession` refetches the FULL session from the server. The server's authoritative message array includes a leading system message the client-side optimistic array never had, AND assigns real `messageIndex` values reflecting the full stored history (observed: `messageIndex: 22`) — so the SAME logical assistant message's key changes from `msg-1` to `msg-22`. React sees a different key for the list item at that position and **unmounts + remounts** `ChatMessageItem` (and everything inside it, including `WorkPlanRecommendationCard`). The remounted card's `useState` initializer re-runs `isWorkPlanRecommendationAlreadyApplied(plan.id, activeWorkPlanTemplateId)` against the NOW-current `activeWorkPlanTemplateId` (which matches, since the accept just succeeded) — producing `{accepted, alreadyApplied: true}` from scratch, discarding the correct `{accepted, alreadyApplied: false}` state that was set a moment earlier from the real, fresh accept response. Confirmed via console trace (5 fresh test users, 100% reproduction): ``` RENDER {status: {"kind":"accepted","alreadyApplied":false}} <- correct, from real accept response getMessageKey {key: msg-1, messageIndex: undefined, index: 1, role: assistant} ... onRefreshSession fires ... getMessageKey {key: msg-22, messageIndex: 22, index: 2, role: assistant} <- KEY CHANGED MOUNT/init useState {activeWorkPlanTemplateId: , recommendationId: } <- REMOUNT RENDER {status: {"kind":"accepted","alreadyApplied":true}} <- wrong, wiped by remount ``` ## Why this isn't a quick fix `ChatMessage` (`types/agentMode.ts`) has no stable client-generated identifier — only `messageIndex` (undefined until server-confirmed) and `metadata.timestamp` (already documented in `getMessageKey`'s own comment as unreliable: "the optimistic user message picks a client-side timestamp and the backend echoes a different one when the response lands — same role, different key -> remount, which is the 'screen flashes black on first response' bug"). A correct fix needs a stable identity assigned at optimistic-creation time and preserved through the SSE-streaming and refresh-merge paths — touching the message type, the optimistic-message construction in the chat-send hook, and `refreshCurrentSession`'s merge logic. That's real design work on a shared, sensitive code path with a documented history of a similar regression, not a one-line patch — hence its own issue rather than folding into [ENG-1491](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1491/post-accept-ux-client-side-surface-flip-start-step-1-suggested-reply). ## Impact Affects ANY local component state inside a message rendered before its `messageIndex` resolves (not just workplan cards) — e.g. any future inline card with transient local UI state on a first-turn message. Currently the only KNOWN visible symptom is the workplan accept success message, but the mechanism is general. ## Acceptance criteria (draft — refine before implementation) 1. Accepting a workplan recommendation on the FIRST assistant turn of a session shows "Workplan started." (not "already active.") and it does not flip after the post-accept session refresh completes. 2. `ChatMessageItem` does not unmount/remount for a message whose only observed change is `messageIndex` resolving from `undefined` to a real value with an unchanged role/content. 3. No regression of the "screen flashes black on first response" bug this code's own history references — dev before/after transcript evidence recommended given the shared, sensitive code path. Not yet scoped into implementation tests — needs its own TDD pass once the exact stable-identity mechanism is designed.

ENG-1839 Landing-page subdomains over 46 chars can never get a TLS cert — 2 live customer pages unreachable while DB says deployed

## Summary Landing pages whose auto-generated subdomain label exceeds 46 characters get an `agentwebforms.com` FQDN longer than 64 characters. Vercel cannot issue a certificate for it, so the TLS handshake is closed and the page is unreachable in a browser (`ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED`), even though DNS resolves and the DB records `status: deployed`. Two live customer pages are currently affected. Neither has been reported through normal channels, because nothing in the product surfaces the failure — the record looks healthy. ## Reproduction / evidence DNS is fine; only TLS fails: ``` $ dig +short create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com cname.vercel-dns.com. 66.33.60.67 76.76.21.98 $ curl -sS https://create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL ... :443 ``` Tested across existing `*.agentwebforms.com` subdomains, the boundary tracks FQDN length, not label length: | FQDN length | Host | Result | | -- | -- | -- | | 28 | `pulseboard.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 34 | `forge-for-cursor.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 57 | `dramabreak-hidden-identity-underdog-fan.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 59 | `codex-live-smoke-2026-06-20t22-32-40-632z.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 77 | `build-a-single-page-pricing-focused-landing-page-called-pro.agentwebforms.com` | **TLS fail** | | 77 | `create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com` | **TLS fail** | ## Root cause The X.509 Common Name field is limited to 64 characters. Our validation is applied to the *label* only, and permits 63: * `backend/src/services/customDomainService.ts:74` — `if (subdomain.length > 63) throw ...` * same file, slug generator — `return slug.slice(0, 63)` But the certificate is issued for `label + "." + "agentwebforms.com"`, i.e. `label + 18` characters. A 63-character label produces an 81-character FQDN. **The safe maximum label is 46** (46 + 18 = 64). So any label between 47 and 63 characters passes our validation and then cannot get a certificate. The known-good ceiling observed in production is a 59-char FQDN (41-char label); the known-bad floor is 77. Exact boundary between 60 and 76 is not pinned — no existing subdomain falls in that range — but 64 is the documented CN limit and is consistent with every observation. ## Suggested fix 1. Validate the **FQDN**, not the label: reject when `label.length + 1 + SUBDOMAIN_BASE.length > 64`. 2. Change the generator's `slice(0, 63)` to derive its cap from `SUBDOMAIN_BASE` rather than hardcoding, so it stays correct if the apex domain changes. 3. Backfill the two affected pages onto short prefixes. 4. Consider surfacing cert-provisioning failure on the page record — both of these read `status: deployed` while being unreachable, which is why they went unnoticed. ## Affected pages | userId | FQDN | status | | -- | -- | -- | | `9ceb1a16` | `create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com` | deployed | | `58ad8518` | `build-a-single-page-pricing-focused-landing-page-called-pro.agentwebforms.com` | deployed | Found while investigating a customer escalation on the first of these (session `1f5cde39-6455-4f78-86a1-7bfcf8812ead`). The second appears unreported.

The mechanism it added is defeated by how requirements are counted: ```ts // controllers/agentModeController.ts:5965-5972 const requiredLinkedInCalls = functionCallMinCalls.linkedin_outreach || 1; const successfulLinkedInCalls = linkedInOutcomeToolCalls.filter( (call) => call?.name === 'linkedin_outreach' && toolCallSucceeded(call), ); const linkedInInviteSendRequirementMissed = Boolean( linkedInInviteSendBlock && heldToFunctionNames.includes('linkedin_outreach') && successfulLinkedInCalls.length < requiredLinkedInCalls, ); ``` Counting is by **tool name**, not by `action` — the in-code comment says this is deliberate ("successful non-invite LinkedIn calls count too"). So a run that made one successful `search-people` and had every `send-invite` blocked satisfies `min: 1`, `linkedInInviteSendRequirementMissed` stays false, `runDelivered` stays true, and **the run reports success.** Every schedule that sets the requirement today is defeated this way: of the 8 in production, 6 use `functionCallMinCalls: {}` (defaults to 1) and 2 use `{ linkedin_outreach: 1 }`. ## Second, narrower gap in the same path `LINKEDIN_INVITE_CAP_BLOCK_RE` (`:671`) matches cooldown and internal-pacing phrasings only. A run whose sends all failed — for **any** reason, cooldown or not — fails validation when `linkedin_outreach` is a required function. 3. Existing publish-equivalence credit (`utils/requiredCallSatisfaction.ts`, ENG-1045/ENG-1276) is untouched. 5. The warning is accurate. `listSpendEvents` (`backend/src/services/spendEventDb.ts:358`) pages the GSI until `LastEvaluatedKey` is exhausted, with no cap and no cursor, and this PR is what makes that path reachable from a UI. Resolving a member to the billing root widens it further, exactly as the check says.

**Why not truncate here: you cannot truncate a sum and still call it a sum.** Every headline on this screen — settled spend, in-flight, the daily trend, each slice — is an aggregate over the full month. Capping the fetch would silently understate all of them, and an understated spend figure on a screen used to explain a pause is materially worse than a slow one. A truncating read has to come with either a server-side aggregate (sum on the server, page only the detail rows) or an explicit "too large to summarise" error — both real work on an endpoint that shipped in #2811, not in this diff.

**Current magnitude, so this is not a guess:** the ledger began writing on 2026-09-07 and ENG-1250 measured system-wide growth at ~546 rows/day across *all* billing subjects. One subject-month is presently tens to low hundreds of events — the render cap removes the practical symptom, and the fetch is not yet a problem. It will become one, which is why it is being filed rather than dismissed.

ENG-1839 Landing-page subdomains over 46 chars can never get a TLS cert — 3 live customer pages unreachable while DB says deployed

## Summary Landing pages whose auto-generated subdomain label exceeds 46 characters get an `agentwebforms.com` FQDN longer than 64 characters. Vercel cannot issue a certificate for it, so the TLS handshake is closed and the page is unreachable in a browser (`ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED`), even though DNS resolves and the DB records `status: deployed`. Two live customer pages are currently affected. Neither has been reported through normal channels, because nothing in the product surfaces the failure — the record looks healthy. ## Reproduction / evidence DNS is fine; only TLS fails: ``` $ dig +short create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com cname.vercel-dns.com. 66.33.60.67 76.76.21.98 $ curl -sS https://create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL ... :443 ``` Tested across existing `*.agentwebforms.com` subdomains, the boundary tracks FQDN length, not label length: | FQDN length | Host | Result | | -- | -- | -- | | 28 | `pulseboard.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 34 | `forge-for-cursor.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 57 | `dramabreak-hidden-identity-underdog-fan.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 59 | `codex-live-smoke-2026-06-20t22-32-40-632z.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 77 | `build-a-single-page-pricing-focused-landing-page-called-pro.agentwebforms.com` | **TLS fail** | | 77 | `create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com` | **TLS fail** | ## Root cause The X.509 Common Name field is limited to 64 characters. Our validation is applied to the *label* only, and permits 63: * `backend/src/services/customDomainService.ts:74` — `if (subdomain.length > 63) throw ...` * same file, slug generator — `return slug.slice(0, 63)` But the certificate is issued for `label + "." + "agentwebforms.com"`, i.e. `label + 18` characters. A 63-character label produces an 81-character FQDN. **The safe maximum label is 46** (46 + 18 = 64). So any label between 47 and 63 characters passes our validation and then cannot get a certificate. The known-good ceiling observed in production is a 59-char FQDN (41-char label); the known-bad floor is 77. Exact boundary between 60 and 76 is not pinned — no existing subdomain falls in that range — but 64 is the documented CN limit and is consistent with every observation. ## Suggested fix 1. Validate the **FQDN**, not the label: reject when `label.length + 1 + SUBDOMAIN_BASE.length > 64`. 2. Change the generator's `slice(0, 63)` to derive its cap from `SUBDOMAIN_BASE` rather than hardcoding, so it stays correct if the apex domain changes. 3. Backfill the two affected pages onto short prefixes. 4. Consider surfacing cert-provisioning failure on the page record — both of these read `status: deployed` while being unreachable, which is why they went unnoticed. ## Affected pages | userId | FQDN | status | | -- | -- | -- | | `9ceb1a16` | `create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com` | deployed | | `58ad8518` | `build-a-single-page-pricing-focused-landing-page-called-pro.agentwebforms.com` | deployed | Found while investigating a customer escalation on the first of these (session `1f5cde39-6455-4f78-86a1-7bfcf8812ead`). The second appears unreported. --- ## Correction (2026-09-09): three affected records, not two A dry-run of the repair script against production finds **three** over-length domain records. The third was missed by the original scan, which filtered on `AW-LandingPages.customDomainUrl` hosts — that page stores a *short* host with a long path, while a separate over-length record exists for it in `AW-CustomDomains`. That table is the authoritative list. | domainId | userId | FQDN | len | | -- | -- | -- | -- | | `6f5e0a2d…` | `58ad8518…` | `build-a-single-page-pricing-focused-landing-page-called-pro…` | 77 | | `37138169…` | `9ceb1a16…` | `create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic…` | 77 | | `2b08cb6f…` | `9fde4157…` | `premium-dark-landing-page-for-open-future-forum-forum-sel…` | 75 | The third belongs to a customer who has not reported it. Its own subdomain fails TLS, and its page's stored URL returns 404 while that host's root returns 200 — I have not established that the 404 and the TLS failure share a cause. ## Scope — remaining work after the length fix - ☑ Stop new over-length subdomains being minted (agentweb#2840) - ☑ Client-side guard so the portal's delete-then-create cannot strand a page (customer-portal#1159) - ☑ Repair script for the three existing records (agentweb#2840, `repair-overlong-subdomains.ts`) - ☐ **Run the repair** — data-plane, needs approval and a human-chosen prefix per record - ☐ **Surface cert-provisioning failure in the UI** — see below. This ticket is not done when the length fix ships. ## Why the surfacing item matters (folded in rather than filed separately) The length fix removes **one** cause. Cert issuance also fails from DNS misconfiguration, pending verification, a customer's apex not pointed at Vercel, and Vercel-side limits — every one of them fails identically silently, which is why this went unnoticed for months. The detection already exists and is already routed: `verifyDomain()` checks Vercel's `verified` flag *and* whether DNS resolves (`isDomainMisconfigured`), and writes `status: active` when healthy. It is on-demand only, and nothing calls it proactively — so **all 58 records in** `AW-CustomDomains` **currently read** `status: active`**, including all three that fail TLS.** The field carries no signal. This is therefore wiring, not a feature build: run the existing check on a schedule (or on landing-pages list read), let it write the true status, and render the non-active state on the page card where a status badge already exists. --- ## Correction (2026-09-10): first surfacing attempt was wrong, reverted, being redone The surfacing work was built and then **pulled from agentweb#2840**, because it could not detect this bug. `verifyDomain` reads exactly two signals — Vercel's `verified` flag (ownership) and `misconfigured` from `/v6/domains//config` (does DNS point at Vercel). Neither fails for an over-length domain. Checked against all three broken records: each resolves correctly to `cname.vercel-dns.com` / `66.33.60.129`, so `misconfigured` is false and ownership is inherent for our own apex. The pipeline reported all three as **healthy**. Shipping it would have been worse than shipping nothing: a warning system whose silence means "not actually checked" trains people to read silence as verified. It also carried a live hazard. `isDomainMisconfigured` returns `true` on ANY thrown error (429, 5xx, timeout). Harmless while the result could only withhold an upgrade; once it drove a write, a transient Vercel blip would have persisted a false "unreachable" and shown the customer a wrong reason. ### The replacement design **Signal — reachability, not configuration.** Attempt a real HTTPS request and classify: | Outcome | Verdict | | -- | -- | | 2xx / 3xx | reachable | | TLS handshake failure | unhealthy — certificate could not be issued (definitive, not transient) | | DNS resolution failure | unhealthy — DNS | | Timeout / network error | **inconclusive — persist nothing** | The last row is the fix for the hazard above: only a definitive negative is ever written. **Mechanism — scheduled sweep, not a user request.** Uses the existing `setInterval` + `isCronEnabled()` + `cronJobRegistry.track` pattern.
