ENG-1839 Landing-page subdomains over 46 chars can never get a TLS cert — 3 live customer pages unreachable while DB says deployed

## Summary Landing pages whose auto-generated subdomain label exceeds 46 characters get an `agentwebforms.com` FQDN longer than 64 characters. Vercel cannot issue a certificate for it, so the TLS handshake is closed and the page is unreachable in a browser (`ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED`), even though DNS resolves and the DB records `status: deployed`. Two live customer pages are currently affected. Neither has been reported through normal channels, because nothing in the product surfaces the failure — the record looks healthy. ## Reproduction / evidence DNS is fine; only TLS fails: ``` $ dig +short create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com cname.vercel-dns.com. 66.33.60.67 76.76.21.98 $ curl -sS https://create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL ... :443 ``` Tested across existing `*.agentwebforms.com` subdomains, the boundary tracks FQDN length, not label length: | FQDN length | Host | Result | | -- | -- | -- | | 28 | `pulseboard.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 34 | `forge-for-cursor.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 57 | `dramabreak-hidden-identity-underdog-fan.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 59 | `codex-live-smoke-2026-06-20t22-32-40-632z.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 77 | `build-a-single-page-pricing-focused-landing-page-called-pro.agentwebforms.com` | **TLS fail** | | 77 | `create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com` | **TLS fail** | ## Root cause The X.509 Common Name field is limited to 64 characters. Our validation is applied to the *label* only, and permits 63: * `backend/src/services/customDomainService.ts:74` — `if (subdomain.length > 63) throw ...` * same file, slug generator — `return slug.slice(0, 63)` But the certificate is issued for `label + "." + "agentwebforms.com"`, i.e. `label + 18` characters. A 63-character label produces an 81-character FQDN. **The safe maximum label is 46** (46 + 18 = 64). So any label between 47 and 63 characters passes our validation and then cannot get a certificate. The known-good ceiling observed in production is a 59-char FQDN (41-char label); the known-bad floor is 77. Exact boundary between 60 and 76 is not pinned — no existing subdomain falls in that range — but 64 is the documented CN limit and is consistent with every observation. ## Suggested fix 1. Validate the **FQDN**, not the label: reject when `label.length + 1 + SUBDOMAIN_BASE.length > 64`. 2. Change the generator's `slice(0, 63)` to derive its cap from `SUBDOMAIN_BASE` rather than hardcoding, so it stays correct if the apex domain changes. 3. Backfill the two affected pages onto short prefixes. 4. Consider surfacing cert-provisioning failure on the page record — both of these read `status: deployed` while being unreachable, which is why they went unnoticed. ## Affected pages | userId | FQDN | status | | -- | -- | -- | | `9ceb1a16` | `create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com` | deployed | | `58ad8518` | `build-a-single-page-pricing-focused-landing-page-called-pro.agentwebforms.com` | deployed | Found while investigating a customer escalation on the first of these (session `1f5cde39-6455-4f78-86a1-7bfcf8812ead`). The second appears unreported. --- ## Correction (2026-09-09): three affected records, not two A dry-run of the repair script against production finds **three** over-length domain records. The third was missed by the original scan, which filtered on `AW-LandingPages.customDomainUrl` hosts — that page stores a *short* host with a long path, while a separate over-length record exists for it in `AW-CustomDomains`. That table is the authoritative list. | domainId | userId | FQDN | len | | -- | -- | -- | -- | | `6f5e0a2d…` | `58ad8518…` | `build-a-single-page-pricing-focused-landing-page-called-pro…` | 77 | | `37138169…` | `9ceb1a16…` | `create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic…` | 77 | | `2b08cb6f…` | `9fde4157…` | `premium-dark-landing-page-for-open-future-forum-forum-sel…` | 75 | The third belongs to a customer who has not reported it. Its own subdomain fails TLS, and its page's stored URL returns 404 while that host's root returns 200 — I have not established that the 404 and the TLS failure share a cause. ## Scope — remaining work after the length fix - ☑ Stop new over-length subdomains being minted (agentweb#2840) - ☑ Client-side guard so the portal's delete-then-create cannot strand a page (customer-portal#1159) - ☑ Repair script for the three existing records (agentweb#2840, `repair-overlong-subdomains.ts`) - ☐ **Run the repair** — data-plane, needs approval and a human-chosen prefix per record - ☐ **Surface cert-provisioning failure in the UI** — see below. This ticket is not done when the length fix ships. ## Why the surfacing item matters (folded in rather than filed separately) The length fix removes **one** cause. Cert issuance also fails from DNS misconfiguration, pending verification, a customer's apex not pointed at Vercel, and Vercel-side limits — every one of them fails identically silently, which is why this went unnoticed for months. The detection already exists and is already routed: `verifyDomain()` checks Vercel's `verified` flag *and* whether DNS resolves (`isDomainMisconfigured`), and writes `status: active` when healthy. It is on-demand only, and nothing calls it proactively — so **all 58 records in** `AW-CustomDomains` **currently read** `status: active`**, including all three that fail TLS.** The field carries no signal. This is therefore wiring, not a feature build: run the existing check on a schedule (or on landing-pages list read), let it write the true status, and render the non-active state on the page card where a status badge already exists. --- ## Correction (2026-09-10): first surfacing attempt was wrong, reverted, being redone The surfacing work was built and then **pulled from agentweb#2840**, because it could not detect this bug. `verifyDomain` reads exactly two signals — Vercel's `verified` flag (ownership) and `misconfigured` from `/v6/domains//config` (does DNS point at Vercel). Neither fails for an over-length domain. Checked against all three broken records: each resolves correctly to `cname.vercel-dns.com` / `66.33.60.129`, so `misconfigured` is false and ownership is inherent for our own apex. The pipeline reported all three as **healthy**. Shipping it would have been worse than shipping nothing: a warning system whose silence means "not actually checked" trains people to read silence as verified. It also carried a live hazard. `isDomainMisconfigured` returns `true` on ANY thrown error (429, 5xx, timeout). Harmless while the result could only withhold an upgrade; once it drove a write, a transient Vercel blip would have persisted a false "unreachable" and shown the customer a wrong reason. ### The replacement design **Signal — reachability, not configuration.** Attempt a real HTTPS request and classify: | Outcome | Verdict | | -- | -- | | 2xx / 3xx | reachable | | TLS handshake failure | unhealthy — certificate could not be issued (definitive, not transient) | | DNS resolution failure | unhealthy — DNS | | Timeout / network error | **inconclusive — persist nothing** | The last row is the fix for the hazard above: only a definitive negative is ever written. **Mechanism — scheduled sweep, not a user request.** Uses the existing `setInterval` + `isCronEnabled()` + `cronJobRegistry.track` pattern. This removes the thundering-herd problem of the reverted version (which fired from a list read that the portal polls every 10s), adds an explicit request timeout, and stamps the check time even on failure so a record cannot become permanently stale. **Scope — domains backing a** `deployed` **page only.** Not cost: at 58 records a full sweep is trivial. It is signal quality — a domain whose page is still building will fail a probe, and that failure is expected. A monitor that reports expected failures gets ignored, which is the same way the original bug survived. Orphaned domains (attached to Vercel, backing no page) are a separate signal and are already detected by `repair-overlong-subdomains.ts`. Surfacing (list-route fields + portal warning) was not the problem and returns unchanged once something real feeds it.

Discovered live-testing ENG-1813 on production (2026-09-08): asked Emma to "remove steps 2&3, then stop and tell me it's done, do not do any further work this turn." Turn 1 correctly stopped and said "It's done!" -- then a second, fully autonomous turn fired anyway and kept working, contradicting the explicit stop instruction. Visually this also looks like "1 prompt -> 2 disconnected responses" in the customer-portal UI, since the injected continuation prompt is deliberately hidden from the chat UI (metadata.kind === 'auto-continuation'). This is NOT a bug in ENG-1813 (already merged/deployed) -- it's a pre-existing gap in the older ENG-1239/ENG-1684 auto-continuation mechanism that ENG-1813's live-test happened to newly exercise (ENG-1813 added one more condition -- unresolved debt -- that can trigger the same pre-existing continuation loop). Three things need fixing, all WITHOUT regressing ENG-1684's real fix: 1. Emma should honor an explicit "stop / don't do more work" instruction from the user, even on an autocomplete plan -- currently the continuation-fire decision has zero awareness of user intent, purely mechanical (plan/tool-call/debt state only). 2. The UI should show the real second prompt, not hide it -- current design makes 2 genuinely separate turns look like 1 prompt with 2 disconnected responses. 3. Do NOT restrict firing to "timeout only" -- ENG-1684's own original incident (session 7a9772f6) was NOT a timeout (a turn ended normally, said "please retry", sat idle 3h16m) -- restricting to timeout-only would reopen that exact bug. ## Full design discussion and verified findings (2026-09-08) **Origin tickets:** ENG-1239 (assignee: Manan Varma, creator: Harsha Vankayalapati, created 2026-08-14, "Image-generation batches hit the agent turn limit and leave requested creatives unfinished", Done) -- the original media-continuation mechanism, Manan built it. ENG-1684 (unassigned, creator: Harsha Vankayalapati, created 2026-09-01, "Autocomplete work plans stall waiting for human nudge instead of self-continuing", Done) -- extended the same pattern to work plans, explicitly for BOTH timeout and non-timeout stalls. **Agreed reconciled design:** keep the existing non-timeout stall check (preserves ENG-1684's real fix), add a NEW async veto check -- "did the user's most recent real message explicitly ask to stop" -- that suppresses firing when true. Checked only on the rare path where the system has ALREADY decided to auto-continue (not on every turn, not on every autocomplete-plan turn). **LLM-only, no regex** -- explicit user decision. Reasoning: this codebase's existing pattern for the opposite-direction check (scheduledTurnDefersToUser, agentModeController.ts ~3416) uses a regex fast-path + LLM-judge fallback, because "the model invents a new phrasing on nearly every run." But a false-negative here (missing an explicit stop) is worse than that case's false-negative (one extra retry) -- it means silently disobeying an explicit instruction. A naive regex would also false-positive on unrelated content mentioning "stop" in a non-instructional sense. So: pure LLM classifier, same cheap/fast model tier as existing judges (gemini-3.1-flash-lite, ~8s timeout budget), fail-SAFE meaning on error/timeout default to NOT suppressing (preserves ENG-1684's guarantee even if the classifier itself fails). **Cost, precisely characterized:** one extra LLM call + one extra DB read, BOTH only incurred on the already-rare "continuation about to fire" path (autocomplete plan + already-stalled state) -- not per user prompt, not per ordinary turn. Comparable-or-lower frequency than the ALREADY-ACCEPTED scheduledTurnDefersToUser judge call. **Correct insertion point (verified via full call-graph trace, NOT the 4-sites design first assumed):** there is exactly ONE place AUTO_WORK_PLAN_CONTINUATION_MESSAGE ever gets injected -- inside scheduleAutoWorkPlanContinuation (agentModeController.ts, function starts ~line 1473), right after its OWN existing pre-fire re-check (~lines 1576-1584) passes, BEFORE the generateSessionResponse(...) call (~line 1587). Every other call site (round-1 dispatch at ~9052/9147-ish, round-N+1 recursive dispatch at ~1662) just calls INTO this one function -- they don't fire independently. Placing the veto here means it re-evaluates fresh on EVERY round (the function re-reads session state each time), giving a nice self-correcting property for free: a user who says "stop" mid-chain gets caught on the very next round's check, automatically. **Data-source problem found:** `currentSession` at that exact point comes from chatbotDb.getChatSessionRecord(sessionId) (chatbotService.ts ~1785) -- confirmed via its own doc comment this does NOT carry real message history ("messages on the returned record is the raw stored value, usually absent... callers that need the real conversation must use getChatSession"). This is a DELIBERATE existing optimization (avoid the message-table read/migration cost) that the new check would need to work around. **Cheaper alternative found and validated (better than swapping to full getChatSession):** reuse the exact pattern of chatbotService.ts's existing getSessionPreview (~line 1260-1274) -- a BOUNDED DynamoDB Query with Limit (not the unbounded paginate-everything getMessagesFromMessagesTable). For "last N messages" specifically: ScanIndexForward: false, Limit: ~10-20, then walk that small result set for the most recent role==='user' message whose metadata?.kind !== 'auto-continuation'. Confirmed valid against the REAL AW-ChatMessages table key schema (verified via `aws dynamodb describe-table`): sessionId (HASH) + messageIndex (RANGE) -- so a reverse-sorted limited query is a correct, cheap, direct-index read, not a scan. **Metadata field verified precisely (both directions):** `metadata.kind === 'auto-continuation'` -- confirmed live from a real production session's raw message (d663ff2d-a26d-4c23-a8e4-a0b59e9d0352, message index 18) AND from the write path (agentModeController.ts ~7795: `...(userMessageKind ? { kind: userMessageKind } : {})`). **Existing UX precedent found (strong signal for design):** when auto-continuation gives up after AUTO_WORK_PLAN_CONTINUATION_MAX_ROUNDS, it does NOT go silent -- it persists a VISIBLE assistant message explaining why (agentModeController.ts ~1484-1495: "I wasn't able to finish this plan automatically... Reply here whenever you're ready"). Strong precedent that the new stop-check branch should ALSO emit an acknowledgment when it suppresses firing, not just silently return. **Critical correctness requirement identified:** the new branch sits in the SAME post-lock-claim region as the existing pre-fire bail-out (~1576-1584, which does autoContinuationSessions.delete(sessionId) + releaseSessionGeneration(sessionId) on bail). The new branch MUST replicate this exact cleanup or the session gets stuck thinking generation is still in-flight, blocking all future turns. **Existing test coverage found, NOT yet fully read:** 554 lines in agentModeController.workPlanAutoContinuation.test.ts (10 named tests: MAX_ROUNDS cap + graceful message, usage-allowance gate, "recheck runs on round 1 too, not only on recursive rounds", fails-open on pre-fire-recheck read failure, lock-release ordering, generation-timeout interaction, does-not-double-fire-alongside-media-deferral, etc.) plus references in agentModeController.stalledAutocompletePlan.test.ts and agentModeController.autoMediaContinuation.test.ts. ENG-1839 Landing-page subdomains over 46 chars can never get a TLS cert — 3 live customer pages unreachable while DB says deployed

## Summary Landing pages whose auto-generated subdomain label exceeds 46 characters get an `agentwebforms.com` FQDN longer than 64 characters. Vercel cannot issue a certificate for it, so the TLS handshake is closed and the page is unreachable in a browser (`ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED`), even though DNS resolves and the DB records `status: deployed`. Two live customer pages are currently affected. Neither has been reported through normal channels, because nothing in the product surfaces the failure — the record looks healthy. ## Reproduction / evidence DNS is fine; only TLS fails: ``` $ dig +short create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com cname.vercel-dns.com. 66.33.60.67 76.76.21.98 $ curl -sS https://create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL ... :443 ``` Tested across existing `*.agentwebforms.com` subdomains, the boundary tracks FQDN length, not label length: | FQDN length | Host | Result | | -- | -- | -- | | 28 | `pulseboard.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 34 | `forge-for-cursor.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 57 | `dramabreak-hidden-identity-underdog-fan.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 59 | `codex-live-smoke-2026-06-20t22-32-40-632z.agentwebforms.com` | 200 | | 77 | `build-a-single-page-pricing-focused-landing-page-called-pro.agentwebforms.com` | **TLS fail** | | 77 | `create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com` | **TLS fail** | ## Root cause The X.509 Common Name field is limited to 64 characters. Our validation is applied to the *label* only, and permits 63: * `backend/src/services/customDomainService.ts:74` — `if (subdomain.length > 63) throw ...` * same file, slug generator — `return slug.slice(0, 63)` But the certificate is issued for `label + "." + "agentwebforms.com"`, i.e. `label + 18` characters. A 63-character label produces an 81-character FQDN. **The safe maximum label is 46** (46 + 18 = 64). So any label between 47 and 63 characters passes our validation and then cannot get a certificate. The known-good ceiling observed in production is a 59-char FQDN (41-char label); the known-bad floor is 77. Exact boundary between 60 and 76 is not pinned — no existing subdomain falls in that range — but 64 is the documented CN limit and is consistent with every observation. ## Suggested fix 1. Validate the **FQDN**, not the label: reject when `label.length + 1 + SUBDOMAIN_BASE.length > 64`. 2. Change the generator's `slice(0, 63)` to derive its cap from `SUBDOMAIN_BASE` rather than hardcoding, so it stays correct if the apex domain changes. 3. Backfill the two affected pages onto short prefixes. 4. Consider surfacing cert-provisioning failure on the page record — both of these read `status: deployed` while being unreachable, which is why they went unnoticed. ## Affected pages | userId | FQDN | status | | -- | -- | -- | | `9ceb1a16` | `create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com` | deployed | | `58ad8518` | `build-a-single-page-pricing-focused-landing-page-called-pro.agentwebforms.com` | deployed | Found while investigating a customer escalation on the first of these (session `1f5cde39-6455-4f78-86a1-7bfcf8812ead`). The second appears unreported. --- ## Correction (2026-09-09): three affected records, not two A dry-run of the repair script against production finds **three** over-length domain records. The third was missed by the original scan, which filtered on `AW-LandingPages.customDomainUrl` hosts — that page stores a *short* host with a long path, while a separate over-length record exists for it in `AW-CustomDomains`. That table is the authoritative list. | domainId | userId | FQDN | len | | -- | -- | -- | -- | | `6f5e0a2d…` | `58ad8518…` | `build-a-single-page-pricing-focused-landing-page-called-pro…` | 77 | | `37138169…` | `9ceb1a16…` | `create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic…` | 77 | | `2b08cb6f…` | `9fde4157…` | `premium-dark-landing-page-for-open-future-forum-forum-sel…` | 75 | The third belongs to a customer who has not reported it. Its own subdomain fails TLS, and its page's stored URL returns 404 while that host's root returns 200 — I have not established that the 404 and the TLS failure share a cause. ## Scope — remaining work after the length fix - ☑ Stop new over-length subdomains being minted (agentweb#2840) - ☑ Client-side guard so the portal's delete-then-create cannot strand a page (customer-portal#1159) - ☑ Repair script for the three existing records (agentweb#2840, `repair-overlong-subdomains.ts`) - ☐ **Run the repair** — data-plane, needs approval and a human-chosen prefix per record - ☐ **Surface cert-provisioning failure in the UI** — see below. This ticket is not done when the length fix ships. ## Why the surfacing item matters (folded in rather than filed separately) The length fix removes **one** cause. Cert issuance also fails from DNS misconfiguration, pending verification, a customer's apex not pointed at Vercel, and Vercel-side limits — every one of them fails identically silently, which is why this went unnoticed for months. The detection already exists and is already routed: `verifyDomain()` checks Vercel's `verified` flag *and* whether DNS resolves (`isDomainMisconfigured`), and writes `status: active` when healthy. It is on-demand only, and nothing calls it proactively — so **all 58 records in** `AW-CustomDomains` **currently read** `status: active`**, including all three that fail TLS.** The field carries no signal. This is therefore wiring, not a feature build: run the existing check on a schedule (or on landing-pages list read), let it write the true status, and render the non-active state on the page card where a status badge already exists. --- ## Correction (2026-09-10): first surfacing attempt was wrong, reverted, being redone The surfacing work was built and then **pulled from agentweb#2840**, because it could not detect this bug. `verifyDomain` reads exactly two signals — Vercel's `verified` flag (ownership) and `misconfigured` from `/v6/domains//config` (does DNS point at Vercel). Neither fails for an over-length domain. Checked against all three broken records: each resolves correctly to `cname.vercel-dns.com` / `66.33.60.129`, so `misconfigured` is false and ownership is inherent for our own apex. The pipeline reported all three as **healthy**. Shipping it would have been worse than shipping nothing: a warning system whose silence means "not actually checked" trains people to read silence as verified. It also carried a live hazard. `isDomainMisconfigured` returns `true` on ANY thrown error (429, 5xx, timeout). Harmless while the result could only withhold an upgrade; once it drove a write, a transient Vercel blip would have persisted a false "unreachable" and shown the customer a wrong reason. ### The replacement design **Signal — reachability, not configuration.** Attempt a real HTTPS request and classify: | Outcome | Verdict | | -- | -- | | 2xx / 3xx | reachable | | TLS handshake failure | unhealthy — certificate could not be issued (definitive, not transient) | | DNS resolution failure | unhealthy — DNS | | Timeout / network error | **inconclusive — persist nothing** | The last row is the fix for the hazard above: only a definitive negative is ever written. **Mechanism — scheduled sweep, not a user request.** Uses the existing `setInterval` + `isCronEnabled()` + `cronJobRegistry.track` pattern. This removes the thundering-herd problem of the reverted version (which fired from a list read that the portal polls every 10s), adds an explicit request timeout, and stamps the check time even on failure so a record cannot become permanently stale. **Scope — domains backing a** `deployed` **page only.** Not cost: at 58 records a full sweep is trivial. It is signal quality — a domain whose page is still building will fail a probe, and that failure is expected. A monitor that reports expected failures gets ignored, which is the same way the original bug survived. Orphaned domains (attached to Vercel, backing no page) are a separate signal and are already detected by `repair-overlong-subdomains.ts`. Surfacing (list-route fields + portal warning) was not the problem and returns unchanged once something real feeds it.

ENG-1856 Publish Tests-gate bypass fails when ANY non-Tests check run exists (e.g. Vercel bot comment) — re-blocks publish forever

The #2846 fix (ENG-1488) skips the required-Tests gate only when a repo has ZERO check runs of any kind AND zero GitHub Actions workflows (landingPageGeneration.ts, the noCiAtAll / checkRuns.length===0 condition). Live-tested tonight on a real generated repo (AgentWebPro/lp-create-a-high-converting-mobil-f80e1869, draft/agentweb-preview): actions/workflows total_count is 0 (confirmed — generated repos genuinely have no CI), but check-runs on the commit returns exactly one entry: "Vercel Preview Comments" (a bot posting the preview link, unrelated to tests), status completed. Because checkRuns.length is 1 (not 0), the workflow-count lookup never runs, noCiAtAll stays false, and publish returns 409 required_tests_pending — "has not started for this draft yet" — which will NEVER become true, since no workflow can ever produce a Tests check. This reproduces the exact original unsatisfiable-gate bug, just triggered by a harmless bot check instead of zero check runs. Likely broadly blocking, not Vincent-specific — any generated repo with a Vercel preview-comment check (probably most of them) would hit this on every publish attempt. Suggest: only consult workflowCount on the absence of a literal "Tests" check, not on checkRuns.length===0 — or explicitly exclude known non-test bot checks (Vercel's app) from the checkRuns.length gate.

A transient OpenRouter failure (429/network/5xx) that survives OpenRouter's own provider fallback is retried once by AgentWeb before failing the turn. 2. The retry is bounded (exactly one attempt) and does not multiply with OpenRouter's SDK-level fallback (`maxRetries` stays 0). 3. A non-transient failure (e.g. 402 insufficient balance, 401 auth) still fails immediately with no wasted retry. ENG-1836 Auto-created outreach schedules cannot be edited — updateScheduledChat 400s on the empty emailNotifications they ship with

Auto-created outreach schedules are created with `emailNotifications: []` (`outreachScheduleAutoCreate.ts`). `updateScheduledChat` rejects any edit that does not supply at least one: ``` PUT /api/agent-mode/scheduled-chats/60c5c825-… body: { nextRunTime: "…" } -> 400 {"error":"At least one email notification is required for scheduled chats"} ``` Reproduced in production 2026-09-09 on a schedule created by the live ENG-1723 auto-create path. ## Why it matters The whole premise of ENG-1723 is that the customer never asked for this schedule — the system made it for them at onboarding. The first thing many will want to do is adjust it: narrow the ICP, change the cadence, rename it. Every one of those edits returns a 400 until they also supply an email address they never chose to give, for notifications they never asked for. Editing is not the only affected path — anything that goes through `updateScheduledChat` inherits the same validation. ## Options 1. **Auto-create seeds the owner's email** — `emailNotifications: [ownerEmail]`. Simplest, and matches what a customer creating a schedule by hand would get. Downside: opts them into result emails they did not request. 2. **Relax the validation for an unchanged empty list** — only require an email when the field is being *set*, so an existing `[]` can be preserved. Keeps the no-email default intact. 3. **Auto-create is exempt** — keyed off `autoCreatedFromTemplateId`. Option 2 looks cleanest: it fixes editing without silently subscribing anyone to email. But it touches shared validation, so it deserves a deliberate decision rather than a drive-by change — which is why this is filed rather than fixed inline. Found while re-verifying ENG-1723 after the `variableValuesUpdatedAt` defect.

A failed post-deploy smoke and explicit `metaTrackingInstalled=false` do not prevent the page from being described as launch-ready. 4. Manual repo edits can install a base pixel without atomically syncing the capture route, form event ID/helper call, page metadata, custom-domain mapping, and smoke result. 5. The Meta paid-campaign gate ([ENG-941](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-941/meta-campaign-launch-has-no-pre-flight-tracking-gate-the-eng-335)) protects campaign activation, but it does not stop a partially instrumented site from being handed off as “live/ready,” and it cannot repair that site. ## Immediate mitigation completed PR [https://github.com/AgentWebPro/lp-create-a-high-converting-mobil-f80e1869/pull/11:]() * browser `Lead` and server CAPI share one `eventId` * capture route carries pixel `2304531030357543` and account `2041725529929988` * UTM, `gclid`, `fbclid`, and campaign/ad identifiers propagate into voice/text agent links * production build and Vercel deployment passed * production HTML/bundles verified for base pixel, agent attribution code, and voice/text targets * `AW-LandingPages` metadata repaired to match the production domain and tracking configuration One real lead or Meta Test Events run is still required to verify `events_received` and browser/server dedup in production; the synthetic CRM smoke marker intentionally suppresses CAPI side effects. ## Preventive acceptance contract 1. Attaching/changing a production custom domain must update `AW-LandingPages.customDomainUrl` through the same path. 6. A newly deployed page with failed smoke or unresolved tracking must alert immediately; do not rely only on the weekly rotation that powers [ENG-1400](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1400/4-generated-landing-pages-cannot-report-conversions-across-4-customers). 7. ENG-1877 createHtmlFromTemplate does not escape HTML — stored XSS via campaign/CRM data

**Confirmed live, not theoretical.** `createHtmlFromTemplate` (`backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts:31484`, prompt built at lines 31590-31623) substitutes `{{variable}}` placeholders into HTML templates via an LLM call — `variableValues`/`arrayVariableValues` are `JSON.stringify`'d raw into the prompt with zero escaping instruction, and the model copies them in verbatim. **Proven exploitable with real data.** Pulled real, currently-active campaign names from a real Meta account live via the Graph API — they already contain double quotes, apostrophes, and an em-dash (e.g. `Post: "Most Employer of Record providers ask you to..."`, `Every.io — Lead Gen (Landing Pages)`). Ran a deliberately adversarial payload through the real function on test-env1 (`campaigns_n_name: [' & "Sale" Bold']`) — the rendered S3-hosted HTML output contained the ` & "Sale" Bold ``` That's a static `.html` file served from S3 and opened directly in a browser as "a clickable link" — the script executes on load. **Real cross-user attack surface, not just self-XSS.** A customer names their own Meta campaign (or any other field an LLM-generated report pulls in) with an embedded script, an admin later reviews that customer's account and opens the generated report — the script runs in the *admin's* browser session, not the customer's. **Scope.** This is a property of the shared substitution engine, used by every HTML template on the platform today (found while building ENG-1552's new template, but not introduced by it or specific to it — ENG-1552's PRs don't touch this function at all). **Recommended fix.** HTML-escape every string value in `variableValues`/`arrayVariableValues` before they're interpolated into the LLM prompt (not after — the LLM regenerates the whole HTML, so there's no clean way to tell substituted values apart from static template markup after the fact). Small, contained code change (~20-30 lines, one helper + applying it before the prompt is built, single file). **Real unknown to check first, not assumed:** whether any existing template intentionally relies on raw/unescaped HTML being passed through a variable value — unlikely given the system's own design intent, but should be verified against real existing templates before shipping, not assumed. **Estimated effort:** code change is small, but full rigor (tests + independent review + merge + the ~20-25min EB deploy wait + a real live re-verification against prod using the same adversarial technique) means real wall-clock time is closer to an hour+, not a 5-minute patch — consistent with every other small-diff fix this session.

ENG-1874 Admin spend ledger divides vendor-only spend by the LLM allowance

## What is wrong The admin spend ledger ([ENG-1838](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1838), live on production) shows a billing subject's **settled spend** beside their **usable allowance**, a **remaining** figure, and a **"% of allowance committed"**. Those two numbers have different bases: * **Numerator** — `AW-SpendEvents`, which holds **vendor spend only**. * **Denominator** — `resolveAllowanceInputs` → `llmUsagePolicy.hardCostThresholdMicroUsd`, the tier's **LLM** cost cap. So the panel can render **"Remaining $199.93 · 0.0% of allowance committed"** for an account whose LLM spend has already consumed most of that same $200. Observed exactly that on production, 2026-09-10, for the `founders@agentweb.pro` billing subject: ledger settled **$0.0745** (apollo + [you.com]()) against a **$200.00** allowance, reported as 0.0% committed — while that subject's LLM spend over a comparable window runs into the hundreds of dollars. ## Why the ledger is vendor-only Verified in code on `main` @ `914305e6a` (2026-09-11), not inferred. `AW-SpendEvents` has exactly two writers: | Writer | Call site | Enclosing function | | -- | -- | -- | | `usageRecordDb.incrementUsageWithSpendEvent` | `usageRecorderService.ts:296` | `recordVendorUsageIdempotent` | | `mirrorVendorUsage` | `usageRecorderService.ts:458` | `recordVendorUsageLegacy` | **Both are inside** `recordVendorUsage*`**.** The LLM path (`recordUsage`) calls plain `incrementUsage` and stops. [ENG-1804](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1804)'s own title scopes it that way — *"dual-write metered **vendor** usage"* — so this is a known boundary, not a regression. [ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250) §1 asks for every AgentWeb-paid call and §6 lists LLM providers first among the slices to bring onto the rail; that slice is unbuilt. ## Why it matters beyond cosmetics The screen exists to **explain a pause** ([ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250) §7: *"no admin should need direct DynamoDB inspection to explain a pause"*). An admin investigating a paused account will read *0.0% of allowance committed* and conclude the pause is wrong. The figure most likely to be consulted under pressure is the one most likely to mislead. It also silently understates the [ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250) §8 basis-divergence work: `projectMonth`'s `policyMode` is computed from the same vendor-only settled figure, so the shadow mode is not yet the all-vendor basis AC6 is waiting to compare. ## Options 1. **Withhold the comparison.** Show settled, in-flight and the slices; drop *remaining* / *% committed* / *usable allowance* until the numerator is complete. Honest, smallest, loses the pause explanation's headline. 2. **Label the basis.** Keep the figures, state plainly that ledger spend is vendor-only and the allowance covers LLM too, so the percentage is a floor not a total. Cheap, but a caveat under a big number is weak against a confident-looking 0.0%. 3. **Fix the numerator** — bring LLM rows onto the ledger ([ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250) §6). Correct, and the only option that also unblocks the §8 divergence measurement and the eventual admission cutover. Largest. **Recommend 1 now and 3 as the real fix.** 2 leaves a wrong-looking number on screen and relies on someone reading the caveat. ## Acceptance criteria 1. No figure on the admin spend surface divides a vendor-only numerator by an allowance sized for LLM too. 2. If an allowance comparison is shown at all, the spend it compares covers every cost class that allowance governs. 3. `explainPause` never reports a committed percentage it cannot substantiate from the events it holds. Found while auditing what the vendor-cost work had actually delivered. Related: [ENG-1838](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1838), [ENG-1803](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1803), [ENG-1804](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1804), [ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250) §6/§8.

You found a real gap, but I am not taking the proposed fix — and the distinction matters, so here it is in full.

**`pause.paused` is not a pause status.** It resolves as `explainPause` → `projection.policyMode` → `shadowPolicyMode(settledMicroUsd, policy)`, and `spendProjection.ts:86` documents that field as *"SHADOW ONLY — see the module header. **Nothing consumes this.**"* It compares **vendor-only** settled spend against the tier's **LLM** cost cap. On measured production data vendor spend is ~13% of total metered spend, so that computation would essentially never report a pause — and when it did, it would be for the wrong reason.

Keeping an alert gated on it, even with the reason withheld, would assert an enforcement outcome derived from a shadow field on an incomplete basis. That is the same class of error this PR exists to remove, one layer up: instead of a wrong percentage it would be a wrong binary, which is harder to notice and easier to act on.

**Where you are right:** there is now no admin surface showing whether an account is paused. I verified that rather than assuming — `grep checkTokenUsage|usageMode routes/admin*.ts` returns nothing, and `llmUnitEconomicsService`'s `usageState` is the tier's `enforcementState` (`hard_only`/`observe`), a policy mode rather than a per-account outcome.

That gap **predates** this PR. ENG-1838 shipped the panel two days ago and made it look filled; removing the misleading signal reveals it rather than creating it.

**Filed as ENG-1886.** The fix is to surface the *enforcer's own* state — the `usageMode` `checkTokenUsage` already returns at `tokenUsageService.ts:418` — not a recomputation. A second definition of "paused" is precisely what ENG-1135 consolidated away, and it would be free to drift from the one that actually admits or refuses work.

One thing that ticket carries, worth stating here too: the enforcer reads `AW-Users.tokenUsage.totalCost`, which ENG-1247 measured wrong in both directions. So that screen will report *what the enforcer decided* — the truth about the customer's experience — and not *what the account spent*. Those differ today, and conflating them is how this bug happened.

Closing without merging — a deep review commissioned specifically to verify the causal
mechanism built a real repro and refuted it: Node.js circular requires do not re-execute
a module's body (confirmed empirically), so this PR's "the cycle causes the singleton
line to run twice" theory does not hold under actual Node semantics. The lazy-import
change itself is harmless but doesn't fix the real bug.

The review surfaced the actual mechanism: emma/tools.ts and apiTools.ts import the
module-level `agentModeService` singleton directly and call methods on it (e.g.
install_skills' own handler), instead of using `context.service` (the ToolContext field
that's supposed to carry the correctly-initialized, per-call instance). Inside the
shared worker process, that plain singleton import is a separate, never-initialized
object from the worker's own properly-initialized local instance — explaining the exact
same-process, same-pid, interleaved 0-tools/264-tools flip-flop this PR was trying to
fix, with a different and more precise mechanism than the one this PR assumed.

Real fix incoming in a new PR against this actual cause.

Full details: Sensitive Data Protection And Privacy **Explanation** The PR activates a privacy exposure for uploaded creative bytes. `metaWriteSimulator.ts` accepts arbitrary multipart file bytes in `/adimages`, sends them to `agentweb-user-files/sandbox/<userId>/adimages/<sha256>.jpg`, stores the returned URL, and returns that URL to the Graph caller. The shared upload helper returns a direct S3 location without access controls. The repository design states that this path is public-read, and the bucket is documented as publicly accessible. A leaked or shared URL therefore permits access by unintended users and does not provide tenant isolation. This behavior is introduced by the new `/adimages` write path; the helper existed before but was not called by the sandbox simulator. **Resolution** Store sandbox creative uploads in a private bucket or private prefix. Return short-lived, tenant-scoped presigned URLs or serve the bytes through an authenticated endpoint. Enforce authorization for every read, prevent cross-user access, and add tests that another sandbox principal cannot retrieve the object. Add retention and deletion handling for revoked or expired evaluations.
Full details: Security And Access Control Integrity **Explanation** The new Meta write path introduces customer-impacting sandbox mutations, but its audit trail is not durable. `sandboxOverlayStore.mutate` commits the overlay first, then appends the audit row in a separate write. It catches every audit failure, logs only to stderr, and still returns success (`sandboxOverlayStore.ts:83-97`). The added test explicitly confirms that an audit failure does not fail the mutation (`sandboxOverlayStore.test.ts:119-134`). This weakens attribution and rollback evidence for create, update, delete, and upload operations. Existing evaluation lifecycle writes use transactional audit records, so this is a changed control on the new mutation path. **Resolution** Make each overlay mutation and its audit record atomic. Use a DynamoDB transaction that applies the CAS condition to the overlay write and conditionally creates the audit row, then retry the complete transaction on a CAS conflict. If the audit write cannot commit, do not report the mutation as successful. Preserve the audit actor, action, timestamp, and unique object identifier in the durable record.
Full details: Performance And Algorithmic Complexity **Explanation** The write path introduces unbounded persistent state. `sandboxOverlayStore.mutate` reads and rewrites the complete per-user overlay on every mutation, while creates add records, deletes append to `deletedIds`, and every audited mutation appends a new audit item. No object-count, serialized-size, retention, compaction, or audit TTL limit exists. `resolveObjects` and object spreads therefore process increasingly large state on each request, and the single DynamoDB overlay item will eventually reject writes as it grows. `/adimages` also hashes and uploads the complete multipart buffer without a file-size limit; the simulator timeout does not bound multipart hydration before the handler runs. These are changed request-path behaviors and match the check's unbounded-growth and missing-size-limit conditions. **Resolution** Bound the write path before deployment. Enforce a maximum image/body size before buffering, hashing, or uploading, and apply an explicit timeout to multipart hydration and the S3 operation. Bound overlay state with a serialized-size/object-count quota and reject writes before the DynamoDB item becomes oversized, or store objects and deletion markers in separately bounded records with compaction and cleanup. Add retention/TTL or bounded retention for audit rows. Keep reads and mutations from copying or rebuilding the entire accumulated overlay where possible.

ENG-1873 withdraw-stale-invitations always stops as 'paced' and withdraws nothing — and mislabels which gate refused

`withdraw-stale-invitations` returns `stopReason: 'paced'` and withdraws nothing, on an account that is demonstrably not being paced. ## Reproduction Account `FtFMgtmhQdezRcG6PJaqMw` (`aseth@argusoft.com`), 2 pending invitations aged >1 day, `older_than_days: 1`. **Three attempts across 14 hours** — 2026-09-10 ~17:50Z, ~17:55Z, and 2026-09-11 07:17Z — all identical: ``` withdrawn: [] failed: [] remainingStale: 2 totalPending: 2 stopReason: "paced" notice: "Withdrew nothing older than 1 days. Stopped early: this account is at its write-pacing limit ... 2 invitations were pending before this run." ``` The 14-hour gap matters: the pacer window is one hour, so it had long cleared. The selection half works — both invitations are correctly identified as stale. The withdrawal half never executes. ## Both gates ALLOW when reproduced locally against the real config ``` configuredDailyInviteCap: 4, daily_volume: { invite: { count: 2, windowStartedAt: … } }, connectedAt: 2026-07-09 (62 days, unramped) PACED_WRITE_ACTIONS.has('cancel-invitation') -> true reserveDailyVolumeSlot('cancel-invitation') -> { allowed: true } reserveWriteSlot('FtFMgtmhQdezRcG6PJaqMw') -> { allowed: true, waitedMs: 0 } ``` Production sets no `LINKEDIN_*` env overrides, so the defaults apply (`minGapMs` 5000, `maxWritesPerHour` 120). Neither of `reserveWriteSlot`'s refusal paths — hourly ceiling, or a non-empty queue projected past `maxQueueWaitMs` — can fire for a lone caller on an empty window. So the refusal comes from production-side state or a path not reachable locally. I could not narrow it further: EB log retrieval is currently returning stale bundles (newest 2026-09-08), and the decisive line is a log, not a stored field. ## A second, independent defect — and it is why this was so hard to diagnose `paceLinkedInWrite` can refuse from **two** distinct sources, which log differently: ``` [linkedInDailyVolumeGate] … refused by daily volume cap — … [linkedInDailyVolumeGate] … refused by write pacer — … ``` The drain collapses both into `stopReason: 'paced'`, and composes a notice that **always** says *"this account is at its write-pacing limit"*. If the real cause was the daily-volume gate, that notice is actively false and sends the reader to the wrong subsystem — which is exactly what happened here. `DrainStopReason` should distinguish them, or the notice should relay the refusal it actually received rather than assuming which one it was. ## Impact Operator-invoked, so nothing silently breaks for customers. But ENG-1719's feature does not work: an operator asked to clear a backlog gets "we are being paced, try later" indefinitely, with the ENG-1132 backlog it was built to clear left in place. Found while verifying ENG-1719 end to end. ## Acceptance criteria *Confirmed by Anurag Seth, 2026-09-14, in response to the PM triage request for an explicit behavioural contract.* **AC1 — a stale invitation is actually withdrawn.** When the account has at least one pending invitation older than `older_than_days`, and no pre-write gate refuses, `withdraw-stale-invitations`: * withdraws it via Unipile (`withdrawn` is non-empty and names the invitee), * removes its row from `AW-UnipileSentInvitations`, * appends `linkedin.invite.withdrawn` to the matching CRM lead where one exists (or reports it in `crmRecordFailed` — never silently), * does not consume the account's daily invite budget. *Verified by:* a production run on an authorized non-customer account with ≥1 invitation older than the threshold returns `withdrawn` ≥ 1, and the ledger row count drops by the same number. **AC2 — a refusal says which gate refused, truthfully.** When the drain stops early because `paceLinkedInWrite` refused, the result identifies **which** of its refusal sources it was — daily volume cap, write pacer, or failure to persist the daily reservation — using that gate's own wording. The notice must never assert "write-pacing limit" unless the write pacer is what refused. *Verified by:* a unit test per refusal source asserting the result names that source, and a production run whose `pacedReason` matches the `[linkedInDailyVolumeGate]` refusal actually taken. **Out of scope:** changing any pacing limit or the drain's per-run cap. If the root cause turns out to be a limit that is wrong rather than a bug, that is a separate decision. **Sequence:** AC2 ships first — once deployed, a single drain run exposes the real refusal in the tool result without depending on EB log retrieval (which was returning stale bundles during the original investigation). AC1's fix follows from what that run reveals.

Do not debit when: * The customer pays through their own connected account (for example Meta ad spend or customer-owned SaaS/API usage). * The cost is shared platform overhead without a reviewed allocation policy. * The unit has no price. Unpriced paid egress must fail closed or be explicitly allowlisted as platform-funded; it must never become a silent $0 charge. ## Architecture ### 1. Immutable spend events are the source of truth Create an append-only, per-call usage event store ([ENG-702](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-702/make-vendor-usage-writes-idempotent-and-fail-loud-gate-before-any) data-plane gate) rather than treating a mutable monthly counter or daily aggregate as authoritative. Required event fields: * `eventId` / idempotency key * `occurredAt`, billing month * `billingUserId`, `orgId`, `actingUserId`, optional `onBehalfOf` * provider, operation, feature, unit, quantity * `costMicroUsd` * cost source: `measured | allocated` * rate-card version when allocated * session/task/run/request references * lifecycle: `reserved | settled | voided` * external vendor reference when available Retries with the same idempotency key must return the original event and add $0. ### 2. One charging API All paid egress goes through one service; callers may not write the ledger or monthly counter directly. Conceptual contract: 1. Resolve the org billing subject. 2. Classify the call as AgentWeb-paid, customer-paid, or platform overhead. 3. Resolve a measured cost or versioned allocated rate. 4. Reserve known/estimated spend when practical. 5. Check admission against settled spend + outstanding reservations. 6. Execute the vendor call. 7. Settle actual spend or void the reservation. 8. Atomically persist the idempotent event and update the billing-subject/month aggregate. LLM, image/video, v0, X, search, enrichment, voice, rendering, and future vendor adapters must use the same service. ### 3. Monthly state is a projection, not an independent counter Maintain an atomic `billingUserId + month` projection for fast admission: * settled chargeable spend * active reservations * included monthly allowance * purchased credits * admin grants/reversals * migration adjustment * remaining usable balance * current policy mode Invariant: summing immutable settled events must reproduce the monthly spend projection within one micro-dollar. Raw spend is always preserved. Credits and migration adjustments change available allowance; they never erase or rewrite spend. ### 4. Admission semantics * A new job is admitted only when remaining balance covers its reservation or the policy explicitly permits an overrun. * Work admitted before the boundary may finish under the existing admitted-work rule. * Fixed-price calls reserve the exact allocated rate. * Variable-cost calls reserve a documented maximum/estimate and settle the actual amount. * Concurrent requests use conditional/transactional writes so two calls cannot both spend the same remaining balance. * `full_choice | optimized | paused` is derived from this one monthly projection; token volume remains an analytical dimension, not a second competing gate. ### 5. Versioned vendor rate registry One reviewed registry defines provider, operation, unit, rate, currency, effective dates, and source. Pricing rules: * Vendor-reported cost wins when available. * Shared wallets/subscriptions use an explicit allocated rate ([ENG-703](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-703/set-the-allocated-vendor-rate-card-blocks-every-metering-adapter-from)). * A price change creates a new version; historical events retain the rate version used. * No adapter embeds an independent dollar literal. ### 6. Coverage Bring existing slices onto the charging API: * LLM providers, embeddings, image/video * X ([ENG-664](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-664/meter-x-twitter-api-usage-cost-per-account-and-per-tool)) * v0 ([ENG-694](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-694/meter-v0-landing-page-generation-including-the-unguarded-iterate-path)) * [You.com]() and Google CSE ([ENG-695](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-695/meter-paid-web-search-youcom-google-custom-search-and-thread-the)) * Apollo and [enrich.so]() ([ENG-696](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-696/bring-apollo-and-enrichso-onto-the-ledger-and-close-the-six-bypassed)) * ElevenLabs, 2captcha, Placid ([ENG-698](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-698/meter-the-single-call-site-per-unit-vendors-elevenlabs-2captcha-placid)) * Remotion Lambda ([ENG-699](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-699/meter-remotion-lambda-renders-at-submission-time)) * other AgentWeb-paid voice/search/media/email vendors identified by [ENG-701](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-701/make-metering-coverage-a-ci-fact-instead-of-an-audit-artifact) The CI paid-egress registry must fail when a new paid client/call site has no charging adapter or explicit platform-funded exemption. ### 7. Read models and product UX Produce daily/provider/member/feature/session aggregates from immutable events. The org usage screen must show: * billing subject and pooled-org behavior * raw spend versus adjustments and usable balance * daily trend * spend by provider, product feature, and acting member * reservations/in-flight spend * why the account is optimized or paused * reset date and purchased-credit history No admin should need direct DynamoDB inspection to explain a pause. ### 8. Reconciliation Run two independent checks: * Internal: immutable event sum = monthly projection = dashboard total. * External: vendor invoice/wallet/usage export versus attributed ledger totals, allowing only documented timing or allocation differences. Drift above one cent or the vendor-specific threshold alerts and prevents enabling enforcement for that provider. A successful vendor call without a settled/voided event is an operational error. ### 9. Migration and rollout 1. Land schema/idempotency behind the explicit data-plane approval gate. 2. Dual-write old and new rails in observe-only mode. 3. Reconcile LLMs first; the existing gate cannot move until the crater class is resolved. 4. Add vendor adapters one family at a time. 5. Run at least seven days of shadow reconciliation and boundary/concurrency tests. 6. Switch admission to the new monthly projection. 7. Observe a month reset and credit purchase/reversal. 8. Stop writes to `extraCostUsage` and the legacy independent cost counter. 9. Delete legacy paths only after rollback evidence and one clean period boundary. ## Complexity impact Adds one idempotent event rail, one monthly projection, and one rate registry; removes multiple counters, special cases, and manual reconciliation paths. Net result must be fewer charging paths than today. ## Acceptance criteria (from Harsha's request) 1. Every AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable API cost is deducted from the same org monthly usage balance exactly once. 2. Customer-paid integrations and unallocated platform overhead are not charged. 3. A pause is explainable to the cent from per-call events, including provider, feature, acting member, and adjustment history. 4. Vendor spend, immutable events, monthly projection, and dashboard reconcile within the defined threshold. 5. Retries, concurrent calls, failed calls, reservations, refunds/reversals, org inheritance, and month rollover have automated tests. 6. No production enforcement moves to the new rail until shadow reconciliation passes and Harsha approves the data-plane change. 7. The legacy `extraCostUsage` and independent counter paths are retired rather than maintained as fallbacks.

ENG-1873 withdraw-stale-invitations always stops as 'paced' and withdraws nothing — and mislabels which gate refused

`withdraw-stale-invitations` returns `stopReason: 'paced'` and withdraws nothing, on an account that is demonstrably not being paced. ## Reproduction Account `FtFMgtmhQdezRcG6PJaqMw` (`aseth@argusoft.com`), 2 pending invitations aged >1 day, `older_than_days: 1`. **Three attempts across 14 hours** — 2026-09-10 ~17:50Z, ~17:55Z, and 2026-09-11 07:17Z — all identical: ``` withdrawn: [] failed: [] remainingStale: 2 totalPending: 2 stopReason: "paced" notice: "Withdrew nothing older than 1 days. Stopped early: this account is at its write-pacing limit ... 2 invitations were pending before this run." ``` The 14-hour gap matters: the pacer window is one hour, so it had long cleared. The selection half works — both invitations are correctly identified as stale. The withdrawal half never executes. ## Both gates ALLOW when reproduced locally against the real config ``` configuredDailyInviteCap: 4, daily_volume: { invite: { count: 2, windowStartedAt: … } }, connectedAt: 2026-07-09 (62 days, unramped) PACED_WRITE_ACTIONS.has('cancel-invitation') -> true reserveDailyVolumeSlot('cancel-invitation') -> { allowed: true } reserveWriteSlot('FtFMgtmhQdezRcG6PJaqMw') -> { allowed: true, waitedMs: 0 } ``` Production sets no `LINKEDIN_*` env overrides, so the defaults apply (`minGapMs` 5000, `maxWritesPerHour` 120). Neither of `reserveWriteSlot`'s refusal paths — hourly ceiling, or a non-empty queue projected past `maxQueueWaitMs` — can fire for a lone caller on an empty window. So the refusal comes from production-side state or a path not reachable locally. I could not narrow it further: EB log retrieval is currently returning stale bundles (newest 2026-09-08), and the decisive line is a log, not a stored field. ## A second, independent defect — and it is why this was so hard to diagnose `paceLinkedInWrite` can refuse from **two** distinct sources, which log differently: ``` [linkedInDailyVolumeGate] … refused by daily volume cap — … [linkedInDailyVolumeGate] … refused by write pacer — … ``` The drain collapses both into `stopReason: 'paced'`, and composes a notice that **always** says *"this account is at its write-pacing limit"*. If the real cause was the daily-volume gate, that notice is actively false and sends the reader to the wrong subsystem — which is exactly what happened here. `DrainStopReason` should distinguish them, or the notice should relay the refusal it actually received rather than assuming which one it was. ## Impact Operator-invoked, so nothing silently breaks for customers. But ENG-1719's feature does not work: an operator asked to clear a backlog gets "we are being paced, try later" indefinitely, with the ENG-1132 backlog it was built to clear left in place. Found while verifying ENG-1719 end to end. ## Acceptance criteria *Confirmed by Anurag Seth, 2026-09-14, in response to the PM triage request for an explicit behavioural contract.* **AC1 — a stale invitation is actually withdrawn.** When the account has at least one pending invitation older than `older_than_days`, and no pre-write gate refuses, `withdraw-stale-invitations`: * withdraws it via Unipile (`withdrawn` is non-empty and names the invitee), * removes its row from `AW-UnipileSentInvitations`, * appends `linkedin.invite.withdrawn` to the matching CRM lead where one exists (or reports it in `crmRecordFailed` — never silently), * does not consume the account's daily invite budget. *Verified by:* a production run on an authorized non-customer account with ≥1 invitation older than the threshold returns `withdrawn` ≥ 1, and the ledger row count drops by the same number. **AC2 — a refusal says which gate refused, truthfully.** When the drain stops early because `paceLinkedInWrite` refused, the result identifies **which** of its refusal sources it was — daily volume cap, write pacer, or failure to persist the daily reservation — using that gate's own wording. The notice must never assert "write-pacing limit" unless the write pacer is what refused. *Verified by:* a unit test per refusal source asserting the result names that source, and a production run whose `pacedReason` matches the `[linkedInDailyVolumeGate]` refusal actually taken. **Out of scope:** changing any pacing limit or the drain's per-run cap. If the root cause turns out to be a limit that is wrong rather than a bug, that is a separate decision. **Sequence:** AC2 ships first — once deployed, a single drain run exposes the real refusal in the tool result without depending on EB log retrieval (which was returning stale bundles during the original investigation). AC1's fix follows from what that run reveals.

ENG-1250 Usage accounting v2: one auditable spend ledger and admission gate for every AgentWeb-paid call

## Outcome Implement one org-level accounting architecture in which every **AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable** upstream call is recorded exactly once, priced honestly, visible in a spend history, and applied to the same monthly usage limit. This is the end-to-end architecture contract requested by Harsha. It replaces the current split between `tokenUsage.totalCost`, the daily `AW-UsageRecords` aggregates, the effectively dead `extraCostUsage` rail, vendor-specific counters, and unmetered vendor calls. ## Billing boundary Debit the user's/org's monthly usage balance when: * AgentWeb pays an upstream and the action is attributable to a billing subject. * The cost is measured by the vendor, or a versioned allocated rate exists. Do not debit when: * The customer pays through their own connected account (for example Meta ad spend or customer-owned SaaS/API usage). * The cost is shared platform overhead without a reviewed allocation policy. * The unit has no price. Unpriced paid egress must fail closed or be explicitly allowlisted as platform-funded; it must never become a silent $0 charge. ## Architecture ### 1. Immutable spend events are the source of truth Create an append-only, per-call usage event store ([ENG-702](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-702/make-vendor-usage-writes-idempotent-and-fail-loud-gate-before-any) data-plane gate) rather than treating a mutable monthly counter or daily aggregate as authoritative. Required event fields: * `eventId` / idempotency key * `occurredAt`, billing month * `billingUserId`, `orgId`, `actingUserId`, optional `onBehalfOf` * provider, operation, feature, unit, quantity * `costMicroUsd` * cost source: `measured | allocated` * rate-card version when allocated * session/task/run/request references * lifecycle: `reserved | settled | voided` * external vendor reference when available Retries with the same idempotency key must return the original event and add $0. ### 2. One charging API All paid egress goes through one service; callers may not write the ledger or monthly counter directly. Conceptual contract: 1. Resolve the org billing subject. 2. Classify the call as AgentWeb-paid, customer-paid, or platform overhead. 3. Resolve a measured cost or versioned allocated rate. 4. Reserve known/estimated spend when practical. 5. Check admission against settled spend + outstanding reservations. 6. Execute the vendor call. 7. Settle actual spend or void the reservation. 8. Atomically persist the idempotent event and update the billing-subject/month aggregate. LLM, image/video, v0, X, search, enrichment, voice, rendering, and future vendor adapters must use the same service. ### 3. Monthly state is a projection, not an independent counter Maintain an atomic `billingUserId + month` projection for fast admission: * settled chargeable spend * active reservations * included monthly allowance * purchased credits * admin grants/reversals * migration adjustment * remaining usable balance * current policy mode Invariant: summing immutable settled events must reproduce the monthly spend projection within one micro-dollar. Raw spend is always preserved. Credits and migration adjustments change available allowance; they never erase or rewrite spend. ### 4. Admission semantics * A new job is admitted only when remaining balance covers its reservation or the policy explicitly permits an overrun. * Work admitted before the boundary may finish under the existing admitted-work rule. * Fixed-price calls reserve the exact allocated rate. * Variable-cost calls reserve a documented maximum/estimate and settle the actual amount. * Concurrent requests use conditional/transactional writes so two calls cannot both spend the same remaining balance. * `full_choice | optimized | paused` is derived from this one monthly projection; token volume remains an analytical dimension, not a second competing gate. ### 5. Versioned vendor rate registry One reviewed registry defines provider, operation, unit, rate, currency, effective dates, and source. Pricing rules: * Vendor-reported cost wins when available. * Shared wallets/subscriptions use an explicit allocated rate ([ENG-703](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-703/set-the-allocated-vendor-rate-card-blocks-every-metering-adapter-from)). * A price change creates a new version; historical events retain the rate version used. * No adapter embeds an independent dollar literal. ### 6. Coverage Bring existing slices onto the charging API: * LLM providers, embeddings, image/video * X ([ENG-664](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-664/meter-x-twitter-api-usage-cost-per-account-and-per-tool)) * v0 ([ENG-694](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-694/meter-v0-landing-page-generation-including-the-unguarded-iterate-path)) * [You.com]() and Google CSE ([ENG-695](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-695/meter-paid-web-search-youcom-google-custom-search-and-thread-the)) * Apollo and [enrich.so]() ([ENG-696](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-696/bring-apollo-and-enrichso-onto-the-ledger-and-close-the-six-bypassed)) * ElevenLabs, 2captcha, Placid ([ENG-698](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-698/meter-the-single-call-site-per-unit-vendors-elevenlabs-2captcha-placid)) * Remotion Lambda ([ENG-699](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-699/meter-remotion-lambda-renders-at-submission-time)) * other AgentWeb-paid voice/search/media/email vendors identified by [ENG-701](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-701/make-metering-coverage-a-ci-fact-instead-of-an-audit-artifact) The CI paid-egress registry must fail when a new paid client/call site has no charging adapter or explicit platform-funded exemption. ### 7. A valid batch can therefore create up to 502 transaction actions (500 spend events plus the aggregate and charge items), exceeding DynamoDB's 100-action transaction limit. The non-transient failure then falls back to `recordUsage()` for every pending record with `Promise.all`, creating up to 500 additional transactions and a large request-path fan-out. This can cause production write throttling for an adversarial but size-valid batch. Second, the admin breakdown now performs one fully paginated `queryByUserDateRange` per current organization member and per ledger-seen actor. The concurrency is capped at 8, but total queries and accumulated rows have no actor or result limit, timeout, or single keyed billing-subject query. This is an N+1 request pattern on an admin request path. **Resolution** For `/api/internal/usage`, bound the derived transaction size before calling DynamoDB. Reject or safely split batches when the number of spend portions plus the fixed two items can exceed the 100-action limit, and preserve idempotency without falling back to one transaction per record. Bound fallback concurrency as well. For the admin breakdown, replace per-actor fan-out with a billing-subject-indexed query or a bounded/paginated aggregation read. Enforce maximum actors and rows, and apply a request timeout so large organizations or high-volume months cannot consume unbounded request time and memory.

ENG-1929 A metering call can fail the vendor request it meters when its cost is computed inline

## Problem `computeAllocatedCost` **throws on an unpriced unit by design** ([ENG-703](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-703) AC2 — an unpriced unit must fail loud, never book $0). So a thrown `computeAllocatedCost` escapes the `void` and propagates into the vendor call's own request handler. A rate-card key rename, or a new operation added without a rate, would fail the **user's** search, enrichment or render — not just the metering. That inverts the rule every adapter's acceptance criteria state: *a metering failure must never prevent the vendor result reaching the caller.* No call site throws today — every key currently in use is priced. Prefer one of: 1. **Move pricing inside the recorder.** Pass `{ provider, operation, quantity }` and let `recordVendorUsage` resolve the rate within its existing never-throw boundary. Removes the class of bug rather than patching instances. 2. **A shared** `meterVendorCall()` **helper** that computes cost and records, with the guard built in, and migrate call sites to it. Either way, ENG-703 AC2 must still hold: an unpriced unit fails **loud** — logged and alerted via `usageWriteFailureMonitor` — not silently booked at $0. The change is *where* it fails, not *whether*. ## Acceptance criteria 1. No vendor call can fail because its own cost could not be computed. 2. An unpriced unit is still reported loudly and never recorded as $0 (ENG-703 AC2 preserved). 3. A new metering call site cannot reintroduce the inline-throw path without failing a test or the coverage guard.

ENG-1886 No admin surface shows whether an account is actually paused

## Gap **No admin surface shows whether a given account is currently paused.** Found while reviewing [ENG-1874](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1874) (CodeRabbit raised it on PR [#2872]()). The spend-ledger panel appeared to show one, but did not. Its `pause.paused` comes from `explainPause` → `projection.policyMode` → `shadowPolicyMode(settledMicroUsd, policy)`, and `spendProjection.ts:86` documents that field as: > *"SHADOW ONLY — see the module header. **Nothing consumes this.**"* It compares **vendor-only** settled spend (all `AW-SpendEvents` holds) against the tier's **LLM** cost cap. On measured production data vendor spend is ~13% of total metered spend, so that computation would essentially never report a pause, and if it did it would be for the wrong reason. [ENG-1874](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1874) withheld it for exactly that reason. Verified there is no other source: `grep checkTokenUsage|usageMode routes/admin*.ts` returns nothing. `llmUnitEconomicsService`'s `usageState` is the tier's `enforcementState` (`hard_only` / `observe`) — a **policy mode**, not whether this account has been cut off. ## Why it matters The authoritative state already exists and nothing surfaces it. `checkTokenUsage` returns `usageMode` (`tokenUsageService.ts:418`) from `evaluateLlmUsageMode`, and that is what actually admits or refuses a user's work. Today an admin answering *"why has this customer stopped working?"* has no screen that tells them the account is paused. That gap predates [ENG-1838](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1838); that panel just made it look filled. ## Scope Expose the **enforcer's own** state per billing subject on the admin surface — the same value `checkTokenUsage` returns, not a recomputation. A second definition of "paused" is exactly what [ENG-1135](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1135) consolidated away. Show: usage mode, the counter and threshold it was decided against, and the reset date. ## One thing to state plainly wherever it is shown The enforcer reads `AW-Users.tokenUsage.totalCost`, which [ENG-1247](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1247) measured as wrong in **both** directions — the AgentWeb org paused at 36% of real usage, and 20 of 58 enforced-tier users passed their real cap with no block. So this screen reports *what the enforcer decided*, which is the truth about the customer's experience, and **not** *what the account actually spent*. Those differ today. Conflating them is how [ENG-1874](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1874) happened; the label has to carry the distinction. ## Acceptance criteria 1. An admin can see whether a given billing subject is currently paused, and against which threshold. 2. The value shown is the one the enforcement path returns — not a second computation that could disagree with it. 3. The screen distinguishes what the enforcer measured from what the account spent, wherever the two can differ. 4. No shadow or observe-only field is presented as an enforcement outcome. Related: [ENG-1874](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1874), [ENG-1838](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1838), [ENG-1135](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1135), [ENG-1247](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1247), [ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250) §7.

ENG-1841 Bound the spend-breakdown read without truncating its aggregates

## Why [ENG-1838](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1838) made the ENG-1250 §7 spend breakdown reachable from a UI for the first time. That turns an unbounded read into an interactive one, and CodeRabbit flagged it on PR [#2843](). `listSpendEvents` (`backend/src/services/spendEventDb.ts:358`) pages the `BillingUserOccurredAtIndex` GSI until `LastEvaluatedKey` is exhausted — no cap, no cursor, no page-size limit. `GET /api/admin/users/:billingUserId/spend/breakdown` calls it for a whole calendar month, and ENG-1838 resolves an org **member** to the billing **root**, so the read spans every member's events. ## Why ENG-1838 did not fix it **A truncated aggregate is a wrong aggregate.** Every headline on that screen — settled spend, in-flight, the daily trend, each of the four slices — is a sum over the full month. Capping the fetch would silently understate all of them, and an understated spend figure on the screen used to explain a pause is materially worse than a slow one. ENG-1838 capped the *rendering* (25 rows per cut, remainder counted and stated), which removes the practical symptom. The read itself needs a different shape, below. ## Current magnitude — measured, not assumed The ledger began writing 2026-09-07, and [ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250) measured system-wide growth at **~546 rows/day across all billing subjects**. One subject-month is presently tens to low hundreds of events. This is not urgent; it is a real ceiling that arrives as the ledger fills and as [ENG-698](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-698) adds the last three vendors. ## Shape of the fix Either, not both: 1. **Server-side aggregation.** Compute the totals and slices on the server (or from the §3b persisted projection when it lands) and return only bounded top-N detail rows with a cursor. Aggregates stay exact; the response is bounded by construction. 2. **An explicit ceiling.** Page to a documented maximum and, past it, return a "too large to summarise" error rather than a wrong total. Cheaper, and honest, but it makes the screen unavailable exactly for the heaviest accounts — which are the ones most likely to be paused. Recommend 1. It also composes with §3b: once the monthly projection is persisted, the totals stop needing a full scan at all. ## Acceptance criteria 1. The endpoint's response size and work are bounded regardless of how many events a subject-month holds. 2. Every total the screen shows remains exact — no aggregate is computed from a truncated set. 3. Detail rows beyond the bound are reachable (cursor) or explicitly stated as omitted; they are never silently dropped. 4. The admin screen behaves identically for a subject-month small enough that no bound is reached. Related: [ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250) §7 (the read models this bounds), [ENG-1838](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1838) (the UI that made it interactive), [ENG-1273](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1273) (the sibling GSI/scan question on `AW-UsageRecords`).
