ENG-1858 29% of metered calls book to `system` — spend recorded but attributable to nobody

## What was found While verifying [ENG-1837](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1837) on production (2026-09-10, range 2026-08-11 → 2026-09-10), the admin **Usage & Cost** table shows a row keyed `system`: | Row id | Calls | Cost | | -- | -- | -- | | `system` | **10,830** | $10.86 | That is **10,830 of 37,078 metered calls — 29% of all calls in the window — attributed to no user.** In dollars it is 0.27% of $4,091.95, so these are cheap calls; the concern is attribution, not spend. ## Why it matters [ENG-664](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-664)'s acceptance contract says *"no call path can spend credits unattributed"* (AC1) and *"an uninstrumented call path fails loudly"* (AC3). Neither is violated in the way those were written — the metering **succeeded**. It booked to a placeholder. That is arguably worse than a loud failure: the row is well-formed, it aggregates cleanly, and nothing about it looks wrong. Under [ENG-666](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-666) AC1 (*"a given user's total upstream cost for a period is queryable"*) and [ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250) AC1 (*"deducted from the same org monthly usage balance exactly once"*), spend booked to `system` is spend that can never reach a customer's balance — it is absorbed by AgentWeb by construction, silently. ## Where it comes from Three call paths in `backend/src/services/usageRecorderService.ts` default the same way: | Line | Function | Fallback | | -- | -- | -- | | `:201` | `recordUsage` | `ctx.userId \|\| "system"` | | `:273` | `recordVendorUsageIdempotent` | `ctx.userId \|\| "system"` | | `:406` | `recordVendorUsageLegacy` | `ctx.userId \|\| "system"` | Note `meterUserUsage` (`:493`) deliberately returns early when `ctx.userId` is absent, so this spend is **recorded but never charged**. The two behaviours are consistent — which is exactly why nothing has ever surfaced it. ## What this issue is not Not a request to remove the fallback. Booking to `system` beats losing the row — that was the right call. The question is which callers are hitting it, and whether each one *can* supply a user. ## Scope 1. Identify the actual callers producing `system` rows — the `model` / `provider` / `feature` mix on those rows should point at them without new instrumentation. 2. For each, decide: thread the real user through, or classify it as genuinely platform-funded (cron, warmup, health checks, system-initiated maintenance). 3. Anything genuinely platform-funded should be recorded as such rather than as an absent user — [ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250)'s billing boundary already names `platform_overhead` as a distinct classification, and `spendChargingService.classify` implements it. 4. Report the residual: after (2), how many calls still book to `system`, and why. ## Acceptance criteria 1. Every `system` row in a recent window is traced to a named call path. 2. Each path is either attributed to a real billing subject or explicitly classified as platform-funded, with the reason recorded. 3. The share of calls booking to `system` for reasons nobody chose is zero, or the remainder is named and tracked. 4. No metering write is removed or made lossy in the process — a row booked to `system` remains better than no row. ## Also found in the same pass — smaller, same family Two ledger rows carry a **non-user string** in the `userId` slot: * `workplans` — 10 calls, $0.67 * `eng1223-live-readonly-check` — 3 calls, $0.0437 The first looks like a feature name reaching the user slot; the second like a test harness. Both are small, but they suggest the user id is not always the thing the writer thought it was. Worth resolving alongside (1). Found while verifying [ENG-1837](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1837). Related: [ENG-664](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-664), [ENG-666](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-666), [ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250), [ENG-702](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-702).

## Closing — the premise this was built on is obsolete

Three independent reviewers went over this diff. Recording why it is being closed so nobody rebuilds it.

**The premise was stale.** This was built on a finding that *nothing* could write to `AW-AdsOutcomeLedger`. That check was run on a branch that predated ENG-502. ENG-502 has since landed and is **live in production right now** — `captureFatigueRecommendations` writes attributed, scoreable rows (there is a real `fatigue_…` row in prod). The ledger has a producer; it just isn't model-driven, and that appears deliberate.

**The tool writes into the wrong lane.** The ledger has two disjoint scoring paths:

| Row | Scored by | Other path |
|---|---|---|
| **with** ENG-502 `context` | the cron, from attributed evidence + execution receipts | REST refuses (`409 attributed_evaluation_required`) |
| **without** `context` | admin REST, from a caller-supplied `actualValue`/`baselineValue` | cron refuses (filtered out of `getDueRecommendations`) |

This tool emits context-less rows, so every agent prediction lands in the lane whose own comment says the manual scorer *"has no attribution/evidence contract"* and must not *"fabricate a causal verdict"*. The PR's headline claim — record-only, so a model cannot rewrite its own track record — holds for the model, but the rows it creates are scoreable **only** by the evidence-free path. And since nobody scores those by hand, they sit `pending` indefinitely, consuming the evaluation cron's page budget on every rotation.

**Fixing it properly is a design decision, not a patch.** Supplying a valid `RecommendationContext` would fix cron evaluation, read-back, tenant attribution and the lane problem in one move — but it requires widening `RecommendationContext.source`, currently a single-value union `'assess_client_health'`. That union is the design saying capture is scoped to one deterministic path on purpose. Having an LLM populate `evidence: [{reference, metric, value}]` is precisely the fabrication risk that contract exists to prevent. **The real question — should L4 widen by extending deterministic capture, and to which recommendation types? — belongs with whoever designed ENG-502.**

**Also wrong in this PR as written:** the `__other_skills__` exclusion is incomplete (bypassed by wildcard subscriptions — which `getAllowedSkills` also returns *on any error* — and by legacy sessions), the "no scoring tool" guard is a name-substring lint that `score_ads_outcome` slips past, one test is vacuous, and the migration loses the record of already-written skills if it throws mid-loop.

## What came out of it that was real

- **A genuine bug in shipped code** — `createRecommendation` accepted a backdated `evaluationDate`, permitting retroactive prediction. Fixed separately in #2942, with one such row already sitting in production.
- **The `__other_skills__` hazard** — any tool not wired to a published skill is exposed to essentially every customer. A general trap for the next person adding a tool; filed separately.
- **The two-lane scoring split**, documented above.

Closing. The exclusion and migration go with it, since both existed only to serve this tool.

ENG-1978 A new tool that isn't wired to a skill is exposed to every customer via __other_skills__

## The trap Adding a tool to the registry and NOT attaching it to a published skill does not make it inert — it makes it **broadly available**. `agentModeService.getUnassociatedTools` sweeps every registered tool that is not a foundation tool, not in `ADMIN_SKILL_TOOL_NAMES`, and not claimed by a **published** skill into the `__other_skills__` bundle. `subscriptionService.resolveSkillsToToolNames` then grants that whole bundle to anyone whose tier lists `__other_skills__`. **Every real production tier enables it** — Super Premium, Free, Managed, Pro, Demo, Starter, Partner. Only `Sandbox` omits it (checked 2026-09-16). So the natural, careful-looking rollout — "merge the tool first, wire it to skills afterwards" — ships the tool to essentially the entire customer base in the gap, offered to the model with no skill context telling it when the tool is appropriate. Found while building ENG-1550's ledger write tool (PR #2940, now closed). Not specific to that tool: **this applies to every new tool anyone adds.** ## Why the obvious fix is not enough The existing precedent is a hardcoded exclusion (`get_visual_context`, excluded with the note "never expose in Agent Mode or `__other_skills__`"). PR #2940 generalised that into a `SKILL_SCOPED_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES` set — **and independent review showed it is still bypassable**: * `getAllowedSkills` returns `["*"]` when the subscription type is missing, when `allowedSkills` is `["*"]` or `[]`, **and on any error**. `resolveSkillsToToolNames` then short-circuits to `["*"]` before `__other_skills__` is ever consulted, so the exclusion never runs. * Legacy sessions set `skillFilter = undefined`, which passes **all** registered tools; the only remaining gate is `filterFunctionCalls`, which returns everything under a wildcard. * `liveVoiceService` calls `getFilteredTools(userId)` with no skill filter at all. A name-exclusion list is therefore not a real containment boundary. ## What is actually worth deciding 1. Should "registered but unattached" default to **exposed** or **hidden**? The current default is exposed, which is the surprising direction and puts the burden on every future tool author to know about this. 2. Should the wildcard/error path in `getAllowedSkills` really grant *every* tool? Defaulting to full access **on error** is a fail-open. 3. If a name-list is kept, it needs to be enforced at the point tools are assembled for a session, not only in `getUnassociatedTools`. ## Not urgent, but not cosmetic Nothing is broken in production today — this is about what happens the next time someone adds a tool. The failure mode is quiet: the tool simply shows up for customers who were never meant to have it, and nothing alerts. Relevant code: `services/agentModeService.ts` (`getUnassociatedTools`), `services/subscriptionService.ts` (`getAllowedSkills`, `resolveSkillsToToolNames`, `filterFunctionCalls`).

Full details: Sensitive Data Protection And Privacy **Explanation** The PR introduces a cross-account privacy and tenant-isolation risk. In `backend/src/routes/slack.ts`, the mapped-thread handler now authorizes only that the mapping exists and that `session.userId === mappedUserId`; it no longer checks the Slack requester, the owner's channel, or admin-channel authorization. The updated tests explicitly verify that internal users, external Slack Connect humans, and external bots can continue `user-fangfang`'s mapped session. The handler then passes the mapped owner's `userId` to `generateSessionResponse`, which loads the full session history and sends that owner identity to the worker and its tools. The generated response is posted to the shared Slack thread. Therefore, any Slack identity able to create an explicit mention in a mapped thread can cause the owner's session context and owner-scoped connected-account operations to be exposed or performed in that thread. Signed-event verification proves Slack origin, not authorization to access the mapped customer's session. This is a changed-code failure under weak tenant isolation and cross-account data leakage. **Resolution** Do not authorize a mapped session from mapping existence alone. Require a durable authorization for the event sender, such as the session owner, an authorized owner-bound channel, an authorized admin/delegation grant, or an owner-approved per-thread participant ACL. Validate the Slack user and workspace/team against that grant before reading or continuing the session, downloading attachments, or invoking tools. Keep the acting Slack principal separate from the mapped session owner, and prevent owner-scoped connected-account tools from running for an external participant unless explicit delegated access exists. Add negative tests for an unapproved internal user, external human, and external bot, and verify that no session generation, attachment upload, or owner-scoped tool call occurs.
Full details: Security And Access Control Integrity **Explanation** The PR weakens mapped-session access control. In `backend/src/routes/slack.ts`, the changed handler now authorizes any signed `app_mention` whose mapping resolves to a session with the mapped `userId`; it no longer verifies the Slack requester, the session owner's channel authorization, or the configured admin channel. The existing test that rejected an unauthorized participant was removed and replaced with tests that allow an external human and external bot to run Fangfang's mapped session. The route then calls `generateSessionResponse(sessionId, ..., userId, ...)` with the mapped owner's identity. That function persists the message and passes the owner identity to the worker, so an unrelated Slack participant can submit work against another user's session and potentially access owner-scoped session context or tools. Signed-event verification and mapping owner consistency do not establish requester authorization. **Resolution** Restore requester authorization for mapped sessions, or implement an explicit per-thread participant authorization model. At minimum, retain the session-owner identity check and require one of: verified requester ownership, an owner-authorized channel, or a configured admin/delegated channel. If Slack Connect participants must be allowed, bind and validate their Slack identity or approved team/channel membership for that mapped thread before calling `generateSessionResponse`. Restore a negative test for an unrelated participant and add coverage for the approved external-participant path. Log rejected authorization decisions with the requester, channel, thread, and session identifiers.

ENG-1250 Usage accounting v2: one auditable spend ledger and admission gate for every AgentWeb-paid call

## Outcome Implement one org-level accounting architecture in which every **AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable** upstream call is recorded exactly once, priced honestly, visible in a spend history, and applied to the same monthly usage limit. This is the end-to-end architecture contract requested by Harsha. It replaces the current split between `tokenUsage.totalCost`, the daily `AW-UsageRecords` aggregates, the effectively dead `extraCostUsage` rail, vendor-specific counters, and unmetered vendor calls. ## Billing boundary Debit the user's/org's monthly usage balance when: * AgentWeb pays an upstream and the action is attributable to a billing subject. * The cost is measured by the vendor, or a versioned allocated rate exists. Do not debit when: * The customer pays through their own connected account (for example Meta ad spend or customer-owned SaaS/API usage). * The cost is shared platform overhead without a reviewed allocation policy. * The unit has no price. Unpriced paid egress must fail closed or be explicitly allowlisted as platform-funded; it must never become a silent $0 charge. ## Architecture ### 1. Immutable spend events are the source of truth Create an append-only, per-call usage event store ([ENG-702](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-702/make-vendor-usage-writes-idempotent-and-fail-loud-gate-before-any) data-plane gate) rather than treating a mutable monthly counter or daily aggregate as authoritative. Required event fields: * `eventId` / idempotency key * `occurredAt`, billing month * `billingUserId`, `orgId`, `actingUserId`, optional `onBehalfOf` * provider, operation, feature, unit, quantity * `costMicroUsd` * cost source: `measured | allocated` * rate-card version when allocated * session/task/run/request references * lifecycle: `reserved | settled | voided` * external vendor reference when available Retries with the same idempotency key must return the original event and add $0. ### 2. One charging API All paid egress goes through one service; callers may not write the ledger or monthly counter directly. Conceptual contract: 1. Resolve the org billing subject. 2. Classify the call as AgentWeb-paid, customer-paid, or platform overhead. 3. Resolve a measured cost or versioned allocated rate. 4. Reserve known/estimated spend when practical. 5. Check admission against settled spend + outstanding reservations. 6. Execute the vendor call. 7. Settle actual spend or void the reservation. 8. Atomically persist the idempotent event and update the billing-subject/month aggregate. LLM, image/video, v0, X, search, enrichment, voice, rendering, and future vendor adapters must use the same service. ### 3. Monthly state is a projection, not an independent counter Maintain an atomic `billingUserId + month` projection for fast admission: * settled chargeable spend * active reservations * included monthly allowance * purchased credits * admin grants/reversals * migration adjustment * remaining usable balance * current policy mode Invariant: summing immutable settled events must reproduce the monthly spend projection within one micro-dollar. Raw spend is always preserved. Credits and migration adjustments change available allowance; they never erase or rewrite spend. ### 4. Admission semantics * A new job is admitted only when remaining balance covers its reservation or the policy explicitly permits an overrun. * Work admitted before the boundary may finish under the existing admitted-work rule. * Fixed-price calls reserve the exact allocated rate. * Variable-cost calls reserve a documented maximum/estimate and settle the actual amount. * Concurrent requests use conditional/transactional writes so two calls cannot both spend the same remaining balance. * `full_choice | optimized | paused` is derived from this one monthly projection; token volume remains an analytical dimension, not a second competing gate. ### 5. Versioned vendor rate registry One reviewed registry defines provider, operation, unit, rate, currency, effective dates, and source. Pricing rules: * Vendor-reported cost wins when available. * Shared wallets/subscriptions use an explicit allocated rate ([ENG-703](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-703/set-the-allocated-vendor-rate-card-blocks-every-metering-adapter-from)). * A price change creates a new version; historical events retain the rate version used. * No adapter embeds an independent dollar literal. ### 6. Coverage Bring existing slices onto the charging API: * LLM providers, embeddings, image/video * X ([ENG-664](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-664/meter-x-twitter-api-usage-cost-per-account-and-per-tool)) * v0 ([ENG-694](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-694/meter-v0-landing-page-generation-including-the-unguarded-iterate-path)) * [You.com]() and Google CSE ([ENG-695](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-695/meter-paid-web-search-youcom-google-custom-search-and-thread-the)) * Apollo and [enrich.so]() ([ENG-696](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-696/bring-apollo-and-enrichso-onto-the-ledger-and-close-the-six-bypassed)) * ElevenLabs, 2captcha, Placid ([ENG-698](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-698/meter-the-single-call-site-per-unit-vendors-elevenlabs-2captcha-placid)) * Remotion Lambda ([ENG-699](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-699/meter-remotion-lambda-renders-at-submission-time)) * other AgentWeb-paid voice/search/media/email vendors identified by [ENG-701](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-701/make-metering-coverage-a-ci-fact-instead-of-an-audit-artifact) The CI paid-egress registry must fail when a new paid client/call site has no charging adapter or explicit platform-funded exemption. ### 7. Read models and product UX Produce daily/provider/member/feature/session aggregates from immutable events. The org usage screen must show: * billing subject and pooled-org behavior * raw spend versus adjustments and usable balance * daily trend * spend by provider, product feature, and acting member * reservations/in-flight spend * why the account is optimized or paused * reset date and purchased-credit history No admin should need direct DynamoDB inspection to explain a pause. ### 8. Reconciliation Run two independent checks: * Internal: immutable event sum = monthly projection = dashboard total. * External: vendor invoice/wallet/usage export versus attributed ledger totals, allowing only documented timing or allocation differences. Drift above one cent or the vendor-specific threshold alerts and prevents enabling enforcement for that provider. A successful vendor call without a settled/voided event is an operational error. ### 9. Migration and rollout 1. Land schema/idempotency behind the explicit data-plane approval gate. 2. Dual-write old and new rails in observe-only mode. 3. Reconcile LLMs first; the existing gate cannot move until the crater class is resolved. 4. Add vendor adapters one family at a time. 5. Run at least seven days of shadow reconciliation and boundary/concurrency tests. 6. Switch admission to the new monthly projection. 7. Observe a month reset and credit purchase/reversal. 8. Stop writes to `extraCostUsage` and the legacy independent cost counter. 9. Delete legacy paths only after rollback evidence and one clean period boundary. ## Complexity impact Adds one idempotent event rail, one monthly projection, and one rate registry; removes multiple counters, special cases, and manual reconciliation paths. Net result must be fewer charging paths than today. ## Acceptance criteria (from Harsha's request) 1. Every AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable API cost is deducted from the same org monthly usage balance exactly once. 2. Customer-paid integrations and unallocated platform overhead are not charged. 3. A pause is explainable to the cent from per-call events, including provider, feature, acting member, and adjustment history. 4. Vendor spend, immutable events, monthly projection, and dashboard reconcile within the defined threshold. 5. Retries, concurrent calls, failed calls, reservations, refunds/reversals, org inheritance, and month rollover have automated tests. 6. No production enforcement moves to the new rail until shadow reconciliation passes and Harsha approves the data-plane change. 7. The legacy `extraCostUsage` and independent counter paths are retired rather than maintained as fallbacks.

ENG-1875 Work-plan debt ledger can drive auto-continuation to silently resume scope the user just removed

**Found while root-causing ENG-1819's origin incident (session** `d663ff2d-a26d-4c23-a8e4-a0b59e9d0352`**, 2026-09-08).** The reported ENG-1819 symptom (auto-continuation overriding an explicit user "stop") is fully fixed and unrelated to this ticket -- this is a separate, adjacent problem found while digging into why that incident's plan looked mechanically incomplete when it wasn't. **Root cause traced precisely:** the user's turn 1 instructed "complete step 1, then call modify_work_plan with removeStepCounts:[2,3], then stop." The model did exactly this -- `modify_work_plan`'s own tool result confirmed a genuinely 1-step, fully-resolved plan. The model's "It's done!" was accurate, not a hallucination. But `workPlanHasUnfinishedAutocompleteWork` = pending step OR unresolved ENG-1811 debt, and removing steps 2/3 left their never-attempted `requiredFunctionCalls` in `workPlan.pendingRequiredFunctionCalls` (the ENG-1811 anti-gaming debt ledger, which exists to stop a MODEL from removing a step to dodge a required call it's failing). That debt made the mechanism see "still unfinished," auto-continuation fired, and the continuation turn itself re-added the removed step and did the work -- confirmed exactly in the message log (index 22, 4s after the continuation fired). **Why this isn't simply fixed:** the debt ledger can't distinguish "user explicitly authorized this removal" from "model dodged a gate" -- both look identical at the point `modify_work_plan` executes. The obvious-looking fix (decouple debt from auto-continuation triggering, only let it block `set_work_plan_status` completion) reopens a DIFFERENT, already-solved problem: `hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan`'s own ENG-1813 doc comment explains debt was deliberately wired into the stall check specifically so debt doesn't leave a plan permanently stuck with no further attempt to resolve it. Removing that coupling means a model that games the ledger just produces a permanently-stalled plan instead of a false completion -- not clearly better. **The real tension, undesigned:** debt genuinely has to eventually trigger an attempt to resolve it (or gaming produces permanent stalls), but that attempt currently can't tell legitimate user-authorized scope cuts from model-initiated gate-dodging, and silently resumes work on scope the user just explicitly removed either way. **Scope assessment (why Low priority, parked rather than fixed now):** requires a fairly narrow combination -- an autocomplete plan, a step removed via `modify_work_plan removeStepCounts` whose required calls were never satisfied, AND no accompanying explicit stop instruction (ENG-1819's fix already covers the stop case). Impact when it does hit is mild -- extra unwanted work on removed scope, not a false-completion lie (ENG-1811/1799/1800's core protection is untouched and still holds). Needs real design thought (how to signal/distinguish authorized vs. gamed removal, or some other reconciliation) before touching -- explicitly NOT a quick patch, don't rush it. **Related:** [[bug-eng1819]] (workplan-brain node, full incident trace + investigation), ENG-1811/1799/1800/1813 (the debt-ledger mechanism this interacts with).

On a multi-instance deployment a poll served by a different instance than the one running the task sees `false` while work continues, so absence of progress is not proof of completion. * A **durable** terminal status already exists: `markRunTerminal()` writes it to the `AW-AgentRuns` table (`services/agentMode/runStore.ts:162`). * **No REST route exposes it.** `grep` for `agent-runs` / `/runs/` across `src/routes` returns nothing. So a tool reaching the backend over `mcpFetch` — which is every MCP tool, by the security design [ENG-974](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-974/emma-mcp-refuse-outbound-action-internal-tools-for-external-callers-at) preserves — cannot read the one signal that would answer the question. ## Why it is not urgent The common path does not depend on it. `/api/agent-mode/generate` is synchronous unless the run detaches, so `emma_run_marketing_task` already returns a confirmed terminal result for ordinary work. Only the detached long-build path polls, and it currently reports honestly-unconfirmed rather than falsely-terminal. ## Acceptance criteria 1. **A read-only endpoint returns the caller's own run status.** Given a session or run id owned by the authenticated user, it returns the terminal state recorded by `markRunTerminal` (`completed` / failed / still running) plus a finish reason where one exists. 2. **Ownership is enforced.** A caller cannot read another user's run. Negative test with a run belonging to a different user → refused, and the record's contents do not leak in the error. 3. `emma_get_task_result` **uses it.** When the endpoint reports a terminal state, the tool returns `completion_confirmed: true`. A test drives the detached path end to end: no active progress on this instance + a terminal run record → confirmed complete. 4. **Absence still fails honest.** If no run record exists (expired TTL, never written), the tool keeps reporting unconfirmed rather than inventing a terminal state. This is the property the whole issue exists to protect. 5. **No change to the quota or entitlement boundaries.** The route goes through `authenticateToken` like every other, and [ENG-973](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-973/quota-bypass-the-apiemma-family-mcps-self-call-surface-never-checks)'s classification covers it. ## Note `AW-AgentRuns` records carry a TTL, so this confirms recent runs, not historical ones. That is the right scope — an agent polls minutes after submitting, not weeks.

Full details: Security And Access Control Integrity **Explanation** The new runner weakens the existing autonomy gate. For every replay failure, `failureReplaySuite.ts` calls `fileIssue` with `executionRoute: 'autofix'` (lines 91–108). `fileAutoIssue` converts that route into `Bug`/`autofix` labels and the unattended-fix assignee. The repository's autofix poller then picks up Bug issues in backlog/unstarted states; its runtime guard only checks `AUTOFIX_RUN_ENABLED`. This bypasses the existing fail-closed, allowlisted route selection in `LinearIntakeTool`, which returns `human-triage` unless the proposal matches approved conditions. No scheduler caller is present in the changed files, but the exported function and new documentation explicitly define this as a scheduled entry point, so the introduced behavior would grant unattended-fix eligibility to every future replay case without a case-level approval decision. **Resolution** Do not hardcode `executionRoute: 'autofix'` for replay failures. Default replay findings to `human-triage`, or require an explicit, independently validated allowlist for cases that may use `autofix`, matching the existing fail-closed route policy. Add a regression test that an ordinary replay failure cannot enter the autofix route, and test any approved autofix case separately.
Full details: Performance And Algorithmic Complexity **Explanation** The new scheduled replay runner has quadratic worst-case work on the intake-outage path. For each failed case, lines 88-120 await filing and, when it rejects, line 114 scans the full `results` array with `find`; if all `n` filings reject, this performs O(n²) comparisons. The runner also maps every case into `Promise.all` at lines 80-83 with no input limit, concurrency bound, or timeout, so a large case set or a never-settling contract can consume unbounded resources or keep the scheduled run open indefinitely. The module is new in this pull request. Repository search found no current production caller, so this is not currently shown on a production request-path outage, but the documented scheduler entry point is directly affected. **Resolution** Index replay results by case ID while evaluating so intake-error updates are O(1). Add a documented maximum case count and bounded concurrency instead of launching every contract at once. Add cancellation-aware per-contract and per-filing timeouts so one large or hung replay cannot retain all results or block the scheduled sweep indefinitely. The backend KNOWS (the `if (!user)` creation branch) but never propagates it. Firing client-side today would require guessing, and firing on a returning login **poisons conversion data** — so this must be a coordinated backend+frontend change, shipped together (a portal-only PR reading a param the backend never sends would be dead no-op code = banned fake-completion). ## The fix (3 edits, spans two repos) 1. `agentweb` `backend/src/controllers/auth.ts` `googleCallback`: `let isNewUser = false;` before the `if (!user)` check (\~L308); set `isNewUser = true` inside the creation branch(es) after successful `createUser`; add it to `resultUserObject` (\~L537): `{ token, userId, email, roles, isAdmin, isNewUser }`. 2. `agentweb` `backend/src/routes/auth.ts` `googleAuthFinalHandler` **(\~L291)**: append only when true — `...?token=${token}${isNewUser ? '&isNewUser=true' : ''}`. 3. `agentweb-customer-portal` `src/pages/OAuthCallback.tsx`: read `searchParams.get('isNewUser')==='true'` and, after `setToken` resolves for a genuinely new account, fire `trackPixelFlowEvent('CompleteRegistration', { email: userData.email, content_name: 'google-oauth' })` — only when true (param absent on returning logins → never fires). Reuse `src/lib/pixelflow.ts`. ## Acceptance criteria (HUMAN-WRITTEN — behavioral contract) 1. New customer-portal Google signup → redirect includes `&isNewUser=true` AND the portal fires exactly ONE `CompleteRegistration` with `content_name: 'google-oauth'`. 2. Returning Google login → no `isNewUser` param → the event NEVER fires. 3. Personal-email new signup (already blocked at `controllers/auth.ts:300-306`) → error redirect, no event. All three are unit-testable (passport verify + mocked `trackPixelFlowEvent`; mirror `src/pages/__tests__/Register.pixelflow.test.tsx`). PURE/MOCKABLE. Both PRs (backend + portal) ship together — never one half alone. ## Audit disposition — executable Todo **Route:** Claude coordinated backend + portal implementation. **Acceptance:** new Google signups emit exactly one `CompleteRegistration`; returning logins and blocked personal-email signups emit none, with both repository halves shipped together. **Dependencies:** existing PixelFlow helper and OAuth tests; no external credential or data-plane gate.

## Why (Harsha, 2026-07-21) Every Emma-built lander that fronts a paid campaign needs Meta conversion tracking wired **automatically at generation time** — not set up by hand afterward. It exposes a "Programmatic Tracking API" for **sending events**, but pixel **provisioning** (create a config per site, set Dataset ID + CAPI token) is dashboard-first — not designed for "spin up a new tracked lander via API." ENG-1165 Make 'blocked by external auth / awaiting user input' a neutral EXCLUDED scoring state, like the Slack-suggestion exception

FEATURE REQUEST (re-raised — previously surfaced on 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-11, still unbuilt; now backed by three fresh divergence cases in one window). THE PROBLEM: when a session is blocked by something outside the agent's control (user not signed in, integration token revoked, upstream API outage, user never replied), the general satisfaction judge charges it to goalCompletion, while the specialist judges correctly score the agent's HANDLING as excellent. The headline metric therefore reports platform gaps as agent failures, and the divergence is the only way to tell them apart. EVIDENCE FROM THE 2026-08-12 WINDOW 1. Session 7ec5c519-fd6b-4b92-88ba-e87bb0c677de 'LinkedIn Profile Review' — general 3 (goalCompletion 3 / outputQuality 5 / dataAccuracy 5) vs Fangfang Judge 5 ('This is the ideal behavior for an unsigned-in session') and Matt Judge 4. A 2-point spread on identical behavior; the ONLY fault is that the visitor was not signed in. 2. Session d3bb5d30-0b3c-42bc-a9a2-1b9c06f80c09 'LinkedIn Profile Review' — headline 4 from all three judges but goalCompletion pinned at 3 by every judge, purely because of the auth gate. 3. Sessions scored 4 with goalCompletion 4 and outputQuality/dataAccuracy 5, where the sole blocker was a platform-side configuration or outage and the agent handled it textbook-well: the AI GTM Positioning Audit runs blocked by a missing email-sender configuration (report generated, link + fix instructions supplied); a Meta Ads session that hit invalidated access tokens, STOPPED before making unauthorized changes and gave a 60-second reconnect fix; and a LinkedIn outreach run that hit a LinkedIn search outage plus invite capacity limits, pivoted to existing CRM leads, drafted compliant messages, updated the CRM and FILED the product issues (Fangfang explicitly noted: 'Since a bug was formally reported via the appropriate tool, the platform limitations are not penalized'). That last quote shows the rubric ALREADY contains the right principle — it is just applied inconsistently between judges and not reflected in goalCompletion. REQUESTED BEHAVIOR: add a neutral terminal state (e.g. blocked_external / awaiting_user_input) that the judges can assign instead of a low goalCompletion, and exclude those sessions from the unsatisfying-cohort percentage the same way Slack-suggestion sessions are excluded. Qualifying conditions: user not authenticated; required integration disconnected or token revoked; upstream provider outage; user never replied to a legitimate clarifying question; publish deliberately withheld under an account-level approval setting. The session should still be reported as an actionable platform gap — just not counted as an agent failure. WHY: 2 of the 5 unsatisfying sessions this window (7ec5c519, and arguably the auth-gated portion of the LinkedIn trio) are this artifact. Removing it would take the reported rate from 6.49% to \~5.19% and, more importantly, stop the metric from hiding real regressions behind noise. It would also make the 'agent excellent, platform broken' cohort directly countable, which is currently only discoverable by manually diffing Fangfang/Matt against the general score. ## Deep audit — 2026-09-17 **Disposition: Todo.** Execute one route: add a typed `blocked_external` / `awaiting_user_input` terminal classification at the shared judge result boundary and exclude it from the unsatisfying denominator while retaining it in platform-gap reporting. Acceptance: deterministic fixtures cover unauthenticated, disconnected/revoked integration, upstream outage, unanswered legitimate question, and configured publish hold; ordinary task failures remain scored; all judges and aggregate reporting agree. Dependency: reuse the existing Slack-suggestion exclusion mechanism rather than a parallel metric path.

ENG-731 Swarm worktrees symlink backend/node_modules into sibling worktrees — pruning a merged worktree silently breaks every borrower

## Hard signal (2026-07-29, hit live while shepherding #2212 / [ENG-693](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-693/give-the-existing-usage-ledger-a-vendor-dimension-unblocks-all-paygo)) A full backend shard-B run in the [ENG-693](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-693/give-the-existing-usage-ledger-a-vendor-dimension-unblocks-all-paygo) worktree reported **419 test suites / 280 tests failed**. Nothing was wrong with the code — the same tree had been fully green minutes earlier and was fully green again minutes later. Root cause: `/.worktrees/eng-693-ledger-vendor/backend/node_modules` was a **symlink** pointing at `/.worktrees/eng-705-v0-credit-guard/backend/node_modules`. When [ENG-705](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-705/unauthenticated-unrate-limited-paths-can-burn-v0-credits-share) (#2210) merged, its worktree was pruned. The symlink dangled, jest walked up the directory tree, and resolved modules out of an unrelated *third* worktree (`eng-629-meta-scope-failclosed`), producing: ``` Cannot find module 'unipile-node-sdk' from 'src/services/linkedInOutreachService.ts' at Resolver._throwModNotFoundError (../../eng-629-meta-scope-failclosed/backend/node_modules/jest-resolve/...) ``` An earlier run in the same worktree showed a *single* unrelated suite (`routes.landingPageGeneration`) failing — that was the same teardown in progress, and it was initially misdiagnosed as an order-dependent flake. Fix applied locally: `rm node_modules && npm ci` (862 packages) in the affected worktree. Both shards then passed (933 + 213 suites). ## Why this matters more than a one-off The failure mode is **maximally misleading to an automated executor**: * It appears only after an *unrelated* PR merges, so it correlates with nothing in the current diff. * It produces a red so large it looks like a catastrophic regression, not an environment fault. * It is intermittent by construction — green, then red, then green — which reads exactly like flake, and the standing rule is not to re-run until green. * A less careful agent could plausibly "fix" it by weakening tests, adding mocks, or reverting good code. That is the real risk, not the lost cycles. It also silently couples worktree lifetimes: pruning a merged worktree (which Watchdog is instructed to do every tick) is currently able to break unrelated in-flight work. ## Acceptance criteria ### Behavioral contract (HUMAN-WRITTEN — please review/replace; the stub below is agent-drafted) 1. Creating a swarm worktree produces a `backend/node_modules` that does not depend on any other worktree's filesystem lifetime — removing any other worktree leaves it fully functional. 2. Removing a merged worktree never changes module resolution in any surviving worktree; a full shard run in a surviving worktree before and after the removal produces identical suite/test counts. 3. If dependencies are unavailable or inconsistent in a worktree, the test command fails **loudly and specifically** (naming the worktree and the missing install) rather than resolving modules out of a sibling directory. 4. Whatever sharing mechanism is chosen does not require a full per-worktree `npm ci` wall-clock cost on every worktree creation. ### Implementation notes (non-binding) Candidates worth comparing before picking: a real per-worktree install; a content-addressed shared store (pnpm-style) that is not tied to a worktree path; a shared install rooted outside `.worktrees/` that no prune step can remove; or making worktree creation refuse to symlink into another worktree at all. Option 3 above (fail loud) is likely the cheapest immediate guard and is worth shipping even if the sharing strategy takes longer to settle. ## Provenance Found by the Watchdog loop on PR #2212 ([ENG-693](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-693/give-the-existing-usage-ledger-a-vendor-dimension-unblocks-all-paygo)). Filed rather than left in chat because the next agent to hit it will see a 419-suite red with no plausible cause in its own diff. ## Audit disposition — executable Todo **Route:** Claude swarm-infrastructure fix. **Acceptance:** remove sibling-worktree lifetime coupling, add a loud dependency-integrity failure, and prove deleting one worktree leaves a borrower's full suite counts unchanged without requiring a full install on every creation. **Dependencies:** current worktree creation/prune scripts and a disposable pair of test worktrees; no production dependency.

That sentence pre-dates [ENG-1311](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1311/follow-explicit-direction-one-line-of-pushback-then-comply) unchanged (verified against the frozen [ENG-947](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-947/p1-publish-gate-deadlock-persists-unattended-scheduled-social-runs)-era literal in `publishGateScopeRewrite.ts`) — not a regression from [ENG-1311](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1311/follow-explicit-direction-one-line-of-pushback-then-comply). The gap CodeRabbit found: `planSkillChange(skill, target)` takes `target.blocks` as a caller-supplied array that defaults to `[]` (see `applyHardening.ts`). A `hardenSkills.ts` `targets.json` config that sets `setPrompt: 'linkedInEngagement'` without also listing `blocks: ['publishGate']` produces a skill row whose systemPrompt tells the model to "obey the PUBLISH AUTHORIZATION block" — but no such block was appended, so an unattended run has no authority to consult. The prompt doesn't specify a safe default for "block absent," so behavior on that row is undefined by the prompt text (the sibling `BLOCKS.publishGate` full block already has an explicit "if an unattended run carries NO PUBLISH AUTHORIZATION block, treat it as attended" fallback — `MIN_PROMPTS.linkedInEngagement`'s rule 1 does not). ENG-937 Per-class fix proposals for one tool need a cooldown-identity migration

Split out of [ENG-820](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-820) during review, where it was implemented, reviewed twice, and then deliberately reverted. This issue exists so the design is done properly rather than bolted onto a digest change. ## What ENG-820 shipped One proposal per **tool**, using the dominant actionable failure class. Other actionable cohorts are **named** in the hypothesis (`Also present: 8 bug`) and the remedy is sized on its own cohort (`10/30`, not the combined `18/30`), so nothing is silently folded away. ## What is still missing A tool with, say, 10 `config` and 8 `bug` failures gets **one** remediation. The config account gets reconnected; the 8 handler bugs get no dispatch of their own. Naming them is a mitigation, not a fix. ## Why it was reverted rather than shipped `sourceRuleId` is the **cooldown key**. `CooldownRuleSet.onCooldown()` filters persisted learning records with an exact match: ```ts .filter((r) => r.proposal?.sourceRuleId === ruleId && r.shippedAt) ``` Class-qualifying the id (`tool-failure:` → `tool-failure::`) orphans every historical record. A tool currently suppressed because its last fix was graded `regressed` or `no_change` would be **re-dispatched immediately**, and every in-flight remediation would look un-attempted. That is a persistence-semantics change with production consequence, not a rendering change — and ENG-820's own scope line is *"nothing here changes how tools execute; it changes what** **one Slack message says."* ## Acceptance criteria ### Behavioral contract (HUMAN-WRITTEN — agent must not modify) 1. A tool with two actionable failure classes above threshold produces a distinct remediation for each, with its own count, rate, error class, quoted message and directive. 2. A tool whose previous **tool-level** proposal is within its cooldown window is still suppressed after the identity change — no re-dispatch of work that is already in flight or recently graded `regressed`. 3. The digest counts **failing tools**, not proposals: two cohorts on one tool must not render as two failing tools, and the truncation line must not mix units. 4. The migration is stated explicitly: either historical `tool-failure:` records are matched by the new ids, or they are migrated, and a test proves an existing cooldown record still suppresses the equivalent class-qualified proposal. ### Implementation tests (AGENT-WRITTEN) Mocked learning store. No live loop run required. ## Note for whoever takes it `CooldownRuleSet` is shared core (`loops/core/policy/cooldownRuleSet.ts`) used by other loop instances, so a compatibility shim there has a wider blast radius than the agent-mode instance alone. Prefer a change scoped to the agent-mode rule set if one exists.

ENG-1250 Usage accounting v2: one auditable spend ledger and admission gate for every AgentWeb-paid call

## Outcome Implement one org-level accounting architecture in which every **AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable** upstream call is recorded exactly once, priced honestly, visible in a spend history, and applied to the same monthly usage limit. This is the end-to-end architecture contract requested by Harsha. It replaces the current split between `tokenUsage.totalCost`, the daily `AW-UsageRecords` aggregates, the effectively dead `extraCostUsage` rail, vendor-specific counters, and unmetered vendor calls. ## Billing boundary Debit the user's/org's monthly usage balance when: * AgentWeb pays an upstream and the action is attributable to a billing subject. * The cost is measured by the vendor, or a versioned allocated rate exists. Do not debit when: * The customer pays through their own connected account (for example Meta ad spend or customer-owned SaaS/API usage). * The cost is shared platform overhead without a reviewed allocation policy. * The unit has no price. Unpriced paid egress must fail closed or be explicitly allowlisted as platform-funded; it must never become a silent $0 charge. ## Architecture ### 1. Immutable spend events are the source of truth Create an append-only, per-call usage event store ([ENG-702](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-702/make-vendor-usage-writes-idempotent-and-fail-loud-gate-before-any) data-plane gate) rather than treating a mutable monthly counter or daily aggregate as authoritative. Required event fields: * `eventId` / idempotency key * `occurredAt`, billing month * `billingUserId`, `orgId`, `actingUserId`, optional `onBehalfOf` * provider, operation, feature, unit, quantity * `costMicroUsd` * cost source: `measured | allocated` * rate-card version when allocated * session/task/run/request references * lifecycle: `reserved | settled | voided` * external vendor reference when available Retries with the same idempotency key must return the original event and add $0. ### 2. One charging API All paid egress goes through one service; callers may not write the ledger or monthly counter directly. Conceptual contract: 1. Resolve the org billing subject. 2. Classify the call as AgentWeb-paid, customer-paid, or platform overhead. 3. Resolve a measured cost or versioned allocated rate. 4. Reserve known/estimated spend when practical. 5. Check admission against settled spend + outstanding reservations. 6. Execute the vendor call. 7. Settle actual spend or void the reservation. 8. Atomically persist the idempotent event and update the billing-subject/month aggregate. LLM, image/video, v0, X, search, enrichment, voice, rendering, and future vendor adapters must use the same service. ### 3. Monthly state is a projection, not an independent counter Maintain an atomic `billingUserId + month` projection for fast admission: * settled chargeable spend * active reservations * included monthly allowance * purchased credits * admin grants/reversals * migration adjustment * remaining usable balance * current policy mode Invariant: summing immutable settled events must reproduce the monthly spend projection within one micro-dollar. Raw spend is always preserved. Credits and migration adjustments change available allowance; they never erase or rewrite spend. ### 4. Admission semantics * A new job is admitted only when remaining balance covers its reservation or the policy explicitly permits an overrun. * Work admitted before the boundary may finish under the existing admitted-work rule. * Fixed-price calls reserve the exact allocated rate. * Variable-cost calls reserve a documented maximum/estimate and settle the actual amount. * Concurrent requests use conditional/transactional writes so two calls cannot both spend the same remaining balance. * `full_choice | optimized | paused` is derived from this one monthly projection; token volume remains an analytical dimension, not a second competing gate. ### 5. Versioned vendor rate registry One reviewed registry defines provider, operation, unit, rate, currency, effective dates, and source. Pricing rules: * Vendor-reported cost wins when available. * Shared wallets/subscriptions use an explicit allocated rate ([ENG-703](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-703/set-the-allocated-vendor-rate-card-blocks-every-metering-adapter-from)). * A price change creates a new version; historical events retain the rate version used. * No adapter embeds an independent dollar literal. ### 6. Coverage Bring existing slices onto the charging API: * LLM providers, embeddings, image/video * X ([ENG-664](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-664/meter-x-twitter-api-usage-cost-per-account-and-per-tool)) * v0 ([ENG-694](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-694/meter-v0-landing-page-generation-including-the-unguarded-iterate-path)) * [You.com]() and Google CSE ([ENG-695](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-695/meter-paid-web-search-youcom-google-custom-search-and-thread-the)) * Apollo and [enrich.so]() ([ENG-696](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-696/bring-apollo-and-enrichso-onto-the-ledger-and-close-the-six-bypassed)) * ElevenLabs, 2captcha, Placid ([ENG-698](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-698/meter-the-single-call-site-per-unit-vendors-elevenlabs-2captcha-placid)) * Remotion Lambda ([ENG-699](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-699/meter-remotion-lambda-renders-at-submission-time)) * other AgentWeb-paid voice/search/media/email vendors identified by [ENG-701](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-701/make-metering-coverage-a-ci-fact-instead-of-an-audit-artifact) The CI paid-egress registry must fail when a new paid client/call site has no charging adapter or explicit platform-funded exemption. ### 7. Read models and product UX Produce daily/provider/member/feature/session aggregates from immutable events. The org usage screen must show: * billing subject and pooled-org behavior * raw spend versus adjustments and usable balance * daily trend * spend by provider, product feature, and acting member * reservations/in-flight spend * why the account is optimized or paused * reset date and purchased-credit history No admin should need direct DynamoDB inspection to explain a pause. ### 8. Reconciliation Run two independent checks: * Internal: immutable event sum = monthly projection = dashboard total. * External: vendor invoice/wallet/usage export versus attributed ledger totals, allowing only documented timing or allocation differences. Drift above one cent or the vendor-specific threshold alerts and prevents enabling enforcement for that provider. A successful vendor call without a settled/voided event is an operational error. ### 9. Migration and rollout 1. Land schema/idempotency behind the explicit data-plane approval gate. 2. Dual-write old and new rails in observe-only mode. 3. Reconcile LLMs first; the existing gate cannot move until the crater class is resolved. 4. Add vendor adapters one family at a time. 5. Run at least seven days of shadow reconciliation and boundary/concurrency tests. 6. Switch admission to the new monthly projection. 7. Observe a month reset and credit purchase/reversal. 8. Stop writes to `extraCostUsage` and the legacy independent cost counter. 9. Delete legacy paths only after rollback evidence and one clean period boundary. ## Complexity impact Adds one idempotent event rail, one monthly projection, and one rate registry; removes multiple counters, special cases, and manual reconciliation paths. Net result must be fewer charging paths than today. ## Acceptance criteria (from Harsha's request) 1. Every AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable API cost is deducted from the same org monthly usage balance exactly once. 2. Customer-paid integrations and unallocated platform overhead are not charged. 3. A pause is explainable to the cent from per-call events, including provider, feature, acting member, and adjustment history. 4. Vendor spend, immutable events, monthly projection, and dashboard reconcile within the defined threshold. 5. Retries, concurrent calls, failed calls, reservations, refunds/reversals, org inheritance, and month rollover have automated tests. 6. No production enforcement moves to the new rail until shadow reconciliation passes and Harsha approves the data-plane change. 7. The legacy `extraCostUsage` and independent counter paths are retired rather than maintained as fallbacks.

Full details: Sensitive Data Protection And Privacy **Explanation** The PR broadens a cross-tenant Drive read path to every user. The base `DEFAULT_FOUNDATION_TOOLS` did not include `read_google_doc`; the head adds it as a foundation tool. Its handler accepts any file ID, and `readGoogleFileById` falls back to the shared service account when the caller has no Google Drive account or receives a 401/403. That path does not verify that the file belongs to the caller or to the caller's registered folder. Any user who obtains an ID can therefore ask the shared service account to read a file shared with that account. The new shortcut path adds a similar scope gap: it resolves `shortcutDetails.targetId` and reads the target without checking that the target remains inside the authorized folder tree or is accessible to the caller. This is a tenant-isolation and customer-data exposure. It is not a production outage path. The Enigma config adds an internal user UUID allowlist, but the diff contains no credential or customer payload. **Resolution** Do not make `read_google_doc` a universal foundation tool until its authorization is independent of subscription gating. Before using the service-account fallback, require proof that the requested file is in the caller's authorized knowledge-base folder or verify access with the caller's Google identity; otherwise return an authorization error. For shortcut reads, apply the same check to `targetId` and reject targets outside the caller's authorized scope. Add tests for an unauthenticated/unconnected user and for a shortcut whose target is outside the registered folder.
Full details: Security And Access Control Integrity **Explanation** The PR weakens access and approval controls for Google Drive. It adds `google_drive` and `read_google_doc` to `DEFAULT_FOUNDATION_TOOLS`, which `buildSkillContext` and `getFilteredTools` treat as always available and exempt from subscription filtering. Before this change, these unassociated tools were reachable through the subscription-gated `__other_skills__` path. `google_drive` is not read-only: its registered actions include `create_folder`. The tool gateway does not classify `google_drive` as a write or require confirmation, so every session can reach a connected user's Drive folder-creation action without the prior entitlement gate. `read_google_doc` also falls back to the shared service account after OAuth failure, which broadens direct document-read access once the tool is made universal. This is an access-control and separation-of-duties defect, not a production-outage path. The new EB allowlist config does not by itself show an unauthorized user grant. **Resolution** Do not promote the multi-action `google_drive` tool to the foundation layer. Keep `create_folder` behind its subscription/skill entitlement, or split the tool into separately gated read-only and write tools. Add an explicit runtime entitlement check so tool-list construction cannot be the only control. Classify the folder-creation action as a third-party write and enforce an explicit user-confirmation gate before execution. Add negative tests proving a non-entitled user cannot invoke `create_folder`, plus tests proving the write requires confirmation. Review the service-account fallback for `read_google_doc` and retain it only with an explicit per-user authorization boundary.

ENG-2076 Meta Ads: false "0 of N produced" completion-claim correction derails publish flow, ads never go live

## Summary Meta Ads campaigns can silently fail to go live because the agent's "false completion claim" guard fires false positives on Meta Ads (and any non-media-generation) tool calls, derailing the user right before the final publish confirmation. ## Where this was found Session `65abb8aa-3732-4be0-9281-edf28de3027c` (Water Heater Warranty, ad account `2041725529929988`, delegated session run by [matthew@agentweb.pro](), 2026-09-21/22). Verified from `AW-ChatMessages` tool-call results: 1. Campaign `WH | FreeWarrantyCheck-TOF | Traffic` created successfully (`120249885535550073`) 2. Ad set `WH | WarrantyCheck-TOF | Broad 30-65` created successfully (`120249885541470073`) 3. All 3 ad creatives created successfully (real creative IDs `1889108739189532`, `1589022319433637`, `2009795059725019`) 4. The 3 ads themselves were never created — the final "publish these 3 ads" confirmation was pending and never answered. So the account/org access was never the issue (24 successful `call_meta_marketing_api` calls in the session prove access worked fine) — the org-sharing done the prior Friday was a red herring. ## Root cause Right after the 3 creatives succeeded, the assistant correctly said "All 3 creatives created." On the very next turn, recapping that same true fact, the backend auto-appended a **false correction**: > "⚠️ Correction: the '3' figure above is not accurate — only 0 of 3 were actually produced this turn." This confused the user into a bug-report side-quest instead of confirming the pending ad publish, and the session ended there with nothing actually live. The bug is in `backend/src/services/agentMode/core/synthesisResidue.ts` (`detectFalseCompletionClaim` / `buildFalseClaimCorrectionFooter`), wired in at `agentModeService.ts:4608`: * It compares any "N of N " claim in assistant text against a tool-call ledger scoped to the **current turn only**. * `ASSET_PRODUCING_TOOL_NAMES` (line \~478) only lists image/video/HTML-template tools (`generate_image`, `generate_video`, `create_html_file`, etc.) — `call_meta_marketing_api` was never included. * So for Meta Ads work `actual` is always `0`, regardless of what really happened, and any turn that recaps a prior turn's real results with no fresh matching tool calls of its own gets a false correction appended. This guard was built for a different failure mode (ENG-1188/ENG-1331, image-generation work-plan steps) and is enabled globally (`AGENT_FALSE_CLAIM_GUARD` env kill-switch only, no domain scoping) — it silently corrupts Meta Ads (and likely other non-media-generation tool) conversations whenever the model recaps a numeric result. ## Fix Being fixed in this chat (branch to follow) — scope `detectFalseCompletionClaim` to claims about `ASSET_PRODUCING_TOOL_NAMES`-type deliverables only, and/or extend the ledger to recognize Meta Ads (and other write-tool) successes, so it stops false-flagging legitimate non-media tool results. ## Immediate unblock (separate from the code fix) The campaign/ad set/creatives already exist in Meta for the session above — someone needs to go back into that chat and confirm ("yes") to publish the 3 pending ads.

ENG-2076 Meta Ads: false "0 of N produced" completion-claim correction derails publish flow, ads never go live

## Summary Meta Ads campaigns can silently fail to go live because the agent's "false completion claim" guard fires false positives on Meta Ads (and any non-media-generation) tool calls, derailing the user right before the final publish confirmation. ## Where this was found Session `65abb8aa-3732-4be0-9281-edf28de3027c` (Water Heater Warranty, ad account `2041725529929988`, delegated session run by [matthew@agentweb.pro](), 2026-09-21/22). Verified from `AW-ChatMessages` tool-call results: 1. Campaign `WH | FreeWarrantyCheck-TOF | Traffic` created successfully (`120249885535550073`) 2. Ad set `WH | WarrantyCheck-TOF | Broad 30-65` created successfully (`120249885541470073`) 3. All 3 ad creatives created successfully (real creative IDs `1889108739189532`, `1589022319433637`, `2009795059725019`) 4. The 3 ads themselves were never created — the final "publish these 3 ads" confirmation was pending and never answered. So the account/org access was never the issue (24 successful `call_meta_marketing_api` calls in the session prove access worked fine) — the org-sharing done the prior Friday was a red herring. ## Root cause Right after the 3 creatives succeeded, the assistant correctly said "All 3 creatives created." On the very next turn, recapping that same true fact, the backend auto-appended a **false correction**: > "⚠️ Correction: the '3' figure above is not accurate — only 0 of 3 were actually produced this turn." This confused the user into a bug-report side-quest instead of confirming the pending ad publish, and the session ended there with nothing actually live. The bug is in `backend/src/services/agentMode/core/synthesisResidue.ts` (`detectFalseCompletionClaim` / `buildFalseClaimCorrectionFooter`), wired in at `agentModeService.ts:4608`: * It compares any "N of N " claim in assistant text against a tool-call ledger scoped to the **current turn only**. * `ASSET_PRODUCING_TOOL_NAMES` (line \~478) only lists image/video/HTML-template tools (`generate_image`, `generate_video`, `create_html_file`, etc.) — `call_meta_marketing_api` was never included. * So for Meta Ads work `actual` is always `0`, regardless of what really happened, and any turn that recaps a prior turn's real results with no fresh matching tool calls of its own gets a false correction appended. This guard was built for a different failure mode (ENG-1188/ENG-1331, image-generation work-plan steps) and is enabled globally (`AGENT_FALSE_CLAIM_GUARD` env kill-switch only, no domain scoping) — it silently corrupts Meta Ads (and likely other non-media-generation tool) conversations whenever the model recaps a numeric result. ## Fix Being fixed in this chat (branch to follow) — scope `detectFalseCompletionClaim` to claims about `ASSET_PRODUCING_TOOL_NAMES`-type deliverables only, and/or extend the ledger to recognize Meta Ads (and other write-tool) successes, so it stops false-flagging legitimate non-media tool results. ## Immediate unblock (separate from the code fix) The campaign/ad set/creatives already exist in Meta for the session above — someone needs to go back into that chat and confirm ("yes") to publish the 3 pending ads.

ENG-2054 Slack events endpoint accepts unsigned requests — forged events can trigger an approval

`POST /api/slack/events` (`backend/src/routes/slack.ts:454`) performs **no request-signature verification**. There is no HMAC check anywhere in the file — `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET` is read only to report a boolean in a diagnostics response (`slack.ts:1970`, `:2028`). Slack signs every request with `X-Slack-Signature` / `X-Slack-Request-Timestamp`; nothing here reads either header. The endpoint is mounted without `authenticateToken` (`app.ts:377`), so the payload is trusted purely because it arrived. **Why this is priority 1 rather than hygiene.** The handler acts on the event body: * `reaction_added` → `handleLoopApprovalReaction` — an **approval** path. The contract in the code comment is "React ✅ to dispatch all to cloud-dev". * `app_mention` → starts agent work with attacker-chosen text. So an unsigned request can impersonate a Slack user and approve a dispatch, or drive the agent. The bar is knowing the URL. **Fix.** Verify the Slack signature before acting: recompute `v0=HMAC-SHA256(signing secret, `v0:${timestamp}:${rawBody}`)`, compare with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, and reject a timestamp older than \~5 minutes to stop replay. This needs the **raw** body, so the `express.json()` on this route must capture `rawBody` (or be replaced by `express.raw`) — a signature computed over a re-serialised object will not match. Fail closed when the secret is unset. **Secondary, same handler:** `slack.ts:456-457` logs the full request body and **all headers** at info level on every event. That writes third-party tokens and customer message content to the application log. Found while building aw-agent; verified against `main` on 2026-09-19 by reading the route and its mount. Not exploited — no forged request was ever sent.

ENG-449 Auto-wire Meta Pixel + Conversions API (server-side) into Emma-generated landers at generation time

## Why (Harsha, 2026-07-21) Every Emma-built lander that fronts a paid campaign needs Meta conversion tracking wired **automatically at generation time** — not set up by hand afterward. Manual pixel setup is the current state and it's the source of "paid campaigns optimizing blind" bugs (see [ENG-443](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-443/rankai-book-a-demo-lander-no-crm-capture-0-meta-conversion-signal-paid) RankAI book-a-demo: 0 Meta conversion signal; [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject) was the Google/GTM half). This is the durable programmatic fix for the Meta side. ## Research verdict on "PixelFlow" ([pixelflow.so]()) PixelFlow is a **no-code dashboard tool** (Webflow/Framer/Squarespace/WordPress apps) that runs Meta Pixel + server-side Conversions API (CAPI) with browser↔server event dedup. It exposes a "Programmatic Tracking API" for **sending events**, but pixel **provisioning** (create a config per site, set Dataset ID + CAPI token) is dashboard-first — not designed for "spin up a new tracked lander via API." Conclusion: **don't depend on PixelFlow for provisioning.** The programmatic path we own is to inject the **Meta Pixel base code + wire CAPI directly** at lander generation, mirroring what [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject) did for GTM/GA4. (If we still want PixelFlow's dedup convenience, it's an optional client-side add, not the backbone.) ## Approach At lander generation (the same seam [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject) uses to inject GTM): given the campaign's Meta pixel/dataset ID, (1) inject the Meta Pixel base snippet + a standard `Lead` event on form submit, and (2) fire the matching server-side CAPI `Lead` event from our lead-capture backend with an `event_id` shared with the browser event for dedup. Pixel/dataset ID resolution depends on [ENG-399](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-399/call-meta-marketing-api-dataset-list-broken-meta-100-nonexisting-field) (call_meta_marketing_api DATASET LIST is broken → pixel discovery impossible in-product) and on the Meta account being connected — so this is partly blocked until [ENG-399](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-399/call-meta-marketing-api-dataset-list-broken-meta-100-nonexisting-field) lands and Meta is connected; the injection + CAPI-emit scaffolding can be built and unit-tested behind a mocked Meta boundary now. ## Acceptance criteria (HUMAN-WRITTEN) 1. When a lander is generated with a Meta pixel/dataset ID present, the deployed HTML contains the Meta Pixel base code and a `Lead` standard event fired on lead-form submit (asserted in a generation test). 2. On lead-form submit, the backend emits a server-side CAPI `Lead` event to the correct dataset, sharing an `event_id` with the browser event so Meta dedups (assert the CAPI call payload + shared event_id with a mocked Meta CAPI boundary). 3. If no pixel/dataset ID is resolvable (e.g. [ENG-399](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-399/call-meta-marketing-api-dataset-list-broken-meta-100-nonexisting-field) unresolved or Meta not connected), the lander still generates successfully and the missing-pixel condition is surfaced loudly (logged + returned in the generation result), never silently skipped. 4. No regression to the existing GTM/GA4 injection from [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject). ## Links Depends on [ENG-399](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-399/call-meta-marketing-api-dataset-list-broken-meta-100-nonexisting-field) (pixel discovery) · complements [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject) (GTM auto-inject, done), [ENG-239](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-239/auto-append-utm-parameters-to-every-emma-deployed-ad-campaign-make-ai) (UTM auto-append, done), [ENG-327](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-327/user-settable-landing-page-utms-pass-through-decoration-from-rankai) (user-settable UTMs), [ENG-443](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-443/rankai-book-a-demo-lander-no-crm-capture-0-meta-conversion-signal-paid) (RankAI 0-conversion-signal).

ENG-2079 A v0 correction that returns no new version fails the whole page, bypassing the 'proceeding without it' fallback

## Summary The three *enhancement* corrections — Meta Pixel Lead event, Google Ads conversion, bridge-out redirect — each end in an explicit fallback: ```ts pixelLeadEventVerified = pixelCheck.ok; if (!pixelCheck.ok) { console.warn(`... still missing ... — proceeding without it`); } ``` A page missing them is **degraded, not broken**, and is supposed to ship. That fallback is unreachable when v0 answers the correction with no new version, because the failure happens at the *await*, not at the check: ```ts versionId = await waitForCompletedV0Version( // throws on deadline v0, chatId, `v0 correction (pixel lead event) for /${slug}`, { ..., afterVersionId: versionId }); continue; ``` `waitForCompletedV0Version` throws, the outer catch marks the page `failed`. ## Two compounding problems 1. The correction is gated only on `effectivePixelId` — not on whether the page actually has a lead-capture form. For a page without one, "fix the lead capture form" is unsatisfiable, so no new version ever arrives. 2. An unanswered correction is fatal to the entire page. A missing pixel is explicitly tolerable; a missing *answer about* the missing pixel is not. That asymmetry is unintended. ## Impact Any site **with a Meta pixel** where v0 fails to wire the Lead event fires this correction. If v0 does not answer, the whole page generation fails after \~17 minutes, with an error that blames v0: ``` No completed version in v0 chat after ~16 minutes — v0 is still generating or has stalled. ``` Observed live twice (env2), both reaching `attempt 34/34` then `failed`, on pages that had already generated and validated fine. ## Fix `awaitOptionalV0Correction(label, wait)` — returns the corrected version id, or `undefined` when no new version arrived. `undefined` falls through to the existing "proceeding without it" path. Applied to all six enhancement-correction sites (3 on the sub-page path, 3 on the root path). Deliberately **not** applied to the `validateV0Output` correction, where un-correctable output genuinely must not ship — those two waits stay fatal. PR: [https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/pull/3017]() ## Verification Regression test asserts a page whose correction is never answered still reaches `deployed` with `pixelLeadEventVerified: false`. Mutation-checked: reverting gives `Expected: "deployed" / Received: "failed"` — the exact production behaviour.

ENG-2078 Post-deploy smoke test races the capture-route sync build, so every new sub-page reports a false ok:false

## Summary Every newly-added sub-page fails its post-deploy landing-page smoke test, deterministically. Not flaky. ## Mechanism Adding a sub-page pushes a **second** commit that regenerates `app/api/capture/route.ts` — the new page's path only enters the deployed `LIST_BY_PATH` in that build (ENG-483). That build was fire-and-forget and its promise was dropped (`v0Service.ts` \~2533), while the smoke test was dispatched immediately after the deployed write (\~2616): ```ts void pollVercelDeployment(...) // promise dropped ... void import("./landingPageSmokeTest") .then((m) => m.runGenerationSmokeTest(deployedSubPage)) // fires now ``` The smoke test submits the page's own form to a capture route that has no entry for `/slug` yet, gets `422 {"error":"This page has no lead list configured…"}`, no lead is created, and the page is reported `ok: false`. Root pages are unaffected — `route.ts` ships in the initial commit. ## Evidence (production) Polled `/api/capture` from the instant `generate` returned: ``` 14:52:24 generate returns api=404 dpl_DWLBfz 14:52:59 ... api=404 dpl_CNUT5i <- rollout mid-flight 14:53:13 ... api=404 14:53:39 ... api=422 <- route exists, path not in map yet ``` All 4 pages generated during verification reported `ok:false` at T+0; all 4 captured correctly minutes later. ## Impact A false negative upstream of everything the smoke test was built to catch — it makes the signal untrustworthy exactly where it is supposed to be strongest, and it fires on every sub-page add. ## Fix Retain the sync build's poll promise and await it in the already-detached smoke dispatch. Request path unchanged (page still returns `deployed` without waiting for the second build). PR: [https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/pull/3017]() ## Verification * unit: smoke not called while the sync build is held open, fires once it resolves; a sync that never commits does not strand it. Mutation-checked (revert -> `Received number of calls: 1`). * live (env1/env2, on the fixed build): happy path `ok=true leadCaptured=true` (+31s), `fullname` page `ok=true` (+36s), phone-only page correctly still `ok=false`, stranded-lead sweep confirmed.

ENG-2056 GET /api/config returns encryptedPassword to the browser

`GET /api/config` (`backend/src/routes/config.ts:22`) strips `password` from each config before responding, and the comment says so — *"Remove password from config object"*. But the destructure names only that one field: ``` const { password, ...configWithoutPassword } = config; ``` `encryptedPassword` is not removed, so it ships to the client in every config listing, including the shared-config branch at `:51`. **Scope, stated honestly:** the query is keyed on the caller's own `userId`, so this is **not** cross-user exposure and is lower severity than the other two filed today. The issue is that an encrypted credential reaches the browser when nothing there needs it — which widens what an XSS or a stolen token yields, and `encryptPassword(password, userId)` (`config.ts:101`) derives from a value the holder already knows. **Fix.** Drop `encryptedPassword` alongside `password` in both places, or build an explicit allow-list of fields to return rather than a deny-list of fields to remove — a deny-list is why this was missed when the field was added. Found while building aw-agent; verified against `main` on 2026-09-19.

ENG-2072 Scheduled work-plan autocomplete forcing doesn't distinguish attended vs unattended turns (ENG-2058 follow-up)

While merging ENG-2058 (PR #3004, "Force autocomplete on work plans for scheduled sessions"), CodeRabbit's review flagged a real gap that I independently verified rather than took on faith: **The gap:** `createWorkPlan`, `modifyWorkPlan`, and `applyPredefinedWorkPlan` (backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts) now force `workPlan.autocomplete = true` whenever `session.sessionType === 'scheduled'`. But `sessionType` records how a session was *created*, not whether the *current turn* is attended. **Confirmed reachable path:** a user can open a schedule-created session from the customer portal's "Scheduled" sidebar tab (`ChatSidebar.tsx`) and type a new live message into that same session (`useAgentModeChat.tsx:429-436` reuses the existing sessionId, does not spawn a fresh one). If that live message leads the model to call `create_work_plan`/`modify_work_plan`/`launch_predefined_work_plan`, it now runs hands-off (no per-step approval pause) even though a real person is watching and expects step-by-step approval. **Precedent:** the codebase hit this exact confusion once before and documented it — `chatbotService.ts:4653` and `agentModeSystemPrompt.ts:689` (ENG-803) explicitly warn: "sessionType can be 'scheduled' here — a user may open a schedule-created session in the sidebar and keep chatting in it — but this turn is ATTENDED." ENG-803's fix threads a resolved, call-site-specific signal (`publishAuthorized`, tri-state) rather than inferring attendance from `sessionType` alone — but that signal is scoped to the publish-authorization prompt block only, not wired anywhere near `createWorkPlan`/`modifyWorkPlan`/`applyPredefinedWorkPlan`. **Why this shipped anyway:** ENG-2058 fixes a confirmed, currently-recurring production incident (daily oncall failures on the Luma Event Lead Engagement schedule). The residual risk here is narrow (requires deliberately reopening a scheduled session's chat and continuing it), soft (autocomplete is an LLM-instruction UX switch, not a code-enforced gate — confirmed via this same PR's security-lens review), and any genuinely irreversible action (publishing, sending, spending) is already gated separately by the autopublishAuthorized/ENG-827/ENG-803 system, untouched by this change. Blocking the confirmed fix on a full architectural addition wasn't the right trade. **The actual fix needed:** thread a real per-turn "is this an unattended scheduled/test run" signal through the tool-dispatch context (`ToolContext` in mcp/client/toolRegistry.ts and mcp/server/registry.ts, populated from runVerifiedChatInner/runScheduledChat vs the interactive generateResponse path) and check THAT instead of `session.sessionType` in the three call sites above.
