ENG-2079 A v0 correction that returns no new version fails the whole page, bypassing the 'proceeding without it' fallback

## Summary The three *enhancement* corrections — Meta Pixel Lead event, Google Ads conversion, bridge-out redirect — each end in an explicit fallback: ```ts pixelLeadEventVerified = pixelCheck.ok; if (!pixelCheck.ok) { console.warn(`... still missing ... — proceeding without it`); } ``` A page missing them is **degraded, not broken**, and is supposed to ship. That fallback is unreachable when v0 answers the correction with no new version, because the failure happens at the *await*, not at the check: ```ts versionId = await waitForCompletedV0Version( // throws on deadline v0, chatId, `v0 correction (pixel lead event) for /${slug}`, { ..., afterVersionId: versionId }); continue; ``` `waitForCompletedV0Version` throws, the outer catch marks the page `failed`. ## Two compounding problems 1. The correction is gated only on `effectivePixelId` — not on whether the page actually has a lead-capture form. For a page without one, "fix the lead capture form" is unsatisfiable, so no new version ever arrives. 2. An unanswered correction is fatal to the entire page. A missing pixel is explicitly tolerable; a missing *answer about* the missing pixel is not. That asymmetry is unintended. ## Impact Any site **with a Meta pixel** where v0 fails to wire the Lead event fires this correction. If v0 does not answer, the whole page generation fails after \~17 minutes, with an error that blames v0: ``` No completed version in v0 chat after ~16 minutes — v0 is still generating or has stalled. ``` Observed live twice (env2), both reaching `attempt 34/34` then `failed`, on pages that had already generated and validated fine. ## Fix `awaitOptionalV0Correction(label, wait)` — returns the corrected version id, or `undefined` when no new version arrived. `undefined` falls through to the existing "proceeding without it" path. Applied to all six enhancement-correction sites (3 on the sub-page path, 3 on the root path). Deliberately **not** applied to the `validateV0Output` correction, where un-correctable output genuinely must not ship — those two waits stay fatal. PR: [https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/pull/3017]() ## Verification Regression test asserts a page whose correction is never answered still reaches `deployed` with `pixelLeadEventVerified: false`. Mutation-checked: reverting gives `Expected: "deployed" / Received: "failed"` — the exact production behaviour.

ENG-449 Auto-wire Meta Pixel + Conversions API (server-side) into Emma-generated landers at generation time

## Why (Harsha, 2026-07-21) Every Emma-built lander that fronts a paid campaign needs Meta conversion tracking wired **automatically at generation time** — not set up by hand afterward. Manual pixel setup is the current state and it's the source of "paid campaigns optimizing blind" bugs (see [ENG-443](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-443/rankai-book-a-demo-lander-no-crm-capture-0-meta-conversion-signal-paid) RankAI book-a-demo: 0 Meta conversion signal; [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject) was the Google/GTM half). This is the durable programmatic fix for the Meta side. ## Research verdict on "PixelFlow" ([pixelflow.so]()) PixelFlow is a **no-code dashboard tool** (Webflow/Framer/Squarespace/WordPress apps) that runs Meta Pixel + server-side Conversions API (CAPI) with browser↔server event dedup. It exposes a "Programmatic Tracking API" for **sending events**, but pixel **provisioning** (create a config per site, set Dataset ID + CAPI token) is dashboard-first — not designed for "spin up a new tracked lander via API." Conclusion: **don't depend on PixelFlow for provisioning.** The programmatic path we own is to inject the **Meta Pixel base code + wire CAPI directly** at lander generation, mirroring what [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject) did for GTM/GA4. (If we still want PixelFlow's dedup convenience, it's an optional client-side add, not the backbone.) ## Approach At lander generation (the same seam [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject) uses to inject GTM): given the campaign's Meta pixel/dataset ID, (1) inject the Meta Pixel base snippet + a standard `Lead` event on form submit, and (2) fire the matching server-side CAPI `Lead` event from our lead-capture backend with an `event_id` shared with the browser event for dedup. Pixel/dataset ID resolution depends on [ENG-399](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-399/call-meta-marketing-api-dataset-list-broken-meta-100-nonexisting-field) (call_meta_marketing_api DATASET LIST is broken → pixel discovery impossible in-product) and on the Meta account being connected — so this is partly blocked until [ENG-399](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-399/call-meta-marketing-api-dataset-list-broken-meta-100-nonexisting-field) lands and Meta is connected; the injection + CAPI-emit scaffolding can be built and unit-tested behind a mocked Meta boundary now. ## Acceptance criteria (HUMAN-WRITTEN) 1. When a lander is generated with a Meta pixel/dataset ID present, the deployed HTML contains the Meta Pixel base code and a `Lead` standard event fired on lead-form submit (asserted in a generation test). 2. On lead-form submit, the backend emits a server-side CAPI `Lead` event to the correct dataset, sharing an `event_id` with the browser event so Meta dedups (assert the CAPI call payload + shared event_id with a mocked Meta CAPI boundary). 3. If no pixel/dataset ID is resolvable (e.g. [ENG-399](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-399/call-meta-marketing-api-dataset-list-broken-meta-100-nonexisting-field) unresolved or Meta not connected), the lander still generates successfully and the missing-pixel condition is surfaced loudly (logged + returned in the generation result), never silently skipped. 4. No regression to the existing GTM/GA4 injection from [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject). ## Links Depends on [ENG-399](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-399/call-meta-marketing-api-dataset-list-broken-meta-100-nonexisting-field) (pixel discovery) · complements [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject) (GTM auto-inject, done), [ENG-239](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-239/auto-append-utm-parameters-to-every-emma-deployed-ad-campaign-make-ai) (UTM auto-append, done), [ENG-327](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-327/user-settable-landing-page-utms-pass-through-decoration-from-rankai) (user-settable UTMs), [ENG-443](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-443/rankai-book-a-demo-lander-no-crm-capture-0-meta-conversion-signal-paid) (RankAI 0-conversion-signal).

ENG-449 Auto-wire Meta Pixel + Conversions API (server-side) into Emma-generated landers at generation time

## Why (Harsha, 2026-07-21) Every Emma-built lander that fronts a paid campaign needs Meta conversion tracking wired **automatically at generation time** — not set up by hand afterward. Manual pixel setup is the current state and it's the source of "paid campaigns optimizing blind" bugs (see [ENG-443](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-443/rankai-book-a-demo-lander-no-crm-capture-0-meta-conversion-signal-paid) RankAI book-a-demo: 0 Meta conversion signal; [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject) was the Google/GTM half). This is the durable programmatic fix for the Meta side. ## Research verdict on "PixelFlow" ([pixelflow.so]()) PixelFlow is a **no-code dashboard tool** (Webflow/Framer/Squarespace/WordPress apps) that runs Meta Pixel + server-side Conversions API (CAPI) with browser↔server event dedup. It exposes a "Programmatic Tracking API" for **sending events**, but pixel **provisioning** (create a config per site, set Dataset ID + CAPI token) is dashboard-first — not designed for "spin up a new tracked lander via API." Conclusion: **don't depend on PixelFlow for provisioning.** The programmatic path we own is to inject the **Meta Pixel base code + wire CAPI directly** at lander generation, mirroring what [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject) did for GTM/GA4. (If we still want PixelFlow's dedup convenience, it's an optional client-side add, not the backbone.) ## Approach At lander generation (the same seam [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject) uses to inject GTM): given the campaign's Meta pixel/dataset ID, (1) inject the Meta Pixel base snippet + a standard `Lead` event on form submit, and (2) fire the matching server-side CAPI `Lead` event from our lead-capture backend with an `event_id` shared with the browser event for dedup. Pixel/dataset ID resolution depends on [ENG-399](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-399/call-meta-marketing-api-dataset-list-broken-meta-100-nonexisting-field) (call_meta_marketing_api DATASET LIST is broken → pixel discovery impossible in-product) and on the Meta account being connected — so this is partly blocked until [ENG-399](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-399/call-meta-marketing-api-dataset-list-broken-meta-100-nonexisting-field) lands and Meta is connected; the injection + CAPI-emit scaffolding can be built and unit-tested behind a mocked Meta boundary now. ## Acceptance criteria (HUMAN-WRITTEN) 1. When a lander is generated with a Meta pixel/dataset ID present, the deployed HTML contains the Meta Pixel base code and a `Lead` standard event fired on lead-form submit (asserted in a generation test). 2. On lead-form submit, the backend emits a server-side CAPI `Lead` event to the correct dataset, sharing an `event_id` with the browser event so Meta dedups (assert the CAPI call payload + shared event_id with a mocked Meta CAPI boundary). 3. If no pixel/dataset ID is resolvable (e.g. [ENG-399](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-399/call-meta-marketing-api-dataset-list-broken-meta-100-nonexisting-field) unresolved or Meta not connected), the lander still generates successfully and the missing-pixel condition is surfaced loudly (logged + returned in the generation result), never silently skipped. 4. No regression to the existing GTM/GA4 injection from [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject). ## Links Depends on [ENG-399](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-399/call-meta-marketing-api-dataset-list-broken-meta-100-nonexisting-field) (pixel discovery) · complements [ENG-334](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-334/emma-generated-landers-ship-with-zero-conversion-tracking-auto-inject) (GTM auto-inject, done), [ENG-239](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-239/auto-append-utm-parameters-to-every-emma-deployed-ad-campaign-make-ai) (UTM auto-append, done), [ENG-327](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-327/user-settable-landing-page-utms-pass-through-decoration-from-rankai) (user-settable UTMs), [ENG-443](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-443/rankai-book-a-demo-lander-no-crm-capture-0-meta-conversion-signal-paid) (RankAI 0-conversion-signal).

ENG-1343 Custom Audience multi-batch upload (>10k rows) fails: session key nested incorrectly in payload

## What's wrong `MetaService.uploadCustomAudienceUsers` (backend/src/services/metaService.ts, ~line 2112) chunks uploads over `CUSTOM_AUDIENCE_USERS_BATCH_SIZE` (10,000) into sequential session-batched requests per Meta's documented multi-batch protocol. The `session` object is currently nested **inside** `payload`: ```js const result = await audience.createUser([], { payload: { schema, data: chunk, session: { session_id, batch_seq, last_batch_flag, estimated_num_total }, }, }); ``` Meta's Marketing API rejects this: `session` must be a **sibling top-level parameter** to `payload`, not nested inside it. ## Live evidence (2026-08-18) Uploading a 12,249-row Custom Audience list to Haven AI's ad account (`act_1842363582956923`, audience `120248879984780173`) via `POST /api/emma/meta-ads/marketing-api` (UPLOAD_USERS) hit: ```json {"success":false,"message":"(#100) Invalid keys \"session\" were found in param \"payload\".","error":"(#100) Invalid keys \"session\" were found in param \"payload\"."} ``` This is almost certainly the first production upload to ever exceed 10,000 rows — every existing Haven/Every/RankAI audience upload has been well under that (the largest prior Haven audience, `haven_meta_custom_audience_7k.csv`, was ~7k rows, single-batch). The single-batch path (`rows.length <= BATCH_SIZE`) is unaffected and works correctly — verified live, that's how the same 12,249-row upload was actually completed (split client-side into two ~6,125-row calls to route around the bug). ## Suggested fix In `uploadCustomAudienceUsers`'s multi-batch branch, move `session` out of `payload` to be a sibling key in the params object passed to `audience.createUser`: ```js const result = await audience.createUser([], { payload: { schema, data: chunk }, session: { session_id: sessionId, batch_seq: batchSeq, last_batch_flag: isLastBatch, estimated_num_total: rows.length }, }); ``` Same fix likely needed in `deleteCustomAudienceUsers` and `replaceCustomAudienceUsers` (metaService.ts) if they share the same session-batching shape — check both. ## Acceptance criteria (behavioral contract) 1. Uploading a payload with more rows than `CUSTOM_AUDIENCE_USERS_BATCH_SIZE` (10,000) to `uploadCustomAudienceUsers` succeeds without a `(#100) Invalid keys "session"` error — verify via a test that mocks the Meta SDK's `createUser` and asserts the params object passed has `session` as a sibling of `payload`, not nested inside it. 2. A payload at or under the batch size continues to send a single request with no `session` key at all (unchanged existing behavior — don't regress the working path). 3. The last batch (and only the last batch) is sent with `last_batch_flag: true`; all others `false`; `session_id` is identical across all batches in one upload. 4. Apply/verify the same fix for `deleteCustomAudienceUsers` and `replaceCustomAudienceUsers` if they use the same nested-session shape. ## Why no one caught this Existing unit tests presumably mock `CustomAudience.createUser` and assert on inputs the test itself constructed — likely never exercised the real >10k branch against Meta's actual validation, so a request-shape bug in the multi-batch path had nothing forcing it to be correct. Live traffic simply never sent >10k rows before.

ENG-1271 No signal distinguishes real customer usage from staff operating a delegated session — caused two real misclassifications

## What's wrong Nothing in the current account data distinguishes "the customer is actually using the product" from "AgentWeb staff are operating it on the customer's behalf through a delegated admin session." This isn't academic — it caused two real misclassifications during the August 2026 audit. Haven and Every were both initially proposed as good pricing-conversation candidates because their campaigns looked healthy — but Haven shows 126M tokens of usage across 5 months with zero logins ever recorded, and Every shows the same pattern. Both are staff-operated, not customer-used. It took manual digging to catch this, twice, before the pattern was corrected. ## Why urgent This is a real, recurring blind spot in how the business reads its own accounts. Any future decision made from "usage looks healthy" without this signal risks repeating the exact same mistake — and it already did, twice, in one session. ## Proposed shape Add a per-account self-operation-rate signal: the ratio of activity that originates from the customer's own authenticated session versus a staff/admin delegated session. At minimum, this needs the token-usage/activity data to be tagged with which session type generated it (likely already distinguishable from existing session/auth records — this may be closer to a reporting/aggregation change than a new tracking mechanism, worth checking before assuming new instrumentation is needed). ## Acceptance criteria 1. Given an account where all activity originates from customer-authenticated sessions, the self-operation rate reads at or near 100%. 2. Given an account where all activity originates from staff-delegated sessions (Haven's actual pattern — heavy usage, zero customer logins), the self-operation rate reads at or near 0%, correctly distinguishing it from genuine heavy customer usage. 3. Haven and Every's actual historical data are used as regression fixtures — replayed against the new signal, both correctly read as staff-operated, not customer-engaged. 4. The signal is visible per-account (not just computable via a one-off manual query) so this class of misclassification doesn't require a manual audit to catch next time. ## Test cases * Unit test: all-customer-session account → high self-operation rate. * Unit test: all-staff-session account → low self-operation rate. * Regression: Haven's and Every's real data, replayed, correctly classified as staff-operated. * Mixed case: an account with both customer and staff activity produces a rate reflecting the real mix, not defaulting to one extreme. ## Complexity ledger Complexity: Medium — likely an aggregation/reporting change over existing session-type data rather than new instrumentation; scope should shrink further once it's confirmed which of those two it actually is. ## Source AgentWeb Landscape Study — August 2026 Amendment, "unsexy things" #10. ## Deep-audit disposition — 2026-09-17 **Blocked.** Exact gate: [ENG-1501](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1501/requires-me-choose-eng-1271-self-operation-data-model-and-approve-any) must choose the activity-provenance data model and approve any historical backfill; current token records cannot compute the mixed self-operation ratio. Next check: after that decision, replay Haven/Every plus all-self/all-staff/mixed fixtures.

ENG-1250 Usage accounting v2: one auditable spend ledger and admission gate for every AgentWeb-paid call

## Outcome Implement one org-level accounting architecture in which every **AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable** upstream call is recorded exactly once, priced honestly, visible in a spend history, and applied to the same monthly usage limit. This is the end-to-end architecture contract requested by Harsha. It replaces the current split between `tokenUsage.totalCost`, the daily `AW-UsageRecords` aggregates, the effectively dead `extraCostUsage` rail, vendor-specific counters, and unmetered vendor calls. ## Billing boundary Debit the user's/org's monthly usage balance when: * AgentWeb pays an upstream and the action is attributable to a billing subject. * The cost is measured by the vendor, or a versioned allocated rate exists. Do not debit when: * The customer pays through their own connected account (for example Meta ad spend or customer-owned SaaS/API usage). * The cost is shared platform overhead without a reviewed allocation policy. * The unit has no price. Unpriced paid egress must fail closed or be explicitly allowlisted as platform-funded; it must never become a silent $0 charge. ## Architecture ### 1. Immutable spend events are the source of truth Create an append-only, per-call usage event store ([ENG-702](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-702/make-vendor-usage-writes-idempotent-and-fail-loud-gate-before-any) data-plane gate) rather than treating a mutable monthly counter or daily aggregate as authoritative. Required event fields: * `eventId` / idempotency key * `occurredAt`, billing month * `billingUserId`, `orgId`, `actingUserId`, optional `onBehalfOf` * provider, operation, feature, unit, quantity * `costMicroUsd` * cost source: `measured | allocated` * rate-card version when allocated * session/task/run/request references * lifecycle: `reserved | settled | voided` * external vendor reference when available Retries with the same idempotency key must return the original event and add $0. ### 2. One charging API All paid egress goes through one service; callers may not write the ledger or monthly counter directly. Conceptual contract: 1. Resolve the org billing subject. 2. Classify the call as AgentWeb-paid, customer-paid, or platform overhead. 3. Resolve a measured cost or versioned allocated rate. 4. Reserve known/estimated spend when practical. 5. Check admission against settled spend + outstanding reservations. 6. Execute the vendor call. 7. Settle actual spend or void the reservation. 8. Atomically persist the idempotent event and update the billing-subject/month aggregate. LLM, image/video, v0, X, search, enrichment, voice, rendering, and future vendor adapters must use the same service. ### 3. Monthly state is a projection, not an independent counter Maintain an atomic `billingUserId + month` projection for fast admission: * settled chargeable spend * active reservations * included monthly allowance * purchased credits * admin grants/reversals * migration adjustment * remaining usable balance * current policy mode Invariant: summing immutable settled events must reproduce the monthly spend projection within one micro-dollar. Raw spend is always preserved. Credits and migration adjustments change available allowance; they never erase or rewrite spend. ### 4. Admission semantics * A new job is admitted only when remaining balance covers its reservation or the policy explicitly permits an overrun. * Work admitted before the boundary may finish under the existing admitted-work rule. * Fixed-price calls reserve the exact allocated rate. * Variable-cost calls reserve a documented maximum/estimate and settle the actual amount. * Concurrent requests use conditional/transactional writes so two calls cannot both spend the same remaining balance. * `full_choice | optimized | paused` is derived from this one monthly projection; token volume remains an analytical dimension, not a second competing gate. ### 5. Versioned vendor rate registry One reviewed registry defines provider, operation, unit, rate, currency, effective dates, and source. Pricing rules: * Vendor-reported cost wins when available. * Shared wallets/subscriptions use an explicit allocated rate ([ENG-703](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-703/set-the-allocated-vendor-rate-card-blocks-every-metering-adapter-from)). * A price change creates a new version; historical events retain the rate version used. * No adapter embeds an independent dollar literal. ### 6. Coverage Bring existing slices onto the charging API: * LLM providers, embeddings, image/video * X ([ENG-664](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-664/meter-x-twitter-api-usage-cost-per-account-and-per-tool)) * v0 ([ENG-694](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-694/meter-v0-landing-page-generation-including-the-unguarded-iterate-path)) * [You.com]() and Google CSE ([ENG-695](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-695/meter-paid-web-search-youcom-google-custom-search-and-thread-the)) * Apollo and [enrich.so]() ([ENG-696](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-696/bring-apollo-and-enrichso-onto-the-ledger-and-close-the-six-bypassed)) * ElevenLabs, 2captcha, Placid ([ENG-698](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-698/meter-the-single-call-site-per-unit-vendors-elevenlabs-2captcha-placid)) * Remotion Lambda ([ENG-699](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-699/meter-remotion-lambda-renders-at-submission-time)) * other AgentWeb-paid voice/search/media/email vendors identified by [ENG-701](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-701/make-metering-coverage-a-ci-fact-instead-of-an-audit-artifact) The CI paid-egress registry must fail when a new paid client/call site has no charging adapter or explicit platform-funded exemption. ### 7. Read models and product UX Produce daily/provider/member/feature/session aggregates from immutable events. The org usage screen must show: * billing subject and pooled-org behavior * raw spend versus adjustments and usable balance * daily trend * spend by provider, product feature, and acting member * reservations/in-flight spend * why the account is optimized or paused * reset date and purchased-credit history No admin should need direct DynamoDB inspection to explain a pause. ### 8. Reconciliation Run two independent checks: * Internal: immutable event sum = monthly projection = dashboard total. * External: vendor invoice/wallet/usage export versus attributed ledger totals, allowing only documented timing or allocation differences. Drift above one cent or the vendor-specific threshold alerts and prevents enabling enforcement for that provider. A successful vendor call without a settled/voided event is an operational error. ### 9. Migration and rollout 1. Land schema/idempotency behind the explicit data-plane approval gate. 2. Dual-write old and new rails in observe-only mode. 3. Reconcile LLMs first; the existing gate cannot move until the crater class is resolved. 4. Add vendor adapters one family at a time. 5. Run at least seven days of shadow reconciliation and boundary/concurrency tests. 6. Switch admission to the new monthly projection. 7. Observe a month reset and credit purchase/reversal. 8. Stop writes to `extraCostUsage` and the legacy independent cost counter. 9. Delete legacy paths only after rollback evidence and one clean period boundary. ## Complexity impact Adds one idempotent event rail, one monthly projection, and one rate registry; removes multiple counters, special cases, and manual reconciliation paths. Net result must be fewer charging paths than today. ## Acceptance criteria (from Harsha's request) 1. Every AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable API cost is deducted from the same org monthly usage balance exactly once. 2. Customer-paid integrations and unallocated platform overhead are not charged. 3. A pause is explainable to the cent from per-call events, including provider, feature, acting member, and adjustment history. 4. Vendor spend, immutable events, monthly projection, and dashboard reconcile within the defined threshold. 5. Retries, concurrent calls, failed calls, reservations, refunds/reversals, org inheritance, and month rollover have automated tests. 6. No production enforcement moves to the new rail until shadow reconciliation passes and Harsha approves the data-plane change. 7. The legacy `extraCostUsage` and independent counter paths are retired rather than maintained as fallbacks.

The PR's 2-second `Promise.race` only stops waiting. It does not cancel the underlying query, so late or large queries can continue consuming resources. This can cause a production notification outage under high lead volume. **Resolution** Use a bounded, owner-scoped lookup for notification enrichment, preferably a direct ID lookup or a capped query. Retain submitted values when the cap is reached. Make the lookup and the ads snapshot query cancellation-aware, and abort all in-flight work when the overall deadline expires. Phase 0, lands first — F2 depends on this landing cleanly since both touch `agentModeService.ts`. **Branch/PR title: use this ticket's id (F1-equivalent) only, never** [ENG-1816](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1816/run-emma-on-customer-funded-claude-code-and-codex-subscriptions). ## Goal Land seven named seams with **no behavior change**. `route` is always `agentweb` after this PR. Every later [ENG-1816](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1816/run-emma-on-customer-funded-claude-code-and-codex-subscriptions) ticket fills one pre-made slot instead of touching `callLLM` again. ## The seven contracts (new dir `backend/src/services/funding/`) 1. `RunFunding` — plain data `{route, connectionId?, provider?, fallback, ownerUserId, billingUserId, resolvedAt}`. Resolved once per run at every entry point (interactive, scheduled, work-plan, API/MCP, Slack/email). Carried across the worker fork as a field on `GenerateMarketingResponseParams` (same shape as the existing `publishAuthorizationOverride`, [ENG-827](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-827/scheduled-run-publish-gate-is-ambiguous-agent-refuses-required-publish)) — `generateSessionResponse` already has \~20 positional params, so this cannot be a 21st. Ambient inside each process via `AsyncLocalStorage` (precedent: `twitterService.ts`'s `xActingUserStore`). Required because the fork worker multiplexes many customers over one IPC channel (`pendingRequests`/`sessionToRequestId` maps) — a module global would leak funding across customers. 2. `LlmConnection` — type + store interface only (`kind: 'api_key'|'claude_subscription'|'codex_subscription'`, `secretRef`, `status`, `health`). A1 builds the real CRUD. 3. `LlmTransport` — `send(model, messages, options)`. `OpenRouterPlatformTransport` extracted from `callLLM`, **bounded to send/validate/retry only** (the client call, `assertOpenRouterResponseHasChoices`, the retry loop). Param construction (provider order/ignore rules, Gemini schema sanitizer, cache breakpoints, the [ENG-1831](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1831/extract-model-capability-metadata-and-request-param-selection-out-of) parameter chain) stays in `agentModeService.ts` — those rules are empirically verified (e.g. the `'Google'` vs `'google-ai-studio'` BYOK slot inversion, confirmed by 10 live A/B calls) and moving them risks silently changing routing for no [ENG-1816](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1816/run-emma-on-customer-funded-claude-code-and-codex-subscriptions) benefit. 4. `RunBackend` — `EmmaLoopBackend` wraps today's `generateMarketingResponse` unchanged. Chosen in the worker. 5. `recordLlmUsage(runFunding, usage)` — the funding branch sits **above** `meterWithResolvedBilling`, not inside it: that whole funnel (`recordUsage` → `AW-UsageRecords` + `AW-SpendEvents`, `incrementUserTokenUsage` → the enforced cap) is fire-and-forget and fail-open at every layer, so a check placed inside it fails silently. `route==='agentweb'` (and `undefined`, counted via a greppable marker, not failed closed): today's path, byte-identical. Any other route: **touches no existing rail** — not `recordUsage`, not `incrementUserTokenUsage`, not the spend-event path — and hands the attempt to the `AttemptUsageJournal` port instead. This is forced, not a stylistic choice: `AW-SpendProjection` now has a live production writer (PR [AgentWebPro/agentweb#3003](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/review/eng-1250-3b-production-projection-writer-backfill-unblocks-96-2f956c158123)) that folds every `lifecycle:"settled"` event into that subject's `settledMicroUsd` with no funding dimension — a customer-funded call that wrote a settled event would silently debit the customer's own AgentWeb cap the moment [ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250/usage-accounting-v2-one-auditable-spend-ledger-and-admission-gate-for)'s enforcement flag goes global. 6. `decideFallback(errorClass, runFunding)` — signature + one invariant test only: never returns `switch_to_agentweb` when `runFunding.fallback === 'stop'`. Not wired into any path yet. 7. `AttemptUsageJournal` — port + type only, no-op bound implementation. The type mirrors the Attempt record already spec'd for the `AW-AgentRuntimeState` data-plane request (`run#`/`attempt#`, funding source/principal/connection/epoch, requested vs actual model/backend, usage, L/C, `entitlementObs`, `settlementState`, `spendEventId?`). A3 binds the real implementation once that table clears data-plane approval. ## Also fixes (customer-caused spend currently booked to "system") Three call sites pass `usageContext` with no `userId`, so they escape both billing and the funding policy: * `wasStepRemovalUserAuthorized` (`agentModeService.ts`) * `restyleContent` / `generateBlogContent` (`controllers/blog.ts`) * chatbot KB embeddings (`chatbotService.ts` — has no metering call at all today, needs one added) Each becomes a two-line fix once the ambient run store exists: read the run's owner from it. ## Flags — data, not env vars `LLM_BYOK` and `LLM_CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION` (each with an allowlist) live in one `AW-Settings` row read at run entry with a 60s cache and an all-off fallback — **not** EB environment variables. This is forced: prod EB (`Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3`) is already at CloudFormation's 4096-char `EnvironmentVariables` limit (67 vars, \~4,057–4,152 chars) — every config-update route fails identically today (tracked as [ENG-2071](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2071/repair-eb-service-role-s3cfn-permissions-so-prod-env-config-updates), currently misdiagnosed as an IAM issue; the real cause is the size limit). No env-var-based flag can ship until someone frees \~700 chars there (lead: `OKAREO_API_KEY` at 856 chars). Data-backed flags are also independently better: flipping a per-customer allowlist becomes a write, not a rolling restart. ## Done when 1. **Characterization (requests):** a recorded fixture of today's `params` (tool call with 60+ filtered tools, Gemini schema sanitization, an Anthropic call with cache breakpoints, a fallback chain, web search) is byte-identical before/after. 2. **Characterization (metering):** for an `agentweb` run, the exact args reaching `usageRecordDb.incrementUsage`, the spend-event write, and `incrementUserTokenUsage` are unchanged. 3. **Negative test:** a synthetic `route: 'api_key'` usage record writes no `AW-UsageRecords` row, no spend event, no cap charge — only the journal port — asserted on real DynamoDB params, not mock-argument assertions. 4. **Ambient propagation:** funding set at run entry is visible to a nested tool-internal `callLLM` inside the worker, and two concurrent runs on the worker never see each other's funding. 5. Three leak-site tests, same real-params standard. 6. With the settings row absent/malformed/unreadable, everything resolves to all-off/`agentweb`. 7. `decideFallback` invariant test passes. 8. Existing `__tests__/agentMode/characterization/*` suites pass untouched. Cite Anurag Seth: this design's `recordLlmUsage` branch is what makes [ENG-1816](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1816/run-emma-on-customer-funded-claude-code-and-codex-subscriptions) the first real caller of `spendChargingService`'s `customer_paid` classification, which has existed since [ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250/usage-accounting-v2-one-auditable-spend-ledger-and-admission-gate-for) with zero callers to date. --- ## Implementation status (2026-09-23) All 7 contracts + the flags module implemented on `mvarma/eng-2102-f1-shared-funding-skeleton` (off fresh `origin/main` @ `4c839d309`), 3 local commits, nothing pushed yet. **Done-when checklist:** 1. ENG-1250 Usage accounting v2: one auditable spend ledger and admission gate for every AgentWeb-paid call

## Outcome Implement one org-level accounting architecture in which every **AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable** upstream call is recorded exactly once, priced honestly, visible in a spend history, and applied to the same monthly usage limit. This is the end-to-end architecture contract requested by Harsha. It replaces the current split between `tokenUsage.totalCost`, the daily `AW-UsageRecords` aggregates, the effectively dead `extraCostUsage` rail, vendor-specific counters, and unmetered vendor calls. ## Billing boundary Debit the user's/org's monthly usage balance when: * AgentWeb pays an upstream and the action is attributable to a billing subject. * The cost is measured by the vendor, or a versioned allocated rate exists. Do not debit when: * The customer pays through their own connected account (for example Meta ad spend or customer-owned SaaS/API usage). * The cost is shared platform overhead without a reviewed allocation policy. * The unit has no price. Unpriced paid egress must fail closed or be explicitly allowlisted as platform-funded; it must never become a silent $0 charge. ## Architecture ### 1. Immutable spend events are the source of truth Create an append-only, per-call usage event store ([ENG-702](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-702/make-vendor-usage-writes-idempotent-and-fail-loud-gate-before-any) data-plane gate) rather than treating a mutable monthly counter or daily aggregate as authoritative. Required event fields: * `eventId` / idempotency key * `occurredAt`, billing month * `billingUserId`, `orgId`, `actingUserId`, optional `onBehalfOf` * provider, operation, feature, unit, quantity * `costMicroUsd` * cost source: `measured | allocated` * rate-card version when allocated * session/task/run/request references * lifecycle: `reserved | settled | voided` * external vendor reference when available Retries with the same idempotency key must return the original event and add $0. ### 2. One charging API All paid egress goes through one service; callers may not write the ledger or monthly counter directly. Conceptual contract: 1. Resolve the org billing subject. 2. Classify the call as AgentWeb-paid, customer-paid, or platform overhead. 3. Resolve a measured cost or versioned allocated rate. 4. Reserve known/estimated spend when practical. 5. Check admission against settled spend + outstanding reservations. 6. Execute the vendor call. 7. Settle actual spend or void the reservation. 8. Atomically persist the idempotent event and update the billing-subject/month aggregate. LLM, image/video, v0, X, search, enrichment, voice, rendering, and future vendor adapters must use the same service. ### 3. Monthly state is a projection, not an independent counter Maintain an atomic `billingUserId + month` projection for fast admission: * settled chargeable spend * active reservations * included monthly allowance * purchased credits * admin grants/reversals * migration adjustment * remaining usable balance * current policy mode Invariant: summing immutable settled events must reproduce the monthly spend projection within one micro-dollar. Raw spend is always preserved. Credits and migration adjustments change available allowance; they never erase or rewrite spend. ### 4. Admission semantics * A new job is admitted only when remaining balance covers its reservation or the policy explicitly permits an overrun. * Work admitted before the boundary may finish under the existing admitted-work rule. * Fixed-price calls reserve the exact allocated rate. * Variable-cost calls reserve a documented maximum/estimate and settle the actual amount. * Concurrent requests use conditional/transactional writes so two calls cannot both spend the same remaining balance. * `full_choice | optimized | paused` is derived from this one monthly projection; token volume remains an analytical dimension, not a second competing gate. ### 5. Versioned vendor rate registry One reviewed registry defines provider, operation, unit, rate, currency, effective dates, and source. Pricing rules: * Vendor-reported cost wins when available. * Shared wallets/subscriptions use an explicit allocated rate ([ENG-703](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-703/set-the-allocated-vendor-rate-card-blocks-every-metering-adapter-from)). * A price change creates a new version; historical events retain the rate version used. * No adapter embeds an independent dollar literal. ### 6. Coverage Bring existing slices onto the charging API: * LLM providers, embeddings, image/video * X ([ENG-664](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-664/meter-x-twitter-api-usage-cost-per-account-and-per-tool)) * v0 ([ENG-694](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-694/meter-v0-landing-page-generation-including-the-unguarded-iterate-path)) * [You.com]() and Google CSE ([ENG-695](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-695/meter-paid-web-search-youcom-google-custom-search-and-thread-the)) * Apollo and [enrich.so]() ([ENG-696](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-696/bring-apollo-and-enrichso-onto-the-ledger-and-close-the-six-bypassed)) * ElevenLabs, 2captcha, Placid ([ENG-698](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-698/meter-the-single-call-site-per-unit-vendors-elevenlabs-2captcha-placid)) * Remotion Lambda ([ENG-699](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-699/meter-remotion-lambda-renders-at-submission-time)) * other AgentWeb-paid voice/search/media/email vendors identified by [ENG-701](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-701/make-metering-coverage-a-ci-fact-instead-of-an-audit-artifact) The CI paid-egress registry must fail when a new paid client/call site has no charging adapter or explicit platform-funded exemption. ### 7. Read models and product UX Produce daily/provider/member/feature/session aggregates from immutable events. The org usage screen must show: * billing subject and pooled-org behavior * raw spend versus adjustments and usable balance * daily trend * spend by provider, product feature, and acting member * reservations/in-flight spend * why the account is optimized or paused * reset date and purchased-credit history No admin should need direct DynamoDB inspection to explain a pause. ### 8. Reconciliation Run two independent checks: * Internal: immutable event sum = monthly projection = dashboard total. * External: vendor invoice/wallet/usage export versus attributed ledger totals, allowing only documented timing or allocation differences. Drift above one cent or the vendor-specific threshold alerts and prevents enabling enforcement for that provider. A successful vendor call without a settled/voided event is an operational error. ### 9. Migration and rollout 1. Land schema/idempotency behind the explicit data-plane approval gate. 2. Dual-write old and new rails in observe-only mode. 3. Reconcile LLMs first; the existing gate cannot move until the crater class is resolved. 4. Add vendor adapters one family at a time. 5. Run at least seven days of shadow reconciliation and boundary/concurrency tests. 6. Switch admission to the new monthly projection. 7. Observe a month reset and credit purchase/reversal. 8. Stop writes to `extraCostUsage` and the legacy independent cost counter. 9. Delete legacy paths only after rollback evidence and one clean period boundary. ## Complexity impact Adds one idempotent event rail, one monthly projection, and one rate registry; removes multiple counters, special cases, and manual reconciliation paths. Net result must be fewer charging paths than today. ## Acceptance criteria (from Harsha's request) 1. Every AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable API cost is deducted from the same org monthly usage balance exactly once. 2. Customer-paid integrations and unallocated platform overhead are not charged. 3. A pause is explainable to the cent from per-call events, including provider, feature, acting member, and adjustment history. 4. Vendor spend, immutable events, monthly projection, and dashboard reconcile within the defined threshold. 5. Retries, concurrent calls, failed calls, reservations, refunds/reversals, org inheritance, and month rollover have automated tests. 6. No production enforcement moves to the new rail until shadow reconciliation passes and Harsha approves the data-plane change. 7. The legacy `extraCostUsage` and independent counter paths are retired rather than maintained as fallbacks.

Full details: Sensitive Data Protection And Privacy **Explanation** The new per-organization resolver can route customer data to the wrong organization’s model vendor after a membership change. `resolveModelForUser` caches `userId -> orgId` for 15 seconds (modelRoles.ts:97-114), and the PR adds no invalidation when `joinOrg` or `clearOrgMembership` changes `orgId` (db.ts:1802-1822, 2384-2401). The migrated enrichment path sends lead email, name, company, location, and source context to the resolved model (enrichmentV3RealDeps.ts:716-724, 755-774). Role options include external OpenRouter providers such as DeepSeek, Qwen, and Anthropic (modelRoles.ts:20-24; llmModelRegistry.ts:258, 295, 300). Therefore, after a user moves from organization A to B, B data can use A’s vendor override for the cache window. This is a tenant privacy and unintended-vendor exposure. It is not a production outage path. **Resolution** Do not use a stale organization membership for privacy-sensitive model routing. Resolve the user’s current org for each model-selection request, or add reliable membership-version invalidation to every join, removal, role-change, and organization-transfer path. Add a regression test that changes a user from org A to org B and verifies that the next workload immediately uses B’s model policy. Also document and enforce the approved external-provider policy for PII-bearing roles before allowing those providers for enrichment and other customer-data workloads.
Full details: Performance And Algorithmic Complexity **Explanation** The new PUT endpoint accepts an arbitrarily large `modelRoles` object and processes it synchronously with `Object.entries(map)` on the request path. The only applicable parser limit is the global `express.json({ limit: "50mb" })`, while this schema has only eight valid role keys. An authorized caller can therefore send a near-50 MB JSON object and force large parsing, allocation, enumeration, and validation work. This is a request-path resource-exhaustion risk, although the evidence does not show a current production outage. **Resolution** Apply a small route-specific JSON body limit before the global parser, such as 8–16 KB, and reject maps with more than `MODEL_ROLES.length` own keys before validation. Also cap model string lengths or validate against the finite model registry without retaining arbitrary input. If resolver calls can run concurrently, consider caching in-flight organization and membership lookups to avoid cold-cache request bursts.

## Why The two-week regression Ed (xCures) reported on 08-17 was invisible to our own quality signal: * The "2 pages → 20 pages" session (`51674765`, 08-14) scored **4 with 5/5/5 dimensions**. * The Phoenix kickoff session where Vince said "I didn't ask for a lecture… asking for permission to run a test" (`822c1ed4`, 08-14, 48K completion tokens) scored **5**. * "argued/pushed back" judge reasons went 3 → 16 across windows and **14 of the 16 scored 5** — the rubric rewards pushback as "excellent reasoning". * Aggregate satisfaction stayed flat (4.83 → 4.85) while interactive ≤3 share went 5.2% → 7.7% and completion tokens per run doubled on 32 fixed-prompt schedules (median 1.97×) after the Opus 5 default switch on 07-31. * The Daily Satisfaction Score Report (08-01) did flag Ed's session as P1 but attributed it to `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` (the picker) when all 33 turns ran on Opus 5, and prescribed the wrong fix (see ENG-1313). The judge scores goalCompletion / outputQuality / dataAccuracy only. It has no notion of concision, instruction compliance, or unnecessary permission requests, so [ENG-1246](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1246/investigate-agent-mode-degradedrunrate-regression-from-post-merge)'s degradedRunRate and the daily reports cannot catch this class. [ENG-1223](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1223/p0-judge-rubric-fangfang-judge-scored-fabricated-tool-output-45-with) (judge scored fabricated output 4/5) is the fabrication cousin of the same blind spot. ## Acceptance criteria (must pass before PR opens) ### Behavioral contract (HUMAN-WRITTEN — drafted by Fable on 2026-08-17 for Harsha to confirm; agent MUST NOT modify) 1. **New judge dimensions.** Every scored session gets `concision` (0–5: did reply length match the question/instruction) and `instructionCompliance` (0–5: explicit user instructions — length, yes/no, "don't guess", "do X" — followed on the first attempt) and a boolean `unnecessaryPermissionRequest` (asked to confirm a read-only/draft/test action). How to verify: `51674765` scores concision ≤2 and instructionCompliance ≤2; `822c1ed4` sets unnecessaryPermissionRequest=true; `68c9a8fb` [15]/[25] score concision ≤2; a control session with terse correct answers scores ≥4 on both. 2. **Pushback is not rewarded by default.** A turn that counters an explicit non-spend/non-publish instruction instead of complying cannot score 5 on outputQuality. How to verify: `9481f94e` [52] "Stop the July campaign Now" → outputQuality ≤3 for that turn's session. 3. **Deterministic replay fixtures with hard thresholds** (chars/tokens, not judge score): the four Ed sessions + Phoenix `822c1ed4` + mvarma `eecb6d31` are checked into the eval set (Okareo or characterization) with the thresholds from [ENG-1309](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1309/response-directness-length-contract-yesno-answered-first-explicit)/1310/1311; a regression above threshold fails CI for agentMode PRs. 4. **Reports use the new dimensions.** The Daily Satisfaction Score Report and `/api/admin/loops/reliability-trend` surface concision/instructionCompliance/unnecessaryPermissionRequest so a fleet-wide 2× verbosity is visible within a day, not two weeks. ### Implementation tests (AGENT-WRITTEN against the contract above) * Unit tests on the judge prompt/parser for the new fields; fixture replays with thresholds; report snapshot tests; ≥95% coverage; `npx tsc` clean. ## Notes * Fixture sessions and numbers: [ENG-1305](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1305/investigate-emma-asserts-guessed-facts-despite-explicit-dont-guess) (audit), [ENG-1306](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1306/investigate-emma-ignores-explicit-lengthconciseness-instructions-20) (verbosity), [ENG-1307](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1307/investigate-emma-argues-with-direct-user-instructions-instead-of) (arguing). Second customer: Phoenix 08-14, Fathom 783353558. * MOCKABLE (judge + fixtures, no live third party); no data-plane change.

ENG-2159 Approval-inbox decisions must always show which account/customer they're about

## What happened Directly caused today's ENG-2158 incident. Manan rejected a real TriCityAI campaign-activation decision in Slack because the card didn't clearly show which account/customer it was about — his words: "had I seen the account, I would not have done it." That decision happened to mention "TriCityAI/Smart Trade Team" in its `businessImpact` prose, but that's incidental, not guaranteed — a different decision could easily omit it. ## Root cause (confirmed via code read) `ApprovalDecision` has `customerId`/`customerName` fields, but `validateCreateRequest` (`src/services/approvalInboxService.ts` \~line 233) explicitly **rejects** a `customerId` on any team-audience decision (`plan_choice`/`meta_write` — the kind routed to Harsha/Matt/Fangfang). So decisions in the approver's own Slack queue structurally cannot carry a customer/account field at all — whatever account info shows up is whatever the model happened to write into free-form `businessImpact`/`evidencePacket.researchSummary`. Separately, `decisionItemBlocks` (`src/services/approvalInboxSlack.ts` \~line 62) never reads `customerId`/`customerName` even when they ARE set (customer-audience decisions) — it only renders `businessImpact` + `evidencePacket.researchSummary` + links. So even the customer-audience path has no dedicated, always-rendered "who/what this is about" line today. ## Proposed fix Add a new required field, e.g. `subjectLabel: string` — short human string identifying the account/customer this decision concerns (e.g. `"TriCityAI · Meta Ad Account 2041725529929988"`), allowed regardless of audience (unlike `customerId`, which stays customer-audience-only by design). Required at creation: * `validateCreateRequest` — reject any decision missing a non-empty `subjectLabel`. * `stage_pending_decision`'s input schema (`emma/tools.ts`) — make it a required parameter so Emma can't omit it, not just encourage it via description text. * `decisionItemBlocks` — render it as its own bolded, prominent line above `businessImpact`, not folded into prose. * Check `approvalInboxCustomerNotify.ts`'s email template for the same gap on the customer-audience path — likely needs the same treatment for parity. ## Scope note This is real engineering work (schema + tool input + render + tests + live verification), not a data-plane fix — normal PR process, not a Yugo infra ask.

ENG-2159 Approval-inbox decisions must always show which account/customer they're about

## What happened Directly caused today's ENG-2158 incident. Manan rejected a real TriCityAI campaign-activation decision in Slack because the card didn't clearly show which account/customer it was about — his words: "had I seen the account, I would not have done it." That decision happened to mention "TriCityAI/Smart Trade Team" in its `businessImpact` prose, but that's incidental, not guaranteed — a different decision could easily omit it. ## Root cause (confirmed via code read) `ApprovalDecision` has `customerId`/`customerName` fields, but `validateCreateRequest` (`src/services/approvalInboxService.ts` \~line 233) explicitly **rejects** a `customerId` on any team-audience decision (`plan_choice`/`meta_write` — the kind routed to Harsha/Matt/Fangfang). So decisions in the approver's own Slack queue structurally cannot carry a customer/account field at all — whatever account info shows up is whatever the model happened to write into free-form `businessImpact`/`evidencePacket.researchSummary`. Separately, `decisionItemBlocks` (`src/services/approvalInboxSlack.ts` \~line 62) never reads `customerId`/`customerName` even when they ARE set (customer-audience decisions) — it only renders `businessImpact` + `evidencePacket.researchSummary` + links. So even the customer-audience path has no dedicated, always-rendered "who/what this is about" line today. ## Proposed fix Add a new required field, e.g. `subjectLabel: string` — short human string identifying the account/customer this decision concerns (e.g. `"TriCityAI · Meta Ad Account 2041725529929988"`), allowed regardless of audience (unlike `customerId`, which stays customer-audience-only by design). Required at creation: * `validateCreateRequest` — reject any decision missing a non-empty `subjectLabel`. * `stage_pending_decision`'s input schema (`emma/tools.ts`) — make it a required parameter so Emma can't omit it, not just encourage it via description text. * `decisionItemBlocks` — render it as its own bolded, prominent line above `businessImpact`, not folded into prose. * Check `approvalInboxCustomerNotify.ts`'s email template for the same gap on the customer-audience path — likely needs the same treatment for parity. ## Scope note This is real engineering work (schema + tool input + render + tests + live verification), not a data-plane fix — normal PR process, not a Yugo infra ask.

ENG-2169 Meta creative swap keeps the old image_hash when only a new image_url is given — ad keeps serving the old image

## Found While building ENG-2141 (creative lineage, PR #3092). Verified on origin/main. In the agent-mode Meta creative-swap path (`backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`, the block that builds `newCreativeParams` before `SWAP_NOT_REFLECTED` handling), the link-ad and video branches build: ```ts image_hash: params.image_hash || ld.image_hash, // video: || vd.image_hash image_url: params.image_url || ld.picture || ld.image_url, ``` When the caller passes only a new `image_url` (the normal case for a freshly generated image), the **old creative's** `image_hash` **is carried over**. Meta's creative builder prefers `image_hash` over `image_url`, so the new creative is built with the **old image**. The swap "succeeds", and the ad keeps serving the image it was meant to replace. ## Expected A new `image_url` without an `image_hash` must not inherit the old hash: drop it, or upload the new URL and use its hash. The existing read-back should then confirm that the new image is live. ## Plan 1. When `params.image_url` is set and `params.image_hash` is not, omit the old `image_hash` (or resolve a fresh hash via `uploadMetaAdsImage`). 2. Extend the swap read-back to compare the creative's actual `image_hash`/URL with the requested one, and fail loudly (`SWAP_NOT_REFLECTED`) when it still shows the old image. 3. Tests: new URL only → no old hash; new hash → used; neither → carried over (unchanged behaviour); read-back mismatch → loud error. Related: ENG-2141 (lineage follows Meta's hash-first rule so it does not credit the wrong image), ENG-592 (success-but-no-op class), ENG-2128.

ENG-1960 create_html_from_template: deterministic backstop for HTML/Markdown leaking into variable values

PR #2910 fixed the HTML-markup-in-customer-report bug (found live-testing ENG-1880 Piece 3) by adding a plain-text instruction to `create_html_from_template`'s tool description. That's prompt-only enforcement — if a tool-calling model ever ignores the instruction, the same class of bug (literal `<ul><li>` text in a report) can resurface silently. Not a security issue (ENG-1877's escaping is the real safety net regardless, and is unaffected either way) — worst case is cosmetic. Deliberately not built as part of #2910: for ENG-1880 specifically, Phase B runs as a scheduled chat monitored directly by Harsha (per the 2026-09-14 call decision) before any customer ever sees a report, which already catches this class of failure during the trust-building window. And building a good deterministic backstop isn't trivial — naively stripping `<`/`>`/`*` from variable values risks corrupting legitimate literal data (a real customer name containing an asterisk, etc.), so it needs its own careful design, not a bolt-on. Scope for whoever picks this up: decide between (a) a deterministic strip/neutralize pass on variable string values right before substitution, scoped narrowly enough to avoid touching legitimate data, or (b) a detection-and-log pass that makes a recurrence visible without altering the data, so at minimum silent regressions get caught. Should reuse or sit alongside the existing `deepEscapeHtmlValues`/`collectRawToEscapedMap` machinery in `agentModeService.ts` (ENG-1877) rather than duplicate it. Related: #2910, ENG-1877, ENG-1880.

The replay parser accepts any positive `--sample` value, so this is not bounded to the default 150 sessions. The replay also reads all paginated sessions into memory (`evalOutcomeJudge.ts:271-274`), sorts the full frame in `sampleUniform`, and has no maximum window or item limit. For each labelled session, `loadSessionItems` already queries messages (`agentGraderLoader.ts:384-391`), then the replay loop queries the same messages again and performs another session query for gate fields (`evalOutcomeJudge.ts:292-300`). That creates redundant per-session query fan-out and processes it sequentially. These defects affect the operator replay/evaluation path rather than proving an immediate production outage. **Resolution** Replace `rocAuc` with an O(n log n) rank/sort or sorted cumulative-count implementation that handles ties. Bound bootstrap iterations and reject or cap replay sample sizes. Bound the date window and total frame size, or use a bounded streaming/reservoir sampler instead of retaining and sorting the complete session frame. Change the loader/replay contract so the initial load carries the required gate attributes and raw messages forward; do not query the same session and message partitions again. ## Outcome Implement one org-level accounting architecture in which every **AgentWeb-paid, user-attributable** upstream call is recorded exactly once, priced honestly, visible in a spend history, and applied to the same monthly usage limit. It replaces the current split between `tokenUsage.totalCost`, the daily `AW-UsageRecords` aggregates, the effectively dead `extraCostUsage` rail, vendor-specific counters, and unmetered vendor calls. ## Billing boundary Debit the user's/org's monthly usage balance when: * AgentWeb pays an upstream and the action is attributable to a billing subject. * The cost is measured by the vendor, or a versioned allocated rate exists. Do not debit when: * The customer pays through their own connected account (for example Meta ad spend or customer-owned SaaS/API usage). * The cost is shared platform overhead without a reviewed allocation policy. * The unit has no price. Unpriced paid egress must fail closed or be explicitly allowlisted as platform-funded; it must never become a silent $0 charge. ## Architecture ### 1. Immutable spend events are the source of truth Create an append-only, per-call usage event store ([ENG-702](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-702/make-vendor-usage-writes-idempotent-and-fail-loud-gate-before-any) data-plane gate) rather than treating a mutable monthly counter or daily aggregate as authoritative. Required event fields: * `eventId` / idempotency key * `occurredAt`, billing month * `billingUserId`, `orgId`, `actingUserId`, optional `onBehalfOf` * provider, operation, feature, unit, quantity * `costMicroUsd` * cost source: `measured | allocated` * rate-card version when allocated * session/task/run/request references * lifecycle: `reserved | settled | voided` * external vendor reference when available Retries with the same idempotency key must return the original event and add $0. ### 2. One charging API All paid egress goes through one service; callers may not write the ledger or monthly counter directly. Conceptual contract: 1. Resolve the org billing subject. 2. Classify the call as AgentWeb-paid, customer-paid, or platform overhead. 3. Resolve a measured cost or versioned allocated rate. 4. Reserve known/estimated spend when practical. 5. Check admission against settled spend + outstanding reservations. 6. Execute the vendor call. 7. Settle actual spend or void the reservation. 8. Atomically persist the idempotent event and update the billing-subject/month aggregate. LLM, image/video, v0, X, search, enrichment, voice, rendering, and future vendor adapters must use the same service. ### 3. Monthly state is a projection, not an independent counter Maintain an atomic `billingUserId + month` projection for fast admission: * settled chargeable spend * active reservations * included monthly allowance * purchased credits * admin grants/reversals * migration adjustment * remaining usable balance * current policy mode Invariant: summing immutable settled events must reproduce the monthly spend projection within one micro-dollar. Raw spend is always preserved. Credits and migration adjustments change available allowance; they never erase or rewrite spend. ### 4. Admission semantics * A new job is admitted only when remaining balance covers its reservation or the policy explicitly permits an overrun. * Work admitted before the boundary may finish under the existing admitted-work rule. * Fixed-price calls reserve the exact allocated rate. * Variable-cost calls reserve a documented maximum/estimate and settle the actual amount. * Concurrent requests use conditional/transactional writes so two calls cannot both spend the same remaining balance. * `full_choice | optimized | paused` is derived from this one monthly projection; token volume remains an analytical dimension, not a second competing gate. ### 5. Versioned vendor rate registry One reviewed registry defines provider, operation, unit, rate, currency, effective dates, and source. ENG-2055 Any user can schedule another user's task — createSchedule never checks taskId ownership

`createSchedule` (`backend/src/controllers/schedules.ts:8`) takes `taskId` **straight from the request body** and stores it with the caller's `userId`. It never loads the task or checks who owns it: ``` const { taskId, frequency } = req.body; const userId = req.user?.userId; if (!taskId || !frequency || !userId) return res.status(400)… // …schedule is created with that taskId, no ownership check ``` The route is authenticated (`routes/schedules.ts:23`), so this is not anonymous — but any authenticated user may name **any** task id. Task ids are UUIDs, which is an obstacle, not a control. **Impact:** a schedule can be created against a task belonging to another tenant, causing that task to execute on a timetable the owner did not set and cannot see from their own schedule list. Given the agent engine polls `AW-TaskSchedules` and runs what it finds, this is a cross-tenant write with side effects, not just a stray row. **Fix.** Load the task and confirm `task.userId === req.user.userId` before creating the schedule; return 404 (not 403) so the endpoint does not confirm which task ids exist. The same check is worth auditing on `updateSchedule` and `deleteSchedule`, which were not examined here. Found while building aw-agent; verified against `main` on 2026-09-19 by reading the controller. Not exploited — no schedule was created.

ENG-2170 Deploy pipeline silently drops a merge's deploy when a newer merge supersedes its pending run

## Observed (2026-09-25) The partner portal stayed on `partner-20260925-pr3070` while the backend advanced to `backend-20260925-pr3081`. The portal changes from PR #3079 (merged 18:22Z) and #3091 were never deployed by their own runs: | Deploy run head | Result | Partner portal job | | -- | -- | -- | | 80897dd5a (#3079, portal change) | **cancelled** | — | | c37519e38 (#3081, backend only) | success | **skipped** | | e8c787fbd, 083a36e32, … | success | skipped | ## Cause `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`: * `concurrency: { group: deploy-production, cancel-in-progress: false }`. GitHub still keeps only **one pending run per group**, so a newer merge cancels an older *pending* run. * `dorny/paths-filter` on `push` has **no** `base`, so it compares only against that push's previous commit. So when a merge that touches `partner-portal/**` (or `backend/**`) is superseded while pending by a merge that doesn't touch that component, **that component's change is never deployed**. It waits until some later merge happens to touch the same component. Nothing reports this, and main and prod silently diverge. ## Fix options 1. Set the paths-filter `base` to the **last successfully deployed SHA** per component (read from the EB version label or a deploy-state marker), so every run deploys everything changed since the last good deploy. 2. Or, cheaper: compare against the SHA of the last *successful* deploy run (GitHub API) instead of `github.event.before`. 3. Add a guard/alert: after a deploy, if main has commits touching a component that the running version doesn't contain, flag it. ## Workaround now Any later merge touching `partner-portal/**` deploys the portal from current main, which includes the skipped changes. A manual `workflow_dispatch` of `deploy.yml` is the documented fallback. Found while verifying ENG-2135 / ENG-2144 (ENG-2128).

## Added: HubSpot revoked refresh token reported as Connected (`110b51878`)

Second, independent change now in this PR. Unrelated to the sequence work — no shared files — but grouped here deliberately rather than split again.

### The bug

`GET /api/oauth/connected-accounts` decides status by whether a `refresh_token` exists:

```ts
// Accounts with a refresh token (e.g. Gmail) auto-renew — don't show the
// short-lived access token expiry; just show them as permanently connected.
const hasRefreshToken = !!(acc.config as any).refresh_token;
status = hasRefreshToken ? 'active' : getTokenStatus(acc.config.token_expires_at);
```

Correct for auto-renewing integrations. What was missing: any path that learns the refresh token **stopped working**. `doRefresh` let the rejection propagate without recording it, so the row reported `active` / `"Connected"` indefinitely.

Production portal `245815183` (`argusoft.com`):

| | |
|---|---|
| access token issued | 2026-06-23 14:04:54Z |
| expiry | 2026-06-23 14:34:54Z (30 min) |
| last successful pull | **2026-06-16** |
| Settings page said | **Active · Connected** |
| every CRM sync | **401** |
| duration | **97 days** |

Same failure the Meta Ads branch of this handler already documents one `else if` above — *"Reporting it as 'Connected' is what let a multi-day zero-data reporting outage go unnoticed (ENG-1158)"*. HubSpot was the last integration with no revoked-credential detection: Fathom live-checks, X uses `needs_reconnect`, Meta checks capability.

### Change

| file | |
|---|---|
| `hubspotService.ts` | classify refresh failures; persist `needs_reconnect` on definitive rejection only |
| `hubspotService.create()` | fast-fail a known-dead grant |
| `connectedAccounts.ts` | flagged HubSpot → `disconnected`, mirroring the `twitter` branch |
| `hubspotAuth.ts` | clear the flag on reconnect, mirroring `outlookAuth` |

**Deliberate asymmetry:** only 400 (`BAD_REFRESH_TOKEN`) and 401 flag. 5xx / timeouts / network rethrow untouched — wrongly persisting "dead" hard-fails a live integration and tells a paying customer they're broken, the asymmetry `linkedInOutreachService` documents for its 403 case. 4 of 14 tests exist only to pin that direction.

**Review** (independent subagent, full diff read): found 2 critical/high real defects, 2 medium, 1 low. Verified each against the actual code before fixing:

1. **Critical** — `executeApprovalInboxMetaWriteManifest` recorded every write's outcome but never resumed the origin session. The turn message promised "I'll resume automatically" and nothing did — the exact ENG-1635/1644 defect, for the flagship meta_write case. **Fixed**: it now calls a shared `resumeOriginSession` primitive (extracted from `approvalInboxExecution.ts`, previously private/decision-scoped) with the packet's real read-back outcome.
2. **Critical/High** — no per-step claim in the new workflow-step builder; two concurrent `approve-all` calls could both reach `dispatchAuthorizedMetaWrite` for the same write before either checkpoint landed. **Fixed**: new atomic `approvalInboxService.claimDispatch(decisionId)` gate; a concurrent loser gets `StepContendedError`, not a second real Meta write.
3. **Medium** — a partial `stageApprovalInboxMetaWriteManifest` failure fell back to the live-deck path for the *whole* batch, including writes already durably staged, risking double-dispatch via a second, uncoordinated claim mechanism (`claimMetaWriteManifestGrant`). **Fixed**: `Promise.allSettled`, never falls back once anything is durably staged.
4. **Medium** — a retried staging call could report a manifestId that doesn't match where the decisions actually landed (`createDecision`'s idempotent-hit branch returns the *original* manifestId, not the freshly-minted one). **Fixed**: reads back real `createDecision` results and reports honestly.
5. **Low** (found independently, live, before the review landed) — pre-existing decisions from before this migration have no `manifestId` and were showing up in the queue as a dead-end entry. **Fixed**: excluded from the grouped queue; still fully reachable via the unchanged Slack flow.

No new DB reads or writes, no new external calls, and no new timeouts or size limits are needed. Retry count drops for terminal blocked plans, which reduces work. Not a finding: the regex scans note text, and notes have no length cap. That is existing stored data, and the PR does not add a new path for it. **Safety answer before merge (head `488ae70b7`).** Safe to ship. This PR adds a capability, so the question is misuse as well as regression; both are covered below, with what I could not close.

- **Nobody gets the capability by default.** The tool needs an `aw_` key that holds the opt-in `gtm:email` scope. Proved at the HTTP layer against the real registry (and again by a reviewer end to end over real HTTP): a default key, a legacy key with no scopes, a `tools:read` key, an OAuth client, an anonymous caller, a batch that hides the call, and a session reused by another key are all refused; `tools:execute` does not imply it; the scope cannot be granted from a delegated (admin-as-customer) session, is not a default, and is not offered by the portal's key form. Emma's own tool of the same name lives in a separate registry and is untouched.
- **Whose people.** The tool calls the portal routes through `mcpFetch`, and both routes check that the plan belongs to the caller. A key can email only the people on its own user's plans (two-tenant test on the real routes, both directions: 403, nothing sent). The agent cannot choose the cap, the path or any other argument: unknown arguments are refused by name and ids must match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` (all 110 plans and 365 phases on production do).
- **How much.** At most 10 people per call (refused before anything is sent), at most 50 emails an hour per account across all of its keys (a reviewer fired 200 parallel calls from one account and exactly 50 reached the route), the same report not twice within 10 minutes, and nobody is emailed unless explicitly chosen.
